# Creative Industries AI Concerns

Artists across different mediums hold the same concerns about AI but do not know it, and that is why organizing across disciplines rather than within one is the source of leverage — the argument Fight for the Future Campaigns and Communications director Lia Holland made to TechCrunch on 2023-10-06. The warrant is stated plainly: "when artists of different mediums move together they have a lot more power."

The grounds are the mutual invisibility Holland reports between fields. "It's funny because if you've talked to musicians who have these concerns, they say, 'Well, authors have been very quiet.' If you talk to others about these concerns, they say, 'Well, musicians and photographers don't seem to care at all,'" she said. "So part of it also is that the different creative fields, when it comes to this sort of work, are a little bit siloed." Hence the design of the day of action: "That was another intent with our launching this effort with the day of action, to try to illustrate how these are common concerns that are shared across artistic mediums. And to create an organizing point."

The argument is deliberately not anti-AI. The campaign targets potential corporate abuse of AI technology, but it's realistic about the ways that musicians and some other creatives could benefit on an individual level from automating parts of their work; the goal is that AI tools "become ways for individual humans to make more money, work less, and compete with the corporations that exploit them." Holland extends this to musicians specifically: "musicians are perhaps more familiar with the idea of AI . . . Musicians in general are more familiar with things like music production software, and AI tools like MIDI drum loops . . . so I think that there is a certain amount of more progressive learning from them, when it comes to technology, and its ability to make their music better."

The complication Holland's framing has to absorb is that the interests within a single industry already conflict. Musicians are nervous about industry giants copyrighting AI music and cutting them out of the process; major record labels are worried about AI models training on their catalogues and stealing a slice of their considerable pie; and Spotify erased thousands of AI-crafted songs from its platform but also recently globally launched an AI-powered DJ that curates music for listeners while talking to them in a synthetic voice.



---


# Genre Labels Should Not Define Music

Michelle Jubelirer argues that music is music and genres should not be defined by colour, and that the business needs to change its definition of "pop" music. Her ground is that there seems to be real confusion in the current usage, and her proposed replacement rule is that any music that streams in volume should be called pop music.

The operating philosophy that follows is that great ideas transcend genre: CMG has experts in every "genre" but they all share, collaborate and respectfully challenge each other. Jubelirer goes further than rejecting particular genre boundaries, saying she does not even like the word "genre" and that it should be changed.



---


# Abdullah on Product Over Profit in the Music Industry

Asked what one thing he would change about the music industry, AfroFuture co-founder Abdul Karim Abdullah said he would have it focus on the product rather than the profit. His ground for that claim is an effect he attributes to the current emphasis: "Profit as a metric has lowered the caliber of the content we consume." The warrant joining the two is his judgement that this has "diluted the purity of music" — that is, using profit as the governing metric changes what gets made, not merely how it is sold.

Asked separately what advice he would give an aspiring entrepreneur in the music industry, Abdullah said: "remain true to your purpose and to always be authentic. With discipline and a solid foundation around you, you can reach your desired level of success – even when you meet adversity or when doors continue to close – you must never give up."



---


# Google's Copyright Filing Against YouTube's Music Reassurances

MBW's counter to the idea that YouTube's rightsholder assurances settle the matter is that Google's take on copyright "harvesting" by generative AI models sits in odd contrast to the copyright-related reassurances YouTube was careful to make to the music industry during the pre-development, development, and trial launch of "Dream Track."

The premise attacked is that the platform relationship and the parent company's legal position can be read separately. MBW's sources close to Sony Music were keen to point out that the company's general ongoing relationship with YouTube and YouTube Music is a harmonious one — YouTube is now the second largest commercial partner of the major record companies, with a stated ambition to catch up with Spotify in the years ahead, and says it paid out over USD $6 billion to music rightsholders in the year to end of June 2022, with around $2 billion of that coming just from ads on user-generated content. However, the October US Copyright Office filing from Google has definitely put the cat amongst the pigeons at Sony Music HQ, as MBW is sure it has at the other two major record companies, because of its position that "Any prohibition or limitation on the use of copyrighted materials for purposes of AI training would undermine the purpose of copyright and foreclose the many opportunities that come with this technology." As well as part-explaining Sony Music's refusal to be included in Dream Track thus far, Google's USCO filing also perhaps explains the careful words selected by Robert Kyncl and especially Sir Lucian Grainge in their respective comments endorsing YouTube's AI experiment — Grainge's statement, after all, began: "We have a fundamental responsibility to our artists to ensure the digital ecosystem evolves to protect them and their work against unauthorized exploitation, including by generative AI platforms…"



---


# Sony Music's Generative AI Principles For Congress

Dennis Kooker, Sony Music Entertainment's President of Global Digital Business & US Sales, asked Congress at the November 29, 2023 AI Insight Forum to embrace a set of five principles around generative AI, on the argument that "if copyrights are protected and enforced appropriately, we are at the beginning of a multi-decade marathon that will change the creative and commercial landscape for music."

The framing condition Kooker set is that "Music is a tremendous driver for AI technology, and AI technology presents a tremendous opportunity for the creative development of music. But these opportunities must be grounded by the human creators' vision with the machine assisting, not with the machine replacing the human creator." The principles are: Assure Consent, Compensation, and Credit — "New products and businesses built with music must be developed with the consent of the owner and appropriate compensation and credit. It is essential to understand why the training of AI models is being done, what products will be developed as a result, and what the business model is that will monetize the use of the artist's work. Congress and the agencies should assure that creators' rights are recognized and respected." Confirm That Copying Music to Train AI Models is Not Fair Use — "Even worse are those that argue that copyrighted content should automatically be considered fair use so that protected works are never compensated for usage and creators have no say in the products or business models that are developed around them and their work. Congress should assure and agencies should presume that reproducing music to train AI models, in itself, is not a fair use." Prevent the Cloning of Artists' Voices and Likenesses Without Express Permission — "We cannot allow an artist's voice or likeness to be cloned for use without the express permission of the artist. This is a very personal decision for the artist. Congress should pass into law effective federal protections for name, image, and likeness." Incentivize Accurate Recordkeeping — "Correct attribution will be a critical element to artists being paid fairly and correctly for new works that are created. In addition, rights can only be enforced around the training of AI when there are accurate records about what is being copied. Otherwise, the inability to enforce rights in the AI marketplace equates to a lack of rights at all, producing a dangerous imbalance that prevents a thriving ecosystem. This requires strong and accurate record keeping by the generative AI platforms, a requirement that urgently needs legislative support to ensure incentives are in place so that it happens consistently and correctly." And Assure Transparency for Consumers and Artists — "Transparency is necessary to clearly distinguish human-created works from AI-created works. The public should know, when they are listening to music, whether that music was created by a human being or a machine." MBW summarised the intended effect: "The principles will ensure that intellectual property businesses can succeed in this new world alongside tech partners, further advancing investment and expanding economic opportunities."



---


# Negative Sentiment as Profitable Streaming Discourse

"Negative sentiment is very profitable," the anonymous AAA game developer told Polygon for its 2023-10-19 piece, noting that social media platforms are built to highlight popular — and sometimes caustic — content.

The relation this sets up is an inherent tension between game developers and hardcore players like Twitch streamers, who are not the main audience of most games but are often some of the most visible players.

The loop closes because Twitch is both cause and measure: the misinformation will vary, but Twitch shapes that discourse while also becoming the very metric people use to make sense of a game's situation. It has gotten so bad, Polygon writes, that people scrutinize Twitch longevity for single-player games, not just live-service or multiplayer ones.

"There is inherently [a] vicious and negative cycle for everyone involved, for how live service interacts with Twitch as a medium," says the developer, who also spent years as a serious Twitch streamer and says he is still recovering from the burnout of livestreaming all the time.



---


# X Found To Have The Worst Disinformation Ratio In EU Analysis

X, formerly Twitter, was called out in the European Union for having the worst ratio of disinformation and misinformation to posts not spreading falsehoods among mainstream social networks.

The finding came in a September 2023 speech by EU commissioner for values and transparency Vera Jourova, discussing the latest updates from platforms signed up to combat disinformation under a beefed-up EU Code of Practice linked to compliance with the bloc's legally binding Digital Services Act. X's poor performance was assessed during a pilot phase of testing of a new methodology developed by Code signatories. "A big novelty under the Code is now the publication of the first set of structural indicators such as how easy it is to find disinformation content, how much engagement such content receives or indicators about sources. These indicators — developed by the signatories — constitute an unprecedented and novel insight into disinformation on online platforms," she said. "Such insight is crucial to understand how effective platforms efforts are to fight this threat even more efficiently. This is a very valuable industry proposal that has great potential while it has to be still further developed. Here, signatories have decided to run a pilot phase in three Member States to evaluate the methodology on two of those indicators. X, former Twitter, who is not under the Code any more is the platform with the largest ratio of mis/disinformation posts."

X was contacted for a response to the EU's analysis of the ratio of disinformation it is spreading, and replied with an automated email reading: "Busy now, please check back later." The finding fits a wider pattern: consistent moderation, fact-checking investment and researcher data access are areas where X under new owner Elon Musk has moved out of step with EU expectations on countering disinformation, suggesting that X — designated by the EU as a VLOP under the DSA back in April — continues to put itself squarely in the Commission's crosshairs, including over its priority issue of tackling Kremlin propaganda.

qid: Does the Sporting News article rank Tyreek Hill as the top wide receiver for Week 14, while The Guardian article focuses on his performance in a specific game, and does the other Sporting News article question his ability to achieve 2,000-plus receiving yards for the season based on the strength of the Miami Dolphins' remaining opponents' pass defenses?
context:
# Tyreek Hill Dolphins Midseason MVP

Yardbarker's Nov. 9, 2023 AFC midseason team MVP list named wide receiver Tyreek Hill the Miami Dolphins' MVP, calling him arguably the best wide receiver in the NFL and saying he had somehow reached a new level of dominance in his age-29 season.

The grounds are league-leading production: the seven-time Pro Bowler led the NFL in receiving yards with 1,076 and in touchdown catches with eight, and he was on pace to break Calvin Johnson's season record for receiving yards of 1,964. The forward-looking claim carries a condition — as long as the Dolphins maintained their success on offense down the stretch, Hill should earn Offensive Player of the Year honors.



---


# NFL Week 11 2023: Tyreek Hill Returns From A Hand Injury, Darius Slayton Does Not

CBS Sports' Week 11 injury roundup of 2023-11-19 records two wide receivers going down with contrasting outcomes. Tyreek Hill of the Dolphins briefly left Miami's game against the Raiders while nursing a hand injury and was ruled questionable to return, but he took the field again soon afterward, securing seven catches for 80 yards and a score before halftime. The roundup notes the pattern that Hill has left multiple games that year, only to return in all of them.

Darius Slayton of the Giants had a big impact against the Commanders, hauling in a deep score from Tommy DeVito, before exiting with an arm injury. He was ruled out for the remainder of the contest halfway through the third quarter.



---


# Drake London Home Road Fantasy Split

CBSSports.com's Dec. 19, 2023 Week 16 wide receiver preview reported that Drake London was averaging 15.88 PPR fantasy points per game at home that season and just 7.37 on the road.

The adjacent note in the same list recorded that after missing the previous week's game, Tyreek Hill needed to average almost 153 yards per game in his final three to reach his stated goal of 2,000 receiving yards that season.



---


# 2023 NFL Offensive Player Of The Year: Hill The Favorite, Lamb The Longshot

Tyreek Hill was the current favorite for 2023 NFL Offensive Player of the Year and CeeDee Lamb the longshot, and Sporting News argued on Dec. 5, 2023 that Lamb could steal the award if Hill faded down the stretch.

There was a good reason why Hill was such a heavy favorite: the Dolphins wide receiver was on track to become the first player with 2,000-plus receiving yards in a single season. But Sporting News saw a solid chance he would not hit that mark, because of Miami's five remaining opponents, four had pass defenses ranked in the league's top eight. If he slowed down, someone like Lamb could catch up.

The Lamb case rests on his trajectory. Based on his current season average, Lamb was on track for close to 1,600 yards, but based on his production over the last seven games he could finish with closer to 1,800. He would probably need Hill to fade down the stretch to have a shot — but if Hill did and Lamb continued to produce, Lamb could steal OPOY from Hill.



---


# CeeDee Lamb Week 16 Top DFS Play

CBSSports.com's Dec. 19, 2023 Week 16 wide receiver preview named CeeDee Lamb, WR, Dallas, No. 88, its top DFS play, with projections powered by SportsLine.

The choice between Lamb and Tyreek Hill would not be an easy one; the tiebreaker for the writer was that Lamb was $900 cheaper and Hill might still not be 100% by the time the Cowboys and Dolphins kicked off. Lamb's form supports the pick: the previous week was the first time since Week 9 that he failed to reach the end zone, and the second time since Week 5 that he did not score at least 17 PPR fantasy points. His weekly breakdown at age 24, four years' experience: at MIA, MIA -1.5, O/U 51, opponent vs. WR 15th, projected 19.4 points, WR rank 2nd; year-to-date 103 receptions, 141 targets, 1,306 receiving yards, 10 TD, 21.6 fantasy points per game.



---


# Week 13's Top Fantasy Wide Receivers

Sporting News argued on Nov. 29, 2023 that Tyreek Hill (@ Commanders) belonged in the top spot for Week 13 PPR leagues, on the grounds that he did his thing despite a tough Week 12 matchup and now faced a putrid Washington stop unit. CeeDee Lamb (vs. Seahawks) was not far behind, with Dallas' WR1 aiming to maintain his efficient play against Seattle.

Usage was the warrant for the next tier. Amon-Ra St. Brown (@ Saints) had been a target hog, seeing at least nine looks in each of his past six games, with no reason to expect his workload to decrease in a bounce-back game for the Lions; Keenan Allen (@ Patriots) looked to continue his dominant ways as Justin Herbert's go-to target with routine double-digit target potential. Mike Evans (vs. Panthers) sat in the top five having totalled four touchdowns over the past three weeks. A.J. Brown (vs. 49ers) faced a sound San Francisco coverage unit in Sunday's NFC Championship rematch, but his ability to dominate in the red zone still made him a top-10 PPR play.

Two arguments came with caveats. Ja'Marr Chase (@ Jaguars) averaged over 20 yards per reception in Week 12, and although the drop-off from Joe Burrow to Jake Browning is massive, Chase still had WR1 upside given his usage. Matchup carried the rest: Michael Pittman Jr. (@ Texans) faced a Houston pass defense that had been shredded for weeks, so another 100-yard receiving day could be in store; Jaylen Waddle (@ Commanders) was looking to post a second consecutive 100-plus-yard day against a struggling Commanders coverage unit; and Tank Dell (vs. Broncos) continued to rise, rounding out the top 10 as a trusted option of C.J. Stroud's.



---


# Tyreek Hill's Receiving-Yards Pace, 2023

Six catches for 163 yards and a touchdown against Carolina left the Dolphins' Tyreek Hill with 812 receiving yards through the first six games of 2023, second in NFL history to Hall of Famer Don Hutson, who had 819 through six with Green Bay in 1942, The New York Times reported on 16 October 2023.

The full top ten for receiving yards through six NFL games reads: Don Hutson (1942) 819; Tyreek Hill (2023) 812; Wes Welker (2011) 785; Elroy Hirsch (1951) 766; Santana Moss (2005) 743; DeAndre Hopkins (2015) 726; Raymond Berry (1960) 725; Jerry Rice (1986) 723; Bob Boyd (1954) 718; and Bobby Mitchell (1962) 714.



---


# Tyreek Hill 2,000-Yard Season Pursuit

CBSSports.com's Dec. 19, 2023 Week 16 wide receiver preview reported that after missing the previous week's game, Tyreek Hill needed to average almost 153 yards per game — 152.67 — in his final three games to reach his stated goal of 2,000 receiving yards that season.

The adjacent note in the same list recorded that Puka Nacua needed 18 more catches to set the rookie record for most catches in a season.



---


# Jaylen Waddle Week 16 Contrarian DFS Play

CBSSports.com's Dec. 19, 2023 Week 16 wide receiver preview named Jaylen Waddle, WR, Miami, No. 17, its contrarian DFS play, with projections powered by SportsLine.

The contrarian logic is that the writers expected Tyreek Hill to return that week, which should drive people off Waddle — but there was at least a chance Hill would not be 100% and Waddle would still be Tua Tagovailoa's top target. His recent form fits the format: Waddle had been the quintessential DFS tournament play of late, with three of seven games over 19 PPR fantasy points and topping 26 twice. His weekly breakdown at age 25, three years' experience: vs. DAL, MIA -1.5, O/U 51, opponent vs. WR 7th, projected 14.2 points, WR rank 16th; year-to-date 71 receptions, 99 targets, 964 receiving yards, 4 TD, 14.8 fantasy points per game.



---


# Dolphins +110 vs Chiefs In Germany

Sporting News took the Dolphins at +110 against the Chiefs in the Germany game in Week 9 of 2023, predicting Dolphins 26, Chiefs 24. It conceded the objections up front — Miami had yet to beat a true contender that season and Kansas City were the reigning champions — but countered that the Chiefs had just had their doors blown off by Russell Wilson and the lowly Broncos in a game in which Patrick Mahomes and company suffered five turnovers and three sacks.

Preparation was a central ground. The column expected a statement win from Mike McDaniel's team on neutral ground, noting the Dolphins had been in Frankfurt since early that week, having flown overnight on Monday to give themselves multiple days to acclimate to the time difference and surroundings, while the Chiefs waited until after Thursday's practice to take the 11-hour trip.

Two individual angles complete the case. It was a revenge game for former Chiefs receiver Tyreek Hill, on pace for multiple single-season receiving records and poised for his first Offensive Player of the Year award. And Raheem Mostert, who led the NFL with 10 touchdowns and ranked second behind only Breece Hall in yards per carry (5.4), should be licking his chops against a Kansas City defense that had surrendered 135.6 rushing yards per game over the previous three weeks.

Other Week 9 moneylines the column liked were Vikings (+170) at Falcons, Bengals (-130) vs. Bills and Cowboys (+140) at Eagles.



---


# Week 14 PPR Wide Receivers To Start

Tyreek Hill (vs. Titans) stood as the unquestioned WR1 for Week 14 in Sporting News' PPR rankings of Dec. 7, 2023, after the league's leading receiver torched the Commanders for five catches, 157 yards and two touchdowns.

The framing is that fantasy owners were gearing up for the last week of the fantasy regular season in most leagues, with the rankings loaded top to bottom because just two teams were on bye, and rolling out a strong receiving corps in a potential must-win week was essential.

CeeDee Lamb (vs. Eagles) and the Cowboys looked to avenge their road loss to the Eagles in Week 9, with Dallas' WR1 routinely carrying double-digit reception potential. Amon-Ra St. Brown (@ Bears) was relatively quiet the previous week but was likely to rebound against a Bears defense he totalled nine catches for 95 yards against in Week 11. A.J. Brown (@ Cowboys) reached the century mark for the first time in four games in Week 13, and another high-usage day looked to be in store for a potential shootout. Keenan Allen (vs. Broncos) caught just five of nine targets the previous week, but as Los Angeles' only reliable receiving option a get-right game felt likely. Justin Jefferson (@ Raiders) was set to suit up for the first time since Week 5 and was a must-start whenever active. Stefon Diggs (@ Chiefs) had not totalled 100-plus receiving yards in any of his past six games, but had every chance to get back on track against a Chiefs coverage unit that showed some leaks in Sunday's loss to the Packers.



---

# Rhamondre Stevenson's Fantasy Outlook In Weeks 5 And 6 Of 2023

CBS Sports listed Rhamondre Stevenson under "Sit Him" in both Week 5 and Week 6 of the 2023 season, and hardened the call in the second week: the claim is that Stevenson's workload no longer converts into production, and the warrant is that his before- and after-contact efficiency is at or near the bottom of the league, so neither volume nor a soft matchup is enough on its own.

The Week 5 case, published 4 October 2023 ahead of a home game with New Orleans, concedes that the workload is nice but expects Stevenson once again not to do much with it. The breakdown lists New England favoured by 1, an over/under of 40, an opponent ranked 8th versus running backs, 13.2 projected points, a 26th running back ranking, and year-to-date totals of 164 rushing yards, 12 receptions, 87 receiving yards, one touchdown and 10.8 fantasy points per game. On film the numbers don't match the talent — Stevenson is a capable runner with great vision, balance and power plus good speed — but he struggled on lateral runs and his line failed him plenty on north-south runs, while game script limited him to one fourth-quarter touch. He has at least 16 touches in every game, which is good, but has yet to total 100 yards and has been under 70 yards three times. The Patriots' front five troubles show up in his 0.98 yards before contact per rush, 29th of 44 qualifying backs, and his 1.75 yards after contact per rush, dead last among those 44. He has one explosive carry of 12 or more yards all year — 12 yards, against Miami — against 21 explosive runs and a 10% explosive run rate in 2022, eighth-best. In the passing game he averages 4.0 targets and catches 75% of them but gets just 7.3 yards per catch with one explosive catch of 16-plus yards, a 32-yarder against the Eagles in Week 1, with no reception longer than seven yards since. The Saints are sixth-best in rushing average allowed to backs (3.6) and top-10 in basically every run-defense metric including just nine missed tackles on the year; only Derrick Henry has exceeded 10 fantasy points against them, PPR or not, with 13 PPR points in Week 1, and no one has run for a touchdown on them. Against backs through the air they are roughly league average except in yards after catch per reception (8.53), inflated by a massive Henry catch-and-run in Week 1 — since Week 2 that figure is 5.94, sixth-best in the span, with zero explosive pass plays allowed to backs. Stevenson is still called a decent start ahead of Najee Harris, Khalil Herbert and Jahmyr Gibbs, but the author would rather chance a lineup on upside plays like Jaleel McLaughlin, if Javonte Williams sits out, or Alexander Mattison.

The Week 6 case, published 12 October 2023 ahead of a road game at Las Vegas, refuses to recommend him at all until there is proof of him playing well, since a favourable road matchup alone isn't enough. The breakdown lists the Raiders favoured by 3, an over/under of 41.5, an opponent ranked 20th versus running backs, 12 projected points, a 27th running back ranking, and year-to-date totals of 188 rushing yards, 12 receptions, 87 receiving yards, one touchdown and 9.1 fantasy points per game. Bill Belichick spoke of "starting all over" after the loss to the Saints; the column notes that while some might say dumping Ezekiel Elliott and giving Stevenson more work would make sense, Elliott actually has a higher rushing average and better before- and after-contact rates, so New England may instead turn to another back hoping to find anything that takes pressure off a depleted passing game. Week 5 was the first time Stevenson did not have 16 or more touches: eight carries, no receptions, a season-low 50% snap share, though he handled 10 of 16 third- and fourth-down snaps; he started and played the first two series, Elliott started the next two, they rotated all game, and Elliott remained the back of choice in the two-minute offense at the end of the first half. His efficiency was unchanged — 0.97 yards before contact per rush, 30th of 41 qualifiers, and 1.79 yards after contact, dead last among them — with the same single explosive carry and the same single explosive catch. The Patriots have run one play inside the opponents' five-yard line all season, which explains his lack of touchdowns. # Garrett Wilson's Fantasy Outlook In Weeks 5 And 6 Of 2023

CBS Sports moved Garrett Wilson from "Start Him" in Week 5 of the 2023 season to "Flex Starter" in Week 6, and both calls rest on the same limiting factor: Wilson's situation, specifically the share of Zach Wilson's throws to him that are uncatchable, holds him back from the potential he so clearly has.

The Week 5 case, published 4 October 2023 ahead of a game at Denver, asks whether the matchup is so easy that Zach Wilson will have tons of time in the pocket to make perfect throws, and answers that this is tough to bank on because he has rarely thrown with precision. Even so, the column likes Garrett Wilson's chances of seeing a lot of targets and coming through with at least a couple of big plays against a defense tied in knots for the past eight quarters. Of the 36 targets Garrett Wilson has seen from Zach Wilson, 11 — 31% — have been uncatchable, not counting another three incompletions thrown late or predetermined enough for defenses to sniff out. The silver lining is that Garrett Wilson is clearly the alpha of the passing game, with at least twice as many targets as anyone else on the Jets; the real silver lining is Denver, whose defense has been awful to watch — no defense has allowed a higher catch rate (85.1%) or a worse defensive EPA per dropback (minus-0.79) to wide receivers, and after yielding an 86.7% catch rate and 20.8 yards per catch to Miami in Week 3 they let up a 92.9% catch rate and 15.6 yards per catch to Chicago in Week 4, while even top cornerback Pat Surtain has allowed a high-for-him 63% completion rate and gave up four catches for 56 yards on six targets in his coverage the previous week, with Denver's pass rush practically non-existent. The verdict starts Wilson over Gabe Davis, Jakobi Meyers and any Broncos wideouts.

The Week 6 case, published 12 October 2023 ahead of a home game with Philadelphia, downgrades him: if he couldn't put up a monster game against the Broncos, it's a tough sell that he'll do so against the Eagles, though volume should be in his favour, making close to 16 PPR points — half that in non-PPR — a fair expectation. Zach Wilson was off-target on 15.4% of his throws for the second straight week even with a higher completion rate (73.1%) and 7.7 yards per attempt, a byproduct of attempting just 26 throws after 39 the game before, and the uncatchable share has risen to 14 of 43 targets, or 33%. # Holiday Season Stress And The Question Of Partner Introductions

The holiday season is often perceived as the most wonderful time of year, but survey data says otherwise for a large minority: in a recent poll by the American Psychological Association, cited by The Independent in December 2023, 41 per cent of US adults said their stress levels increased from November to January compared with other months of the year, and nearly 50 per cent of Americans described their stress level during the season as "moderate."

That backdrop is what makes introducing a new partner to your family over the holidays a genuine question rather than an obvious opportunity. People approaching Christmas, Hanukkah or New Year carry different concerns — from family drama at the dinner table to small spats with a mother about decorations — which raises the question of whether you really want to bring a partner into the mix. The Independent's framing is that while it is important to introduce your loved ones to your significant other eventually, relationship experts believe there are discussions to have beforehand, especially during the holidays.



---


# Govee LED Strip Light M1 Matter Deal

Govee's Matter-ready LED Strip Light M1 went on sale for an all-time low of $44.99 at Amazon — $15 off, down from $60, a 25 percent discount — when buyers clipped the on-page coupon, and could also be bought for $3 more, at $48, direct from Govee through October 31st, which The Verge called still one of its better prices to date. The customizable 6.56-foot (2m) strip can display millions of colors and shades of white and can create light patterns that sync with music.

The Verge framed the timing on October 28th, 2023 around the calendar: Halloween is not the only holiday on the horizon as October draws to a close, since once the clock strikes midnight on October 31st, Mariah Carey will defrost, peppermint mochas will inevitably return, and the 2023 holiday season will have officially begun. While handy throughout the year, the light strip is particularly convenient during Halloween and other holidays — the bright, tunable LEDs can flash and blink to the beat of your music and act as festive decor that adds a pop of color to holiday parties. What is particularly great about this strip, the writer noted, is that it supports the newer Matter protocol, which allows you to control the lights with a wide array of smart home platforms.



---


# Preparing Both Partner And Family Before A Holiday Introduction

Relationship experts told The Independent that the preparation for introducing a partner to your family at the holidays happens in a set order, and before anyone travels. The precondition is clarity between the couple: Saba Lurie, a licensed marriage and family therapist at Take Root Therapy in California, says there is no right or wrong time for the introduction, but the intentions behind it must be clear — you should already have discussed where the relationship is headed. Step one is then to brief your partner on the purpose: "I think you should tell the person why you're bringing them home for the holidays, so you're on the same page about the intentions and what's motivating the decision to include," Lurie said. Step two is to brief them on the family they are walking into: "Sometimes it can be helpful for them to know about the dynamics that they're stepping into and how they can best support you. Frankly, they should be aware if there is tension or if there is stress within your family."

Step three runs the other way. Rachel Zar, a licensed marriage and family therapist at Spark Chicago Therapy, says the family needs advance notice too: "If there's something about your partner that could be surprising to your family, or that's a notable difference from who someone you've brought home before, tell your relatives that. Let's set your family and partner up for success." Step four is to say how you want your family to include your partner — for example by incorporating your partner's family traditions into your own celebration. The limit on the procedure is oversharing: Zar advises against telling too much before Christmas, since you still want your family and partner to connect in person rather than hearing about each other through the grapevine. Zar also sets the context for why the preparation matters — every family is different, but problems arise mainly because we put too much pressure on having a joyful holiday: "I think anytime that emotions are heightened, with the holidays certainly being one of those times, our expectations are really high. We're expecting it to be this joyful, happy, perfect occasion. So, we sometimes forget that the holidays come with a lot of stress."

# Logistics And Check-Ins During A Holiday Family Visit

The first is settling logistics in advance: if you are travelling, you may need to decide on sleeping arrangements — potentially staying somewhere other than a parent's house — in order to minimise family stress. "It would be really helpful to have conversations beforehand, so it's clear what you are agreeing or not agreeing to," said Saba Lurie. # Black Friday / Cyber Monday

## Definition

Black Friday and Cyber Monday are the paired retail sale events — the Friday after the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday and the Monday that follows it — that together anchor the start of the U.S. holiday shopping season, with retailers running discount campaigns across both dates and the days between them.

## Context

Retailers treat the two days less as isolated events than as bookends of a single extended sale window: Engadget reported that Amazon, Target, Best Buy, and Walmart all kicked off Black Friday-branded deals as early as late October 2023, so that "what was once a one-day event filled with limited-time deals has grown into a month-long event with a plethora of sales to sift through each day." Amazon itself began its Black Friday sale on Friday, November 17 — a week ahead of the calendar date — then switched to "Cyber Monday" branding in the early hours of Saturday, November 25, carrying many of the same discounts forward under the new label through the official close on Monday, November 27. Polygon likewise noted that the two named days (November 24 and 27 in 2023) no longer bound when the best prices actually appear, since retailers now front-load doorbuster-style deals across the preceding weeks. The pairing also functions as the header under which media outlets organize their own coverage: The Verge's "under $25" roundup groups both days together as one shopping period with "always a ton of hype about the discounts on big-ticket items."

## Key Characteristics

- **Two named days, one continuous season** — Black Friday (the day after Thanksgiving) and Cyber Monday (the following Monday) are distinct calendar dates, but retailer promotions now span from late October through the Monday close, blurring the boundary between them.
- **Retailer-driven timing shift** — multiple retailers (Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, Target) started Black Friday-branded deals days to weeks before the actual date in 2023, a strategy aimed at spreading out demand rather than concentrating it on one doorbuster day.
- **Deal carryover across the pairing** — items discounted for Black Friday commonly remain discounted, or are re-labeled, once Cyber Monday branding begins, rather than the two events offering wholly separate deal sets.
- **Broad retailer participation** — coverage spans Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and several other retailers, indicating the pairing is not a single-retailer promotion but an industry-wide sale convention.
- **High online-spend period** — the surrounding Thanksgiving-to-Cyber-Monday window ("Cyber Week") is tracked by analytics firms as a major driver of U.S. holiday online sales, with Thanksgiving Day alone producing billions in online spending as the de facto season opener.

# Thanksgiving Observance Outside the United States

Thanksgiving is not observed only in America: while it is one of the most important cultural holidays in the United States, Canada also has its own Thanksgiving Day, held on the second Monday in October, and Liberia celebrates Thanksgiving on the first Thursday of November.

The distinguishing feature between these observances is therefore the date rather than the existence of the holiday — the American fourth-Thursday-in-November timing is one national convention among several.

# Smart Home Device

## Definition

A smart home device is a connected household product — a speaker, camera, thermostat, light, plug, lock, sprinkler controller, or storage container — that can be controlled remotely (typically via a smartphone app or voice assistant) and often coordinates with other such devices through a shared smart home platform.

## Context

The corpus covers smart home devices mainly as a deal category in seasonal shopping roundups: The Verge devotes an entire Prime Day roundup (doc_0205) to smart home products, grouping the category into robot vacuums, security cameras and doorbells, smart speakers and displays, and smart lighting/locks/thermostats/sprinklers/plugs — all controllable from a phone and, increasingly, interoperable through a common home-automation platform.

The Verge's Black Friday under-$25 roundup (doc_0090) similarly carves out a "Smart home tech" section for budget smart plugs and a smart lamp, placed right alongside networking gear like a Wi-Fi extender.

The term also surfaces as a regulatory subject: the EU's antitrust probe into Amazon's iRobot acquisition explicitly gathered views from market participants including "suppliers of RVCs and other smart home devices," treating robot vacuum cleaners as one instance of the broader smart-home-device category.

Keep Labs' medicine-storage device (the Keep) shares the same connected-appliance characteristics described above — an app to unlock the lid, plus a scale and phone notifications to track medication use — even though its own category (secure medical storage) is unusual for a smart home device.

## Key Characteristics

- **Remote/app control** — devices are opened, adjusted, or monitored via a companion smartphone app (e.g., the Keep's lid opens via an app button; the Meross smart garage door controller lets you control your garage door from anywhere, and the MyQ Chamberlain Smart Garage Control opens the garage door from any location using a smartphone).
- **Voice-assistant integration** — many devices work with a voice assistant such as Amazon's Alexa; the Echo smart speaker is described as "a great way to get started with the smart home" and doubles as a smart home hub.
- **Interoperability via shared protocols** — devices such as the Govee LED Strip Light M1 and the Google Nest Thermostat support the Matter protocol specifically so a single hub can control gadgets from different manufacturers ("a wide array of smart home platforms" / "every major smart home platform, including Apple Home").
- **Hub/bridge role** — some devices (the fourth-gen Echo) act as more than an endpoint: it is also a Matter controller, Thread border router, and Zigbee bridge, connecting other gadgets to the home network.
- **Regulatory relevance beyond consumer tech** — the category is broad enough to draw antitrust scrutiny of channel access: the EU's iRobot probe frames robot vacuum cleaners as one of the "other smart home devices" whose competing suppliers depend on Amazon's marketplace for distribution.

# Thanksgiving 2023 Retail Closure Policy

The origin of that policy was the pandemic. The outbreak had initially pushed these chains to close their doors on Thanksgiving in order to limit crowding and spread out the shopping season.

The closure is not universal, and it is short. Not all grocery stores remain closed on Thanksgiving Day — there are some retailers that shoppers could visit on the morning of the holiday, in preparation for the annual feast — and once Thanksgiving Day comes to a close, many stores reopen on the Friday, operating during their earlier or usual business hours in preparation for some of the biggest sales of the year.

# Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade

The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is the annual parade held in New York City on Thanksgiving Day, and is the world's largest Thanksgiving parade.

Its defining features are giant balloons of cartoon characters that float above the city sky, along with marching bands and dancers. Photographs of the event show the Tom Turkey float in place to start the parade, the Ronald McDonald, Charlie Brown, Olaf and Sinclair DINO balloons being inflated or flying as the parade passes down 6th Avenue, marching bands, flag wavers, clowns on roller blades and other performers, with an NYPD officer standing by.

# Criticism of Thanksgiving as a Celebration of Conquest

The case against Thanksgiving attacks the premise that the holiday commemorates a peaceable shared meal: although many Americans view it as a beloved holiday, it is viewed by many who have abandoned it as an erroneous celebration of what was actually the conquest of Native Americans and Native American lands.

The grounds are historical rather than about the modern celebration itself. The celebration has become controversial because Thanksgiving has a contentious history that goes far beyond when the first feast was held — the event has been viewed as deeply controversial over the years, due to the contentious history of the first Thanksgiving celebration in the 17th century.

A second strand of the objection concerns how that history is transmitted. In addition to being a holiday steeped with cultural appropriation, the period of American history involved is frequently white-washed, which leads some Americans to ignore or condemn the holiday, or instead to observe a National Day of Mourning. So while Thanksgiving is often viewed as a day for Americans to express what they are grateful for, that does not mean that everyone will celebrate.

# Friendsgiving Alternative Activity Ideas

For a Friendsgiving that is not a sit-down dinner, the options below can be chosen instead of hosting a big meal; the enabling precondition throughout is that Friendsgiving is not necessarily held on the Thanksgiving holiday itself, which frees the date and the venue.

Visit a holiday market. While Christmas is still over a month away, many cities in the US already have their holiday-themed markets up and running, so a Friendsgiving held off the holiday can be used as an opportunity to check out new shops. In New York City, Bank of America hosts its annual Winter Village at Bryant Park in Manhattan, where a wide variety of food vendors lets a group pick dinner and dessert, and vendors also sell goods from ornaments to jewellery to scarves — a chance to do some early holiday shopping.

Host a movie marathon at home. This is the budget-friendly indoor alternative to a big dinner: with the help of friends, make a list of any horror, romance or comedy films to watch for the day, and top the activity off by supplying an assortment of snacks or cooking a meal together. Options can match the Thanksgiving theme, with films like A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood (2019), Toy Story (1995), Addams Family Values (1993) and A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving (1973), and Christmas films can be added to the mix, including Elf (2003), It's A Wonderful Life (1947) and Steel Magnolias (1989).

Go on a hike — this one is weather-dependent, so check the conditions outside first. Whether at a local park or a trail an hour or so away, hiking is the perfect daytime activity for a friend group of any size.

Bake or decorate treats. This is another easy indoor activity: make a pie from scratch or simply frost ready-bake sugar cookies, which gives the group something interactive to do together. Treats can be chosen on theme with the fall and winter seasons, from baking an apple crisp to decorating gingerbread cookies.

Run a Turkey Trot. Whether before, during, or after Thanksgiving Day, many cities in America host an annual Turkey Trot run, and the length varies — from a 5K to a half marathon — so the group can pick what it prefers. In New York City in 2023, one Turkey Trot was held at Flushing Meadows-Corona Park on 25 November, with participants running for the Rolling Thunder organisation, a non-profit "for mainstream athletes who are developmentally disabled or have other special needs".

Host an at-home wine tasting. A night out at the bars can get expensive depending on the venue, and a trip to a winery can rack up a hefty bill and is not the most enjoyable activity in cold weather — which is the reason to host your own instead. Everyone brings a different type of wine, from red to white, and the group tries a few sips from each bottle; a big wine fan may end up discovering a new favourite brand. A homemade charcuterie board, filled with different meats and cheeses, can be prepared to pair with the wine.

Play an outdoor game. If the friends have a fun, competitive side, the group can host the event in any big outdoor space — a local park or a friend's backyard. Football in particular meets the typical theme of Thanksgiving, as a beloved tradition on the actual holiday is to watch a sports game with the family.

Hold an early gift exchange. The winter holidays are still weeks away, but Friendsgiving can be used to host the annual exchange: many friend groups in the US opt for the budget-friendly Secret Santa format, where each person is randomly assigned someone to give a gift to and, during the exchange, reveals that they are that person's "secret Santa" before handing over the present.

# The Friendsgiving Tradition

Friendsgiving is a popular tradition held around Thanksgiving that consists of a celebration with close pals, arising because some Americans do not have the opportunity to return home for the holidays.

Its defining feature is that it is not fixed to the holiday itself: Friendsgiving can be held before, during, or even after the 23rd of November in 2023. Over the years, people have celebrated it in a similar vein to Thanksgiving, with everyone sitting around the table for one big feast, and it is often done potluck style, with each guest bringing their own dish to contribute.

The big meal is a convention rather than a requirement — you do not need to have one to celebrate your Friendsgiving, as there are many ways to change up the usual plans. The tradition sits alongside Thanksgiving itself, which remains a day filled with food and family, as Americans write their menus and buy ingredients for their lavish feasts.

# Why Introducing A Partner To Your Family Can Deepen The Relationship

Relationship experts argue that letting a partner see you with your family — including the awkward parts — deepens the relationship rather than endangering it, because the act is a vulnerable one. "I think introducing a significant other to family is a really vulnerable act, and that vulnerability is going to be what allows for greater intimacy," Saba Lurie told The Independent. "When your significant other sees you with your family, they may see another side of you that they may not have had access to before."

The obvious objection — that a partner may discover your relationships with your parents and extended family are complex — is answered by framing that discovery as evidence of self-knowledge, provided you have explained the family dynamics in advance. "I think that we tend to be our best relational self when we've really done the work around understanding all of our past relationships," Rachel Zar explained. "You can tell your partner: 'I don't have a close relationship with my brother, and here's why. Here are the intentional choices that I've made around it.' Or you can say: 'Here's my chosen family. These are the people who are important to me.' Your significant other will see that you've been introspective and have takeaways around how you've navigated your family's origin." The conclusion carries a condition and a limit: as long as the couple have discussed their relationship expectations both before and during the holidays, the introduction may deepen the relationship and be a step in the right direction — or it may simply be an opportunity to bring two important people in your life together. And the timing remains the couple's own call: "I don't think there's ever going to be a perfect time for folks," Lurie said. # Thanksgiving: The American Holiday

Thanksgiving is a national holiday in the United States, celebrated every fourth Thursday in November — falling on Thursday 23 November in 2023 — and it is a cultural holiday that symbolises peace, thankfulness, and the beginning of the holiday season. # OpenAI's Founding And Its 2023 Board Crisis

The Rosewood hotel dinner led to the creation of a startup called OpenAI later that year; backed by hundreds of millions of dollars from Elon Musk and other funders, the lab promised to protect the world from Larry Page's vision. Thanks to its ChatGPT chatbot, OpenAI has fundamentally changed the technology industry and introduced the world to the risks and potential of artificial intelligence, and it is valued at more than $US80 billion, about $A123 billion, according to two people familiar with the company's latest funding round. Musk and Sam Altman's partnership did not survive, and the two have since stopped speaking. Altman's own gloss on such splits: "There is disagreement, mistrust, egos. The closer people are to being pointed in the same direction, the more contentious the disagreements are. You see this in sects and religious orders. There are bitter fights between the closest people."

The month before the 9 December 2023 article, that infighting came to OpenAI's boardroom: rebel board members tried to force out Altman because they believed they could no longer trust him to build AI that would benefit humanity, and over five chaotic days OpenAI looked as if it were going to fall apart until the board, pressured by giant investors and by employees who threatened to follow Altman out the door, backed down. The drama gave the world its first glimpse of the bitter feuds among those who will determine the future of AI, but years before the near meltdown there was a little-publicised but ferocious competition in Silicon Valley for control of the technology now quickly reshaping the world, from how children are taught to how wars are fought. That earlier story begins with DeepMind: five years before the Napa Valley party and two before the cat breakthrough on YouTube, Demis Hassabis, a 34-year-old neuroscientist, walked into a cocktail party at Peter Thiel's San Francisco town house and realised he had hit pay dirt, because there in Thiel's living room, overlooking the city's Palace of Fine Arts and a swan pond, was a chessboard; Hassabis had once been the second-best player in the world in the under-14 category, and said "I was preparing for that meeting for a year. I thought that would be my unique hook in: I knew that he loved chess."

# OpenAI's Nonprofit Governance And Capped-Profit Structure

OpenAI's for-profit subsidiary, OpenAI Global, LLC, is fully controlled by OpenAI's nonprofit: the subsidiary is permitted to commercialize its technology, but it is subject to the nonprofit's mission of attaining artificial general intelligence (AGI), which OpenAI defines as AI that can "outperform humans at most economically valuable work."

The discriminating feature of this structure is where the power over AGI sits. The nonprofit OpenAI's board has the power both to determine when the company has achieved AGI and to exclude that AGI from IP licenses and other commercial terms — including terms with Microsoft, one of OpenAI's biggest investors and a steadfast integrator of OpenAI's technologies. OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit in 2015 but restructured in 2019 as a "capped-profit" company in order to raise capital, an acknowledgement of the huge costs associated with training cutting-edge AI systems. Altman underlined the point in an interview with the Financial Times in the week of his firing, saying he "hoped" Microsoft would increase its investment to help pay for "huge" imminent model training costs.



---


# The OpenAI Board Ousts Sam Altman, November 2023

As reported on November 18, 2023, the OpenAI board had ejected billionaire and AI evangelist Sam Altman from his CEO role after an apparent vote of no confidence. The board's exact wording in a release issued that afternoon: Altman's "departure follows a deliberative review process by the board, which concluded that he was not consistently candid in his communications with the board, hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities."

What followed was a whirlwind four days for OpenAI, the generative AI poster child behind the smash hit ChatGPT. The board ousted CEO and co-founder Altman and demoted president and co-founder Greg Brockman, who subsequently resigned, paving the way for what looked like a mutiny by staff insisting the founders be reinstated post-haste. By the time TechCrunch wrote again on November 21, 2023, Microsoft had already hired Altman and Brockman to head up a new internal AI unit — though, as things transpired, nothing had actually been signed yet, with rumors suggesting the ousted leaders might actually return to OpenAI after all, in some capacity at least.

TechCrunch cautioned on November 18 that the full truth would not be known for a long time, as the characters in the drama are likely to be NDA'ed up. Per various whispers and leaks, an all-hands meeting about the situation that afternoon did not produce any revelations beyond banal reassurances that the company is fine and they will get a fresh CEO soon.



---


# Musk's Founding Of OpenAI And His Departure

Convinced that Larry Page's optimistic view of AI was dead wrong, and angry at his loss of DeepMind, Musk built his own lab: OpenAI was founded in late 2015, just a few months after he met with Sam Altman at the Rosewood hotel in Silicon Valley. Musk pumped money into the lab and his former PayPal buddies, Reid Hoffman and Peter Thiel, came along for the ride; the three men and others pledged to put $US1 billion into the project, which Altman, then 30, would help run, and to get started they poached Ilya Sutskever from Google, one of the graduate students Google had "bought" in Hinton's auction. Initially Musk wanted to operate OpenAI as a nonprofit, free from the economic incentives driving Google and other corporations, but by the time Google wowed the tech community with its Go stunt he was changing his mind about how it should be run: he desperately wanted OpenAI to invent something that would capture the world's imagination and close the gap with Google, and it wasn't getting the job done as a nonprofit.

In late 2017 Musk hatched a plan to wrest control of the lab from Altman and the other founders and transform it into a commercial operation that would join forces with Tesla and rely on supercomputers the car company was developing, according to four people familiar with the matter; when Altman and others pushed back, Musk quit and said he would focus on his own AI work at Tesla. In February 2018 he announced his departure to OpenAI's staff on the top floor of the startup's offices in a converted truck factory, three people who attended said; when he said OpenAI needed to move faster, one researcher retorted that Musk was being reckless, and Musk called the researcher a "jackass" and stormed out, taking his deep pockets with him. OpenAI suddenly needed new financing in a hurry: Altman flew to Sun Valley for a conference and ran into Satya Nadella, Microsoft's CEO, and a tie-up seemed natural, since Altman knew Microsoft's chief technology officer Kevin Scott and Microsoft had bought LinkedIn from Hoffman, an OpenAI board member; Nadella told Scott to get it done. The deal closed in 2019, leaving Altman and OpenAI with a for-profit company formed under the original nonprofit, $US1 billion in fresh capital, and Microsoft with a new way to build AI into its vast cloud computing service. Not everyone inside OpenAI was happy.

# OpenAI's Nonprofit-To-For-Profit Structure

OpenAI started out as a nonprofit when it launched with financial backing from Tesla CEO Elon Musk and others, with stated aims to "advance digital intelligence in the way that is most likely to benefit humanity as a whole, unconstrained by a need to generate financial return." That changed in 2018, when it incorporated a for-profit business, OpenAI LP, and shifted nearly all its staff into that business, not long after releasing its first generation of the GPT large language model for mimicking human writing.

Around the same time, Musk — who had co-chaired its board with Altman — resigned from the board, in a move OpenAI said would eliminate a "potential future conflict for Elon" due to Tesla's work on building self-driving systems. The resulting arrangement is a split one: OpenAI's board has preserved its nonprofit governance structure, while the startup it oversees has increasingly sought to capitalize on its technology by tailoring its popular chatbot to business customers.

# Sam Altman Fired As OpenAI CEO In November 2023

Sam Altman was fired as CEO of OpenAI late on Friday, November 17, 2023, by the board of directors of OpenAI, Inc. — the 501(c)(3) nonprofit that acts as the governing body for OpenAI, the startup behind ChatGPT, GPT-4 and DALL-E 3. He both left the company's board of directors and stepped down as CEO, with chief technology officer Mira Murati stepping in as interim CEO.

OpenAI announced the shake-up in a post on its official blog; the company's management team was made aware shortly after. The blog post said Altman's departure followed a "deliberative review process by the board" which concluded that Altman "wasn't consistently candid in his communications" with other board members, "hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities," and that the board "no longer has confidence in [Altman's] ability to continue leading OpenAI." In a joint statement the board wrote that "OpenAI was deliberately structured to advance our mission: to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all humanity," said it remained "fully committed to serving this mission," thanked Altman for "his many contributions to the founding and growth of OpenAI," and said that "we believe new leadership is necessary as we move forward" and that Mira, "as the leader of the company's research, product, and safety functions," was "exceptionally qualified" as interim CEO. OpenAI said it would begin a formal search for a permanent CEO immediately.

Altman responded on X: "i loved my time at openai. it was transformative for me personally, and hopefully the world a little bit. most of all i loved working with such talented people. will have more to say about what's next later." The removal came unexpectedly. OpenAI had just hosted its first developer conference, OpenAI DevDay, the week before with Altman emceeing; Altman had spoken at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation conference and at an Oakland, California event on the Thursday. According to The Verge and The New York Times, citing multiple internal sources, OpenAI employees learned of Altman's firing when it was announced publicly. The same change also saw co-founder Greg Brockman step down as chairman of the board while remaining OpenAI's president, reporting to Murati.

# The OpenAI Crisis As A Case Against Centralized AI Control

The claim is that the OpenAI debacle exposes a structural risk in depending on a centralized proprietary AI player. The situation remained fluid as of November 21, 2023, with any number of potential outcomes still on the table, but the whole debacle has shone a spotlight on the forces that control the burgeoning AI revolution, leading many to question what happens if you go all-in on a centralized proprietary player and things then go belly-up.

Mark Surman, president and executive director at the Mozilla Foundation, put the ground this way to TechCrunch: "The OpenAI / Microsoft drama underlines one of the big near-term risks with AI — that this next wave of technology is controlled by the same tiny set of players who have shaped that last era of the internet. We might have a chance of avoiding this if GPT-X were responsibly open sourced, giving researchers and startups a shot at making this technology safer, more useful and more trustworthy for people everywhere." The warrant is that concentration of control is itself the hazard, and open sourcing distributes it.

TechCrunch qualifies the claim: it is still too early to make any surefire claims on what impact the OpenAI fallout will have on LLM development and uptake in the future, and Altman and Brockman are undoubtedly steady hands for a commercial AI startup who may even return to steward OpenAI. But some might argue it is unhealthy that so much focus lies on just a handful of people — and it is telling that their departure has created such widespread havoc.

# Board Governance

In this corpus, board governance is illustrated by cases where a board of directors exercises (or conspicuously lacks) the power to oversee and remove a company's CEO: OpenAI's board firing Sam Altman, Flexport's board ousting Dave Clark, and FTX's absence of any board at all.

## Context

The corpus's clearest working example is OpenAI's board, which in November 2023 fired co-founder and CEO Sam Altman after "a deliberative review process" concluded he was "not consistently candid in his communications with the board, hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities."
That framing treats board governance as a standing check on the CEO: the board's stated justification was not a business or legal failure but a breakdown in the information flow the board needs to do its job.
OpenAI's board itself sits atop a nonprofit structure that "preserved its nonprofit governance structure" even as the startup underneath pursued commercial growth, so the board's authority over the CEO ran through that nonprofit layer rather than ordinary shareholder control.
Board composition determines whose judgment gets exercised: OpenAI's board consisted of chief scientist Ilya Sutskever and three non-employee directors (Adam D'Angelo, Tasha McCauley, and Helen Toner), and the subsequent standoff over reinstating Altman turned on negotiating a new board (Bret Taylor, Larry Summers, Adam D'Angelo) as a condition of his return.
The corpus also frames board governance by its absence: Paradigm co-founder Matt Huang testified he was "concerned about FTX's lack of a board of directors" before investing anyway, though on cross-examination he said Bankman-Fried told him he didn't want investors as directors but did plan on having a board with experts.
Flexport's board, by contrast, illustrates governance operating through composition rather than absence: a board "made up largely of investors who were betting on the founder" held quarterly meetings on June 1 and Aug. 31 before Clark was forced to resign on Sept. 5.

## Key Characteristics

- **Power to remove or reinstate the CEO** — OpenAI's board fired Altman outright, then negotiated the terms (including its own reconstitution) under which he could return.
- **Grounded in a formal duty to oversee, not just advise** — the board's justification for firing Altman was specifically that his conduct hindered "its ability to exercise its responsibilities," i.e., an oversight duty rather than a performance complaint.
- **Structure shapes authority** — OpenAI's nonprofit board sat above the commercial subsidiary, giving it authority that ordinary shareholder-elected boards would not have over a purely for-profit company.
- **Composition determines outcome** — who sits on the board (employee vs. non-employee directors, investor-aligned vs. independent) is itself a lever contested during crises, as seen in both the OpenAI reinstatement talks and Flexport's investor-heavy board.
- **Its absence is itself notable** — the corpus flags FTX's lack of a board of directors as a specific governance gap investors identified before FTX's collapse, distinguishing "no oversight body" from "an oversight body that failed."

## Background (external)

Outside this corpus, corporate governance is generally defined as the mechanisms, processes, and relations by which corporations are directed and controlled by their boards of directors, managers, shareholders, and other stakeholders.
The widely cited Cadbury Report formulation puts it more simply: corporate governance is "the system by which companies are directed and controlled."
Source: [Corporate governance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporate_governance), Wikipedia, accessed 2026-09-02.

Microsoft is OpenAI's largest corporate backer — it had poured $13 billion into OpenAI as of November 2023 and holds what amounts to a 49% stake — and its public response to Altman's firing was to reaffirm the partnership and to back interim CEO Mira Murati rather than to intervene.

# Valuation

## Definition

Across the corpus, "valuation" denotes the dollar figure attached to a company at a given moment — most often the headline number a startup or company is described as "valued at" following a funding round or share sale.

The corpus also uses the term for the analytical output public-stock analysts arrive at by pricing a stock through one of two competing methods, relative valuation or absolute (DCF) valuation.

## Context

The corpus repeatedly ties valuation to funding rounds and their trajectory: FTX's valuation rose to $32 billion at its peak after a $400 million Series C round in January 2022, before its collapse into bankruptcy; Flexport was valued at $8 billion amid the turmoil around Dave Clark's ouster; Adaptive, an AI startup based in Amsterdam and co-founded by French AI researcher Julien Launay, was about to raise a seed round at a $100 million valuation; and OpenAI closed a $300 million share sale at a $27–29 billion valuation in April 2023, separate from an earlier Microsoft investment. Scalable Capital's $65 million raise came in at a "flat" $1.4 billion valuation — unchanged from its prior round despite the company being four to five times larger, illustrating that valuation is a negotiated figure set at the moment of a deal, not a mechanical output of size or growth alone. Separately, the corpus's "Fundamental Investing" piece treats valuation as a discipline: analysts price stocks either through absolute valuation (a discounted cash flow model, "an interesting story backed by credible and validated numbers") or relative valuation (comparing a stock's PE, P/B, or EV/EBITDA ratio against peers, "an interesting number backed by a credible and validated story"), with about 85% of equity research and 50% of M&A valuation work using the relative approach because full DCF modeling across hundreds of stocks is impractical.

## Key Characteristics

- **Point-in-time and deal-driven** — a valuation is set at the moment of a funding round or share sale (e.g., FTX's $32B peak after its Series C, OpenAI's $27–29B share sale, Scalable Capital's raise), not a continuously updated market price.
- **Can be "flat"** — a company can raise new capital at the same valuation as its prior round even after growing substantially, as Scalable Capital did at $1.4 billion despite being four to five times bigger than at its 2021 round.
- **Detached from later outcomes** — a peak valuation (FTX's $32 billion) does not protect against later collapse; valuation reflects investor sentiment and negotiated terms at the time, not guaranteed durability.
- **Two competing methodologies for public stocks** — absolute valuation (DCF, modeling a company's own cash flows) versus relative valuation (comparing multiples like PE, P/B, EV/EBITDA against peers, growth, and history); the corpus reports relative valuation as the more prevalent in practice despite absolute valuation being considered theoretically superior.
- **Applies across scales** — the term covers everything from a seed-stage AI startup ($100 million) to a crypto exchange or foundation model company (tens of billions of dollars), with the same basic concept of "worth implied by a deal" underlying both.

## Background (external)

Outside the corpus, valuation in finance is the general process of determining the worth of a potential investment, asset, or security, typically through discounted-cashflow, relative, or contingent-claim approaches. (Source: Wikipedia, "Valuation (finance)," accessed 2026-09-02.)

# The Four Layers Of The GenAI Tech Stack

Rick Grinnell, founder and managing partner at Glasswing Ventures, categorizes the generative AI landscape into four distinct layers in the firm's proprietary view of the GenAI tech stack: foundation model providers, middle-tier companies, end-market or top-layer applications, and full stack or end-to-end vertical companies. He was answering, in TechCrunch's 13 October 2023 survey of AI investors, whether startups will build striated solutions for individual layers of the LLM stack — models, pre-training solutions and fine-tuning tools — or pursue a more vertical approach.

The relations between layers are stated as market-structure predictions. At the foundational layer, providers like Alphabet/Google's Bard, Microsoft/OpenAI's GPT-4, and Anthropic's Claude show that the more significant players possess inherent advantages regarding data accessibility, talent pool and computational resources; this layer is expected to settle into an oligopolistic structure like the cloud provider market, albeit with the addition of a strong open source contingency that will drive considerable third-party adoption. Above the model itself lies the largest market opportunity: companies that introduce AI-powered APIs and operational layers for specific industries will create brand-new use cases and transform workflows, and by embracing this technology to revolutionize workflows, these companies stand to unlock substantial value. Within the stack, most of the opportunity lies in the application layer, where the best applications will harness their in-house expertise to build specialized middle-layer tooling and blend them with the appropriate foundational models, and where startups can use speed to their advantage as they work to "innovate, iterate and deploy solutions" to customers.

The range over which the model holds is explicitly limited by market immaturity. The market is still far from being crystallized; LLMs are still in their infancy, with adoption at large corporations and startups lacking full maturity and refinement, and robust tools and platforms are needed to enable broader utilization among businesses and individuals. Startups have the opportunity here to act quickly, find novel solutions to emerging problems, and define new categories. Even large tech companies recognize the gaps in their services and have begun investing heavily in startups alongside VCs — these companies apply AI to their internal processes and thus see the value startups bring to LLM deployment and integration, as with the recent investments from Microsoft, Nvidia, and Salesforce into companies like Inflection AI and Cohere.

A dissenting position within the same survey bears on how much weight the layer model should carry for strategy. Edward Tsai, a managing partner at Alumni Ventures, offered a potentially "controversial opinion that VCs and startups may want to temporarily reduce their focus on defensibility and increase their focus on products that deliver compelling value and focusing on speed to market."

# ChatGPT Overview And Significance

ChatGPT is OpenAI's text-generating AI chatbot, and it has taken the world by storm: what started as a tool to hyper-charge productivity through writing essays and code from short text prompts has evolved into a behemoth used by more than 92% of Fortune 500 companies for far more wide-ranging needs.

That growth propelled OpenAI itself into becoming one of the most-hyped companies in recent memory, even though CEO and co-founder Sam Altman's firing and swift return raised concerns about the company's direction and opened the door for competitors. The fallout was still settling, but it might empower competitors such as Meta and its LLaMA family of large language models, or help other AI startups get attention and funding as the industry watched OpenAI implode and put itself back together. Whatever the nefarious side of ChatGPT, it was clear that AI tools were not going away anytime soon: since its initial launch nearly a year earlier, ChatGPT had hit 100 million weekly active users, and OpenAI was investing heavily in it.

The capability boundary at the time was defined by model access and modality. GPT-4, which can write more naturally and fluently than previous models, remained largely exclusive to paying ChatGPT users, although it could be accessed for free through Microsoft's Bing Chat in the Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome and Safari web browsers. Beyond GPT-4 and the OpenAI DevDay announcements, OpenAI had recently connected ChatGPT to the internet for all users, and with the integration of DALL-E 3, users could generate both text and images right inside ChatGPT.

# OpenAI Corporate Deals And Business Moves

Alongside its product releases, OpenAI made a series of corporate moves in 2023: a news-content partnership with Axel Springer, an indemnity promise to business customers over copyright claims, its first acquisition, a $300 million share sale, and a stalled attempt to trademark "GPT."

OpenAI struck a deal with the Berlin-based news publisher Axel Springer, which owns Business Insider and Politico, to "help provide people with new ways to access quality, real-time news content through our AI tools"; under it OpenAI will train its generative AI models on the publisher's content and add recent Axel Springer-published articles to ChatGPT. Bowing to peer pressure, OpenAI also said it would pay legal costs incurred by customers who face lawsuits over IP claims against work generated by an OpenAI tool, though the protections seemingly do not extend to all OpenAI products, such as the free and Plus tiers of ChatGPT. In its first public acquisition in its seven-year history, OpenAI acquired Global Illumination, a New York-based startup leveraging AI to build creative tools, infrastructure and digital experiences; OpenAI wrote in a brief blog post, "We're very excited for the impact they'll have here at OpenAI. The entire team has joined OpenAI to work on our core products including ChatGPT."

On financing, OpenAI closed a $300 million share sale at a $27 billion to $29 billion valuation, with VC firms including Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive and K2 Global picking up new shares according to documents seen by TechCrunch, and a source saying Founders Fund was also investing. That round was separate from a large Microsoft investment announced earlier in the year, which closed in January and is believed to be around $10 billion. On trademarks, OpenAI applied for a trademark for "GPT" — Generative Pre-trained Transformer — in December, and petitioned the USPTO to speed up the process, citing the "myriad infringements and counterfeit apps" beginning to spring into existence; the petition was dismissed because OpenAI's attorneys neglected to pay an associated fee and to provide "appropriate documentary evidence supporting the justification of special action," meaning a decision could take up to five more months.

# Sam Altman's Rise As The Face Of Generative AI

In the year since Altman catapulted ChatGPT to global fame, he became Silicon Valley's sought-after voice on the promise and potential dangers of artificial intelligence, and his sudden and mostly unexplained exit brought uncertainty to the industry's future. He helped start OpenAI as a nonprofit research laboratory in 2015, but it was ChatGPT's explosion into public consciousness that thrust him into the spotlight as a face of generative AI — technology that can produce novel imagery, passages of text and other media. On a world tour in 2023 he was mobbed by a crowd of adoring fans at an event in London.

He has sat with multiple heads of state to discuss AI's potential and perils. On Thursday, 2023-11-16, he took part in a CEO summit at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation conference in San Francisco, where OpenAI is based. At OpenAI's first developer conference the week before, Altman was the main speaker, showcasing a vision for a future of AI agents that could help people with a variety of tasks; days later he announced the company would have to pause new subscriptions to its premium version of ChatGPT because it had exceeded capacity.
