# Digital Services Act Obligations For Very Large Online Platforms

The EU's Digital Services Act places an obligation on so-called very large online platforms (VLOPs) to assess societal risks attached to their use of algorithms and to put in place "reasonable, proportionate and effective mitigation measures" for identified risks, with their reporting and mitigation plans subject to independent audit and oversight by the Commission.

Back in April 2023, X/Twitter was named as one of 19 larger platforms that face the strictest level of regulation under the DSA. The bloc's executive, which also devised the anti-disinformation Code, is responsible for oversight of VLOPs' compliance with the DSA, and has powers under the law to fine violators up to 6% of global annual turnover; the Commission has previously wanted that not following the Code of Practice on Disinformation would be factored into its assessments. The key distinction is that the Code is voluntary while compliance with the DSA is not: the DSA is now legally binding on X/Twitter, including in particular the obligation on VLOPs to mitigate the risks their platforms pose for the spread of disinformation. On timing, the Commission noted that the TrustLab study to measure two Structural Indicators covers signatories of the Code at the time of the launch of the exercise, which then included X/Twitter, and that during this period the DSA had not entered into force yet for VLOPs and VLOSEs including X/Twitter. The Commission said it could not comment further on the substance of the risk assessments, that it was analysing available information on a range of issues and in close contact with X but could not comment on specifics and timelines, and that — as stated by Commissioner Thierry Breton — minor protection and integrity of elections are priorities in the enforcement of the DSA.

One practical limit on the deterrent: while the price for X ignoring the EU's warnings on disinformation could be steep, its ad revenue has cratered since Musk's takeover as a result of his failure to tackle toxicity and harmful disinformation encouraging an advertiser exodus, and shrinking earnings would effectively downsize any future penalties X could face under the DSA.

# Data Breach

## Definition

A data breach, in the corpus, is an incident in which hackers or unintended exposure let unauthorized parties reach personal or organizational data — spanning the 2017 Equifax hack, the 2023 23andMe breach, an individual's hacked Roblox account, and, more loosely, TikTok's pre-consent data scraping, which a senator branded a "mass breach of privacy" (doc_0015, doc_0334, doc_0178, doc_0189).

## Context

The corpus uses the term across several registers of the same underlying event. The canonical reference point is the Equifax data breach of 2017, invoked in a discussion of Google's search-revenue deals as the event that made identity-theft-protection services like LifeLock a hot commercial topic (doc_0015). The clearest 2023 instance is 23andMe: hackers first accessed the personal data of about 14,000 users (0.1% of customers), a number the company later acknowledged undercounted the real scope, in a breach it disclosed in October 2023 (doc_0334). The same TechCrunch weekly roundup that covers 23andMe also reports a related but distinct exposure — patient scans and health records "spilling online" through security weaknesses in the decades-old DICOM medical-imaging standard, which made private data accessible on the open web without any hacker having to breach a perimeter at all (doc_0334). At smaller scale, the term extends to individual account compromise: Sarah Michelle Gellar described her son's Roblox account being "hacked," which she treated as serious enough to cancel a linked credit card (doc_0178). The corpus also shows the vocabulary of "breach" stretched to cover non-hacking exposure: Australian coverage of TikTok's tracking pixel, which scraped site visitors' names, emails, and phone numbers before consent was given, was branded a "mass breach of privacy" by a senator — a data-handling violation rather than an intrusion, but framed with the same breach language (doc_0189).

## Key Characteristics

- **Unauthorized access or exposure, not just data collection** — a breach denotes information reaching parties (or the open web) it was never meant to reach, whether via hacking (doc_0334, doc_0178) or unintentional exposure of insecure infrastructure (doc_0334's DICOM item).
- **Initial disclosures tend to understate scope** — 23andMe first quantified only 0.1% of customers as affected before acknowledging the wider group whose data was exposed (doc_0334).
- **Consequences reach beyond the breached company** — Gellar's response to her son's Roblox account being hacked was to cancel a family credit card, showing breach fallout propagating into unrelated financial accounts (doc_0178).
- **The term is applied loosely** — commentary uses "breach" both for classic hacking incidents (23andMe, Roblox) and for non-consensual data collection practices (TikTok's pixel), even though the latter is a policy/consent violation rather than an intrusion (doc_0189).

## Background (external)

More broadly (outside this corpus), a data breach is any security incident in which unauthorized parties access sensitive, confidential, or protected information (IBM, "What Is a Data Breach?", accessed 2026-09-02, https://www.ibm.com/topics/data-breach).

# CCPA To CPPA: The Regulatory Lineage Behind The ADMT Rules

The CPPA's bid to tackle AI follows the introduction of GDPR-inspired privacy rules back in 2019, with the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) coming into effect in early 2020. Since then the Agency has been pushing to go further, and in fall 2020 a ballot measure secured backing from state residents to reinforce and redefine parts of the privacy law. The new measures laid out in draft to address automated decisionmaking are part of that effort — so the ADMT rules are an implementation of an existing statute, not a new law.

"The proposed regulations would implement consumers' right to opt out of, and access information about, businesses' uses of ADMT, as provided for by the [CCPA]," the CPPA wrote in a press release. "The Agency Board will provide feedback on these proposed regulations at the December 8, 2023, board meeting, and the Agency expects to begin formal rulemaking next year."

In parallel, the regulator is considering draft risk assessment requirements intended to work in tandem with the planned ADMT rules: "Together, these proposed frameworks can provide consumers with control over their personal information while ensuring that automated decisionmaking technologies, including those made from artificial intelligence, are used with privacy in mind and in design," it suggests. # Layoffs

## Definition

Layoffs are the employer-initiated, batch workforce cuts the corpus tracks through 2023's "techwide reckoning" — TechCrunch's running tally puts total tech-industry job losses at more than 240,000 for the year, driven by companies pivoting "from a growth mindset to one based on efficiency" (doc_0049).

## Context

Across the corpus, 2023 is depicted as a "techwide reckoning" year: TechCrunch's running tracker put total tech-industry job losses at more than 240,000 for the year, already 50% above 2022 and still climbing, with cuts driven by the biggest names in tech — Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Yahoo, Meta and Zoom — as well as startups across many sectors (doc_0049).
The phenomenon recurs across very different company situations: a cybersecurity startup that went public but "failed to gain traction" and later shuttered outright, laying off its remaining staff (IronNet, doc_0011); a browser maker cutting 9% of its workforce across departments (Brave Software, doc_0043); a music-streaming giant cutting roughly 1,500 jobs (17% of its workforce) in its third layoff round of the year while its CEO framed the move as "right-sizing" for "productive and efficient" operations (Spotify, doc_0334); and a logistics startup cutting about 20% of its staff (roughly 600 people) under its founder, who returned as CEO after ousting his "hand-picked successor" over alleged overspending (Flexport, doc_0536, doc_0537).
Layoffs also follow directly from an acquired or platform company's takeover events: X's (formerly Twitter's) 2022 change of ownership "saw major layoffs, including in content moderation and human rights," which the corpus ties to the platform's later inability to respond to disinformation reports (doc_0024).
In the video-game industry specifically, layoffs are described as one of three interlocking forces — alongside consolidation and unionization — reshaping the sector: an estimated 9,000-plus video-game jobs were lost in 2023 versus roughly 1,000 in 2022, with layoffs concentrated at recently acquired studios (doc_0050).

## Key Characteristics

- **Batch, employer-driven terminations** — layoffs affect many employees at once (e.g., Brave's 9%, Spotify's 17%, Flexport's 20%), distinguishing them from case-by-case firings (doc_0043, doc_0334, doc_0537).
- **Framed as cost/efficiency correction** — companies in the corpus consistently attribute layoffs to macroeconomic pressure and a shift "from a growth mindset to one based on efficiency," rather than to sectoral collapse (doc_0049).
- **Can accompany full shutdown** — the most severe outcome pairs layoffs with the company ceasing operations entirely, as with IronNet, which "has shuttered and laid off its remaining staff following its collapse" (doc_0011).
- **Recurrent, not one-time** — several companies underwent multiple rounds within the same year (Spotify's third round by December 2023; Flexport cutting 20% in January with "more layoffs expected soon" by October) (doc_0334, doc_0536).
- **Concentrated post-acquisition** — layoffs and closures are described as "the most extreme negative outcomes for an acquired indie studio," recurring after ownership changes (video games) or leadership takeovers (X) (doc_0050, doc_0024).
- **Aggregate scale tracked industry-wide** — outlets maintain running trackers (TechCrunch's tech-layoffs list, Layoffs.fyi, layoffstracker.com) that quantify the year's cuts across sectors (doc_0049, doc_0050).

# Foundation Model

## Definition

A foundation model is a large AI model — trained by a small set of well-resourced providers — that sits at the base of the generative-AI stack and is adapted or built upon by other tools and applications, rather than being the end product itself.

## Context

In the corpus the term surfaces in two distinct settings: market structure and government regulation. In a TechCrunch survey of venture capitalists on the emerging LLM stack, Glasswing Ventures' Rick Grinnell divides the generative-AI landscape into four layers — foundation model providers, middle-tier companies, end-market/top-layer applications, and full-stack vertical companies — with foundation models sitting at the base layer that middle-layer tooling and top-layer applications are built on top of. He names Alphabet/Google's Bard, Microsoft/OpenAI's GPT-4, and Anthropic's Claude as examples of this foundational layer. Separately, in coverage of the Biden Administration's AI executive order, "foundation model" is the regulatory unit the order targets: it directs new reporting standards specifically for developers whose foundation models might affect national or economic security.

## Key Characteristics

- **Base-layer position** — foundation models sit beneath the middle tier (fine-tuning, prompt engineering, orchestration) and the application layer in the GenAI tech stack; other companies build and compete on top of them rather than replacing them.
- **Concentrated provider set** — the layer is dominated by a small number of large players (Alphabet/Google, Microsoft/OpenAI, Anthropic), whose advantages in data access, talent, and compute are expected to push this layer toward an oligopolistic structure akin to the cloud-provider market, tempered by open-source alternatives.
- **Reused across applications** — applications "blend" foundation models with in-house middle-layer tooling to build specialized, defensible products, rather than starting from scratch.
- **Trigger for regulatory reporting** — under the White House AI executive order, a company training any foundation model that poses a serious risk to national security, economic security, or public health/safety must notify the federal government when training the model and share red-team safety test results before public release.
- **High-capability threshold for regulation** — the EO's reporting duty is scoped to a computational threshold (10^26 petaflops) beyond the capacity of existing models at the time, so it targets only the next generation of the largest foundation models, not models currently on the market or built by small/independent developers.



---


# Atlassian's Critical Security Flaw Warning

Atlassian issued a warning about a critical security flaw that could result in significant data loss for its customers, TechCrunch reported on November 3, 2023.

Notably, this product was recently the target of Chinese state-sponsored hackers.

Atlassian has not yet detailed how the flaw can lead to data loss, but has urged customers to patch against the flaw immediately.



---


# Keep Labs' Repositioning From Cannabis To Medicine

Keep Labs stopped presenting its product as a cannabis device after CES took back an innovation award over exactly that framing: look at the website now and cannabis is not mentioned, and the Keep is marketed with the catch-all term "medicine." The observation comes from TechCrunch's 4 October 2023 conversation with co-founder, president and chairman Philip Wilkins about the company's journey from a preorder success story to finding an enterprise offering by partnering with Canadian healthcare providers — the writer's second conversation with him, the first having been back in 2019.

The triggering event dates to that first period. Keep Labs won an innovation award at CES 2020, and the award was later rescinded because the device was marketed as a cannabis storage device. The governing condition at the time was a policy inconsistency: in 2019, going into 2020, the trade group hosting CES had a strict but convoluted stance on cannabis products, and somehow Keep Labs won an award anyway. Eventually someone at the CTIA noticed Keep Labs' marketing and pulled the prize. This set off a firestorm, and eventually led the CTIA to soften its stance on cannabis-adjacent products — after all, cannabis is legal in Nevada, where CES is held.

The repositioning is presented as a change of vocabulary rather than of mission. The experience has had a lasting effect on Keep Labs, but "Cannabis is still there," Wilkins said, noting that the company is still on the same mission of harm reduction. "Cannabis was a great way to start a conversation because everyone wants to talk about cannabis, but no one wants to talk about getting high."



---


# CyberGhost, Best For Cross-Platform Accessibility

CyberGhost was named the best VPN for cross-platform accessibility. Specifications: 7 simultaneous connections across 7 devices; Windows, Mac, Android, iOS and Linux; Chrome and Firefox browser extensions; dedicated IP addresses available with an additional purchase; 2 free months and a 45-day money-back guarantee; $2.11/month at CyberGhost.

Cross-platform support is not always necessary, because several of the best VPN services connect to routers — connecting a VPN to your home router lets you cover unlimited devices in your household, as long as they all access the internet through that router. But if you use VPNs on the go and across several devices, being able to connect to a wide range of platforms is indispensable.

CyberGhost offers simultaneous connectivity on up to seven devices for $2.11 to $12.99 per month depending on subscription term, and supports several types of gadgets like routers, computers, smart TVs and more. It is similar to the support ExpressVPN offers, but CyberGhost provides detailed instructions on how to set up the cross-platform connections, making it a bit more user-friendly for those purposes. It also just expanded its network of servers from 91 to 100 countries, adding Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Guatemala and the Dominican Republic.

On security, CyberGhost completed an independent security audit by Deloitte earlier this year, runs a vulnerability disclosure program and provides access to a transparency report explaining requests for its data, with an updated version going live in August. It passed all of the tests, though the reviewers had trouble connecting to servers in the United Kingdom and had to run the gaming test through an Ireland-based server instead.



---


# Windscribe, Best Free VPN

Windscribe was chosen as the best free VPN because of its high security and wide range of server locations compared with other free VPNs. Signing up for the free plan with an email gets you 10GB per month of data, unlimited connections and access to more than 10 countries. Specifications: unlimited simultaneous connections and devices; Windows, Mac, Android, iOS and Linux; Chrome and Firefox browser extensions; no dedicated IP addresses; no trial and no money-back guarantee; $0 at Windscribe.

Its infrastructure is broad: over 500 servers in over 60 countries, according to the company, and it can be configured to routers, smart TVs and more on top of the usual operating systems.

On security, Windscribe does not have a recent independent security audit, but it does publish a transparency report showing it has complied with zero requests for its data, runs a vulnerability disclosure program encouraging researchers to report flaws, and offers multiple protocols for users to connect with.

It is also easy to use: setup is intuitive and it passed the geoblock, streaming and gaming tests. The paid version costs $5.75 to $9 each month depending on the plan, and includes unlimited data, access to all servers and an ad/tracker/malware blocker; alternatively, for $1 per location per month, users can build a plan tailored to the VPNs they want to access. Windscribe is still expanding its reach, having added Japan to its list of available spots.

qid: Does the Yardbarker article suggest that the New Orleans Saints' performance is poor due to their easy schedule, while The Roar | Sports Writers Blog article implies that Manchester United's poor performance is attributed to the goals scored by Jarrod Bowen and Mohammed Kudus?
context:
# Manchester United's Defeat To West Ham In December 2023

Goals from West Ham's Jarrod Bowen and Mohammed Kudus beat Manchester United on 23 December 2023, extending United's miserable run in the English Premier League, as reported by The Roar that day.

Bowen bundled home at the second attempt in the 72nd minute for his 11th league goal of the season, breaking the deadlock, and Kudus struck his fourth goal in as many games to settle matters, finishing after a defensive howler from Manchester United — a goal Kobbie Mainoo would not want to see back, and one created by an assist from Lucas Paquetá.

The result is recorded as another worrying setback for manager Erik ten Hag: United had now suffered a 13th defeat in 26 games in all competitions.



---


# Sherwood's Analysis Of Tottenham Over-Attacking After Leading

Speaking on Optus Sport after the 7 December 2023 defeat, ex-Spurs boss Tim Sherwood diagnosed the losing run as a game-management failure: the claim is that Tottenham keep trying to win a game they have already won, and the warrant is that in doing so they leave themselves open to being exploited.

His grounds start with the pattern rather than the single match: "They're quietly having a bad run, it's five without a win now. They've led in every game and I've said when they take the lead, I wouldn't say the game is over. It's not good enough."

Sherwood was careful to separate style from outcome, crediting the change under Postecoglou before faulting it: "But they've changed. The last three or four years they've been watching some dross there but it's better to watch. It's game management." He then spelled out the mechanism and the evidence from this match: "They go ahead and they're already winning the game but they try and win it again and again and leave themselves open. Jarrod Bowen was outstanding out there and you can really exploit them. They leave space and they make poor decisions on the ball and it's costing them at the moment."



---


# Tottenham's Home Defeat To West Ham, December 2023

Spurs fell to their fourth defeat in five games with a 2-1 home reverse against West Ham on 7 December 2023, and, as The Roar reported that day, they only had themselves to blame.

Ange Postecoglou's men were sitting pretty at 1-0 up thanks to an early Cristian Romero header, then missed a host of chances to extend the lead against a Hammers side who couldn't get out of their own end. Having spurned their own opportunities, Tottenham presented two gift-wrapped chances to their opponents. Their defence was nowhere to be seen as Mohammed Kudus was able to shoot, his effort deflecting off two Spurs players and into the path of Jarrod Bowen to level the scores. Then Destiny Udogie's blind backpass — short of the mark, intended for Guglielmo Vicario — allowed James Ward-Prowse an easy shot on goal; he hit the post, and the rebound fell perfectly for the midfielder to finish, silencing the stadium.



---


# Postecoglou's Response To Tottenham's Losing Run

Ange Postecoglou's response to the 7 December 2023 defeat was less damning than his captain's but still described the showing as poor: the claim is that Tottenham keep dominating games without taking advantage, and the warrant is that playing nice football can disguise how a team is going, so only winning counts as evidence of progress.

"It's another game where we've dominated a game of football but we haven't taken advantage," Postecoglou said. "I thought we were poor in both areas with our finishing and also both goals we conceded were terrible."

He then refused the consolations available to him and named the only remedy he would accept: "There's no point in feeling sorry for ourselves, looking for a cuddle anywhere. There's only one way to change our circumstances and that is to come here on Sunday and put in a performance, not just play good football but go out there and show some conviction about ourselves as a team." He tied that to a standard he says he set on arrival: "Sometimes we can disguise how we're going by playing some nice stuff but like I said from day one, that's not what I'm about. I want to win and that's why I came to this football club and that's the message. We've still got a long way to go, I've said that from the start, we're still right at the beginning what we need to create and days like today just give me further evidence and fuel of how much we need to do."



---


# Ten Hag's Defence Of Manchester United's Performance

Erik ten Hag tried to put a positive spin on the defeat to West Ham on 23 December 2023 by claiming to the BBC that his side were the better team before the first goal: the claim is that the loss came from a single lapse rather than a systemic failure, and the warrant is that United created the better chances and had recently matched the top of the league.

His grounds for the first part are the shape of the match: "I think it was a decent 72 minutes where we didn't take our chances. We should've gone in the lead but we didn't and then it was one moment of switching off."

His grounds for the second part are the previous fixture, which he uses to set the standard he says the team must reproduce: "At this moment we are not top, but we have seen last week against the top of this league we were head-to-head. We didn't score, we had the best opportunities of the game." He added: "There we defended very well for 90 minutes, that has to be always our standard like what we did there. You have to bring that to every game on the pitch."



---


# Jaguars Survive Late Saints Rally To Win 31-24 On Thursday Night Football

Jacksonville beat New Orleans 31-24 in the Week 7 "Thursday Night Football" game on Thursday, Oct. 19, 2023, surviving a late scare at the Caesars Superdome. Doug Pederson's crew improved to 5-2 and extended its winning streak to four games, while the loss dropped the Saints to 3-4.

The Jaguars controlled most of the game, building an early first-half lead and entering the fourth quarter up 24-9, at which point the Saints offense was completely out of sync — Derek Carr had just thrown a pick-six to Foye Oluokun and was struggling to connect with any key weapon other than running back Alvin Kamara. But Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars failed to put the game away, and New Orleans scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns to tie the game with less than six minutes to go, with the momentum fully shifted to the home side. Christian Kirk then broke loose for a 44-yard touchdown after an exchange of punts, retaking the lead for Jacksonville with 3:08 remaining. New Orleans nearly tied it in the final seconds: tight end Foster Moreau had a touchdown in his fingertips on third-and-goal but could not hold the catch, and a fourth-down pass to Chris Olave was broken up. The quarter-by-quarter line was Jaguars 7-10-7-7 for 31 and Saints 3-3-3-15 for 24.

Kickoff was 8:15 p.m. ET (7:15 p.m. CT), the normal start time for all of Amazon's "TNF" games in 2023; because the game was in New Orleans, in the Central time zone, local viewers saw it at 7:15 p.m. Historically the Saints had the Jaguars' number: in seven meetings between the franchises New Orleans held a 5-2 record and a four-game winning streak, and the previous meeting, in 2019, was a 13-9 Saints win in a defensive battle.



---


# Howe On Newcastle's Inconsistency And Injury Load

Eddie Howe accepted after the 3-0 defeat at Everton on 7 December 2023 that Newcastle have to do better, while attributing the inconsistency to an inability to rotate: the claim is that there are reasons behind every performance, and the warrant is that the quality of players unavailable makes it harder the longer the run goes on.

The Roar frames the pattern Howe was answering for: his side are proving one of the most inconsistent in the league, albeit with a lengthy injury list. In the previous month they had defeated Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea, and drawn at French heavyweights PSG in the Champions League, but had now lost comfortably to two cellar dwellers in Everton and Bournemouth.

"We have to do better," Howe said. "There are reasons behind every performance and we have struggled to change players. That is a big miss with the quality of players out. The longer you do it, the harder it gets. I am disappointed, a missed opportunity, we did not grab it." He also located the turning point within the match itself: "The game was there for us to win in the second half. The first half was even and we had them penned in in the second half. We conceded the first goal and it changed the momentum of the match. Frustrating and a chance missed."



---


# Manchester United's Defensive Imbalance: Ferdinand's Critique

Rio Ferdinand argued that Manchester United's European problems stem from a lack of balance in the team — they can score at will but make defensive mistakes that undo the game plan — and that the fix has to be applied over a period of games, not one or two, talkSPORT reported on 29 November 2023.

The grounds are the numbers and the pattern of the concessions. Eight points have been dropped from winning positions, and no other team has suffered a worse fate that term. United had conceded 14 goals in the Champions League group stages, a new and unwanted record for the club that could get worse when they faced Bayern in the final match, while their 12 goals scored was the fifth-highest tally of any club — so the downfall was defensive. "I think they've got to look at themselves," said Ferdinand, a 2007/08 Champions League winner with United. "You can't go into a Champions League campaign and score nine goals in three away games and have one point at the end of it. I think that shows you that there's a lack of balance in the team at the moment. Yes they can get goals and yes they are attacking at will and creating chances, many of them coming through Bruno. But I think defensively, they just made mistakes, I think the goalkeeper today has to hold his hands up and say, 'Yep, I was at fault for a couple of goals. He should do better."

The warrant is that the tactical work was sound and the errors, not the plan, cost the points — and that repeated collapses leave a psychological residue. "I think the manager will be scratching his head and thinking, 'The game plan first-half worked perfectly,' and then all of a sudden they score a goal, it changes the dynamic of the game. They were 2-0 up, 2-1, and you're thinking, 'Wow, I set the team up perfectly well, they execute it but then a mistake cost us,' and at 3-1, the same again. So I think there's a lot of question marks in the performances and the way they're going about things at the moment but balance for me is one of the key aspects that they've got to really find." He continued: "We mentioned in commentary, scars from throwing away leads, those are hard to get away, you've got to really manage games and he mentioned that himself Bruno, you've got to go out managing games correctly. They've got to do that not over one or two or three games, they've got to do that over a period of games now so they can erase those scars that they've created and they'e grown through bad results and throwing away leads, especially in Europe."



---


# Schmeichel's Criticism Of Manchester United's Lack Of Identity

Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel attacked the premise that the defeat to West Ham on 23 December 2023 could be read as a performance at all: his counter is that there was no plan to the display, so the question of whether United played well before conceding does not arise.

Schmeichel lashed the team's lack of a plan and blasted them for looking slow against the Hammers. "It was just in many ways irrelevant. There was no plan to it," he said. "West Ham got an easy win which is a little bit silly to say." He then pressed the point beyond the single match, into the team's identity: "When I look at the team, I don't know what the identity of the team is. What is the style of play, what's the plan?"

His prescription attacks the manager's framing directly by naming two concrete failures instead: "He needs to take a step back, ten Hag, and say what do I need to do with these players I have available in order to first of all stop leaking goals, because that's a problem, and secondly, score goals – how do I get the next goal? Four games without a goal, it's a long time."



---


# Jaguars-Saints First Half: Two Etienne Touchdowns And A Fake Punt Build A 17-6 Lead

Jacksonville led New Orleans 17-6 at halftime of the Oct. 19, 2023 "Thursday Night Football" game, scoring two Travis Etienne Jr. touchdowns and adding a field goal set up by a fake punt. The Jaguars received the opening kickoff at 8:15 p.m. and drove straight down the field: a 21-yard completion to Evan Engram and a 15-yard Etienne Jr. dump-off reached Saints territory (8:17 p.m.), Lawrence found Christian Kirk for 10 to reach the New Orleans 16 (8:21 p.m.), Jamal Agnew took a reverse to the two (8:22 p.m.), and Etienne Jr. barreled in from two yards out at 8:23 p.m. — 5:16 into the game — against a Saints defense that had not allowed an opening-drive touchdown since the previous season.

New Orleans wasted its early chances. The Saints avoided a three-and-out on a five-yard Carr-to-Kamara third-down completion (8:28 p.m.) and Carr rushed 10 yards for a first down across midfield (8:29 p.m.), but a Jacksonville blitz forced a throwaway on third-and-seven and rookie Blake Grupe pushed a 51-yard attempt right at 8:33 p.m. — his third miss in five kicks. On Jacksonville's first play after the miss, Paulson Adebo punched the ball out of Kirk's hands and the Saints recovered at their own 41 (8:37 p.m.), but the Jaguars forced a three-and-out (8:40 p.m.). Moments later Tevaughn Campbell ran into his own returner Agnew on a punt, forcing a muff that New Orleans recovered deep in Jacksonville territory with 3:36 left in the first quarter. A seven-yard Kamara reception gave first-and-goal at the six (8:44 p.m.), but the Saints could not convert and Grupe made a 23-yard chip shot at 8:47 p.m. for a 7-3 score with 1:26 left in the quarter, which ended after Lawrence hit Kirk for nine on third-and-three (8:52 p.m.).

Jacksonville stretched the lead early in the second quarter. Kirk took a handoff and tossed it back to Lawrence, who found Agnew for nine (8:55 p.m.); Lawrence escaped pressure for a 26-yard run, the second-longest of his career, showing no sign of knee trouble (8:57 p.m.); and Etienne Jr. took a pitch 17 yards down the sideline at 8:58 p.m. for his second touchdown of the game and his sixth in three games, making it 14-3. New Orleans repeatedly went for it and failed: an 18-yard Carr-to-Moreau completion reached the Saints' 48 (9:03 p.m.), Darious Williams batted away a third-down pass to Michael Thomas and Allen kept the offense out on fourth-and-three (9:05 p.m.), and Carr's fourth-down attempt to Chris Olave was tipped away, giving Jacksonville the ball at its own 44. The Saints defense forced a three-and-out (9:10 p.m.), Kamara ran 21 yards on the next drive's first play (9:12 p.m.), but Tre Herndon broke up a third-down pass to Olave and New Orleans punted with 7:17 left (9:15 p.m.). Another Saints three-and-out stop plus a 15-yard penalty on Antonio Johnson for running into returner Rashid Shaheed gave New Orleans the ball at the Jacksonville 46 (9:20 p.m.). Allen again went for it on fourth-and-three (9:23 p.m.) and Kamara's 17-yard catch-and-run converted (9:24 p.m.), but Carr scrambled for only three on third-and-eight before the two-minute warning (9:26 p.m.), and Grupe made a 35-yard field goal at 9:29 p.m. for 14-6.

The half ended with Jaguars trickery and a reversed interception. Completions to Kirk and Engram both ended out of bounds to stop the clock, leaving Jacksonville all three timeouts inside two minutes (9:32 p.m.). The Saints forced another punt (9:35 p.m.), but Pederson called a fake punt at 9:36 p.m. on which punter Logan Cooke hit Tim Jones for 17 yards. At 9:38 p.m. Marcus Lattimore appeared to intercept Lawrence inside the 10 with 34 seconds left, diving in front of intended receiver Agnew; on review at 9:41 p.m. officials ruled the ball hit the ground, making it an incomplete pass on fourth down, and Brandon McManus converted the field goal at 9:42 p.m. with 32 seconds left for a 17-6 lead. Carr fumbled on the final play, recovered by one of his own linemen, and New Orleans left the field to boos (9:44 p.m.).



---


# Jaguars-Saints Second Half: A Tied Game Broken By Christian Kirk's 44-Yard Score

New Orleans erased a 17-6 halftime deficit to tie the Oct. 19, 2023 "Thursday Night Football" game at 24, only for Christian Kirk's 44-yard touchdown to give Jacksonville a 31-24 win. The Saints received to start the half at 9:58 p.m., in desperate need of offense. They went for it on fourth down after coming up half a yard short on third — their third-down record was one-for-nine at that point (10:00 p.m.) — and Alvin Kamara turned the half-yard need into a 17-yard gain (10:01 p.m.). Taysom Hill, barely used to that point, kept a read option for six yards down to the Jacksonville 23 (10:02 p.m.), but a second-down penalty pushed New Orleans back 10 yards and Blake Grupe settled for a 42-yard field goal at 10:06 p.m., his third make in four attempts, cutting the lead to 17-9.

Jacksonville then extended it through a Saints turnover. At 10:12 p.m. the Jaguars called a draw on third-and-six from their own 29 and Travis Etienne Jr. came up less than a yard short; Pederson punted rather than go for it. At 10:17 p.m. Carr forced a third-down throw that was deflected into the air and into the arms of Jaguars linebacker Foye Oluokun, who sprinted the length of the field and dove for the pylon — a pick-six for a 24-9 lead. Carr then completed six straight passes to move swiftly into Jacksonville territory (10:17 p.m.). On the Saints' best, up-tempo drive (10:25 p.m.), Dennis Allen again went for it on fourth down and Kamara moved the chains to the Jaguars' nine (10:26 p.m.); Hill picked up gains of one and five (10:31 p.m.); a late hit on Foster Moreau by Rayshawn Jenkins moved New Orleans to the two (10:32 p.m.); and Kamara was denied twice from two yards out as the third quarter ended 24-9, the Saints still without a touchdown but facing third-and-one.

The fourth quarter belonged to New Orleans until the very end. After Kamara was chased down short by Evan Lloyd (10:37 p.m.), Hill punched it in from a yard out behind a lead block from defensive lineman Khalen Saunders at 10:38 p.m.; Grupe's extra point doinked off the upright and in for 24-16 with 14:21 left. The Saints defense forced a Jaguars punt (10:42 p.m.) and Carr's offense went three-and-out (10:47 p.m.) after Olave appeared to pull up on the first deep ball of the night. A Paulson Adebo pass interference call gave Jacksonville an automatic first down (10:50 p.m.), but on fourth-and-inches Etienne Jr. was stopped on a read option for a turnover on downs at 10:54 p.m., setting the Saints up at their own 47 with 7:29 left. Carr hit Michael Thomas for 17 and Hill for 19 (10:56 p.m.), then found Thomas at the back of the end zone for the touchdown and lofted the two-point conversion to a wide-open Kamara to tie it 24-24 at 10:57 p.m. Jacksonville punted after three straight stops (11:03 p.m.), and the Saints punted after three plays as Carr appeared to reach for his groin scrambling on third down, staying down before walking to the sideline (11:06 p.m.). At 11:12 p.m. Kirk took a short pass from Lawrence and weaved through the defense for a 44-yard touchdown and a 31-24 lead with 3:08 to go. New Orleans reached the Jaguars' 41 by the two-minute warning on completions to Hill (18) and Kamara (nine and seven), then Kamara's 18-yard run gave a first down at the 18 (11:17 p.m.) and an Olave catch plus a Kamara run reached the six (11:19 p.m.). On third-and-goal Carr found Moreau wide open in the back left corner but the ball went off his fingertips (11:21 p.m.), and on fourth down Buster Brown covered Olave for an incompletion (11:23 p.m.). Three Lawrence kneels ended it at 11:25 p.m.



---


# Cole Palmer Stoppage-Time Penalty Vs Manchester City

Cole Palmer, who left Manchester City for Chelsea in a deal worth around $A82 million in September, showed supreme composure to fire past Ederson in the dying stages of the 4-4 draw at Stamford Bridge, scoring from the spot in the 95th minute, The Roar reported on Nov. 12, 2023.

In his post-match interview he said of penalties: "I'm not going to say I work on them, because I don't. I just trust in my natural abilities."



---


# Dennis Allen Saints Hot Seat

Yardbarker's Nov. 30, 2023 NFC hot-seat roundup named head coach Dennis Allen as the New Orleans Saints' hottest seat, concluding that he needed a playoff appearance or there could be big changes in New Orleans.

The grounds are threefold: New Orleans' 5-6 record against the league's easiest schedule was bad; running back Alvin Kamara made a concerning claim after a 24-15 loss to the Falcons that the team did not have an identity, which the piece called worse than the record; and Allen carried a 20-44 record as head coach of the Raiders and Saints. The warrant is that a weak record made worse by a favorable schedule, plus a public sign that the locker room has lost its bearings, plus a long career track record of losing, together leave only a playoff berth as a defense.

# First Half Live Updates From Manchester United 2-1 Chelsea

The first half at Old Trafford ended 1-1, with Scott McTominay putting United ahead in the 19th minute and Cole Palmer levelling in the 45th, per Sporting News' live blog of Dec. 6, 2023, which called it a hectic first half.

The visitors got the game underway. In the 3rd minute Dalot picked out Fernandes on the edge of the box, who blasted well over the bar with a first-time strike; in the 4th Sanchez made a great save to deny Hojlund the opener after he was well found by Luke Shaw. In the 7th minute United were rewarded for their bright start with a penalty as Antony was brought down by Enzo Fernandez in the box — Chris Kavanagh originally waved play on, but VAR instructed him to take a look at the monitor and the referee gave the penalty. In the 9th minute it was saved: a woeful penalty from Fernandes and an easy diving save to his right by Sanchez. In the 15th minute it had all gone a bit wild as neither side appeared to have a midfield capable of dictating the play, with Chelsea having two glorious chances but Mudryk unable to beat Onana and Fernandes making a brilliant recovery run to prevent the other attack. In the 18th minute Silva's block denied Antony the opener; he had not scored at Old Trafford since his debut.

In the 19th minute came the goal for 1-0 United, Scott McTominay finishing off a scrappy period of play for a deserved lead. In the 25th minute there was a penalty appeal for Chelsea as Sterling dropped to the floor after very minimal contact with Victor Lindelof, but neither the referee nor VAR bought his theatrics. In the 32nd minute McTominay should have had his second — Fernandes picked him out beautifully from the left but the Scotsman headed directly at Sanchez, and either side of the Chelsea goalkeeper would have given United a two-goal lead. In the 36th minute Mudryk found himself in the box on his weak foot but dragged his effort wide. In the 45th minute came the equaliser: the former City man found the bottom corner with a delicate stroke past Onana, a wonderful goal from Cole Palmer to pull level right before the break.



---


# Liverpool 3-0 Brentford Salah 200th English Goal

Liverpool beat Brentford 3-0 with Mohamed Salah continuing his remarkable Anfield scoring record with two more goals to bring up his 200th in English football, The Roar reported on Nov. 12, 2023, leaving them second, just a point behind City, with Tottenham fourth and two points adrift.

The Reds broke the deadlock after two earlier efforts were disallowed by VAR. Only Erling Haaland, on 13, had scored more in the Premier League that season than the Egypt international, who took his tally to 10 by scoring for the sixth successive home game to write another entry in the club's history books. Diogo Jota's late strike then put a quick end to questions over Liverpool's mini-stumble after the draw at Luton and the Europa League defeat in Toulouse.

# Tottenham's Premier League Record Of Failing To Win After Leading

OptaJoe recorded on 7 December 2023 that Tottenham had become the first side in Premier League history to fail to win five consecutive games despite going 1-0 up in each match, and the first to lose three consecutive home games despite going 1-0 up in each — a run the post summed up as "Spursy."

The Roar's report places that record in the table. Spurs had rebounded from three consecutive defeats with a stirring 3-3 draw at Manchester City over the weekend, but after this result they sat outside the Champions League qualification spots in fifth place, level with Manchester United.

# NFL Week 11 Power Rankings, 17-24

Sporting News' Week 11 rankings of Nov. 13, 2023 placed the New Orleans Saints 17th at 5-5 (previous week: 15), heading into a bye without knowing what to do at quarterback: Derek Carr further hurt his right shoulder and needed to be checked for a concussion, and while Jameis Winston provided a spark it was too little too late at Minnesota, leaving a precarious division lead with poor quarterback play overall. The Los Angeles Chargers were 18th at 4-5 (17), having got well offensively with Justin Herbert, Keenan Allen and Austin Ekeler against the Lions before the defense went back to crumbling against big pass plays and wilting against the run, putting the pressure right back on Brandon Staley with a trip to Green Bay next. The Indianapolis Colts were 19th at 5-5 (19), stopping their streak of scoring at least 20 points in every game during an ugly, run-heavy victory in Germany against the Patriots, though Jonathan Taylor was doing his normal things and the defense was playing well again while Gardner Minshew looked meh.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were 20th at 4-5 (23), with Baker Mayfield and the offense back on track to move the ball well after a brief midseason slump — not lighting it up, but playing smart complementary football with a rebounding defense and perhaps a long-term quarterback answer. The New York Jets were 21st at 4-5 (18): Aaron Rodgers could not come back soon enough and a December miracle might be too late after two straight key losses to the Chargers and Raiders, with Zach Wilson always capping the potential of a talented offense that keeps making mistakes, and back-to-back division games against the Bills and Dolphins possibly deciding their season.

The Denver Broncos were 22nd at 4-5 (24), having sandwiched their Week 9 bye with upsets over the Chiefs and Bills, with the offense hitting a balanced groove under Russell Wilson and the defense making a lot more plays. The Washington Commanders were 23rd at 4-5 (21), pleased with Sam Howell and an offense showing more fight with additional weapons and better all-around running backs, but with a reeling defense and pass protection that remained un-winnable assets. The Atlanta Falcons were 24th at 4-5 (20), forced into another quarterback change because of injury; they found a few more offensive answers but that position still made things an overall mess, and the defense did not seem well prepared for different styles of offense.



---


# PSG 2-1 Nantes In Ligue 1

Randal Kolo Muani's late goal gave Paris Saint-Germain a 2-1 win over Nantes on Dec. 9, 2023, their eighth consecutive Ligue 1 win, extending their lead at the top to six points.

Bradley Barcola opened the scoring in the 41st minute, finding space in the six-yard box after a solo run from the left. Mostafa Mohamed equalised for the visitors in the 55th minute from a corner, heading home from close range. Kolo Muani restored the lead seven minutes from time by capitalising on a rebound after a save by the visitors' keeper following a set piece. PSG moved to 36 points, six clear of Monaco, who beat Rennes 2-1; third-placed Nice were on 29 points and would host Reims on the Sunday.



---


# Pochettino Reaction To Chelsea City Draw

Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino said after the 4-4 draw with Manchester City that he was proud and happy and that the players never gave up, The Roar reported on Nov. 12, 2023.

"That is why we always say the Premier League is the best in the world. We want to do something special here and this is how we need to play. We scored four goals against the best team in the world. It's good to go into the international break like this," he said. "The approach of the game was good. We were brave. That is the idea of football. I am so proud and happy. The players never gave up. The reaction of the players was amazing." Pochettino struggled to stay composed during the game and apologised for his behaviour: "Maybe I crossed the limit because I was emotional on the touchline. I want to apologise to everyone and the referee. It's trying to help and encourage the players to keep going. We faced an amazing team."



---


# Jaguars-Saints Pregame: Jamaal Williams Activated, Saints Tackles Out

Before the Oct. 19, 2023 Jaguars-Saints "Thursday Night Football" game, the headline roster news was that New Orleans activated running back Jamaal Williams off injured reserve and expected him to play, per Adam Schefter at 6:52 p.m.; Williams had not played since Week 2 after a hamstring injury. At 7:56 p.m. the live blog noted that Williams' return marked the first time all season that both he and Alvin Kamara were in the Saints backfield, since Kamara had missed the first three games of the season due to a suspension.

The inactives, posted at 7:19 p.m., showed Demario Davis notably active for the Saints — a boost to New Orleans' defense — but both starting tackles out. Trevor Lawrence was officially active for Jacksonville.

On records, the blog noted at 7:43 p.m. that the Jaguars entered Week 7 with a perfect 2-0 mark as the away team, while the Saints were 1-1 at home at the Caesars Superdome.



---


# Preview Of Chelsea's December 2023 Visit To Old Trafford

Manchester United would love a repeat of the previous season's 4-1 home win over Chelsea when the Blues visited Old Trafford that Wednesday, per Sporting News on Dec. 5, 2023.

The pressure on United had grown again following their lacklustre 1-0 defeat at Newcastle on the Saturday, and another setback against a Chelsea side — who beat Brighton & Hove Albion 3-2 the following day — would worsen the misery around Old Trafford.

Sporting News framed the meeting as one between two heavyweights of world football: United and Chelsea are two of only seven teams to have won the modern Premier League, and are only behind Liverpool when it comes to English success with European trophies. Chelsea's recent record against United was poor, but they had won the Premier League twice since United last did so in the 2012/13 season and could exploit the poor form of Ten Hag's side. The article set out to look at a rivalry that stretches back decades and had been sharply in focus over recent years.



---


# Aaron Glenn Lions Hot Seat

Yardbarker's Nov. 30, 2023 NFC hot-seat roundup named defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn as the Detroit Lions' hottest seat, on the claim that his unit's poor scoring defense had become a pattern rather than a blip.

The grounds are that the Lions finished near the bottom of the NFL in points against — 31st and 28th — the past two seasons and were on pace to do so again for the third time in as many years under Glenn, at 24th and 23.5 points allowed. Furthermore, the unit had regressed in 2023, with opponents averaging 29 points per game since Week 7, a five-game stretch. The warrant is that three straight years of bottom-tier scoring defense, worsening rather than improving, is what puts a coordinator's job at risk.



---


# Ten Hag Rejects The Crisis Framing Of Manchester United's Season

Asked about a potential crisis at Manchester United after the Chelsea win, Erik ten Hag rejected the premise outright: "Crisis? Not for us. We keep calm. We know where we have to build. We are going in the right direction. This team is capable to be successful," per Sporting News on Dec. 6, 2023.

The premise he attacks is that United's results amount to a crisis rather than a build. The immediate evidence he could point to is that United were successful that night thanks to McTominay; Ten Hag explained how his midfielder had managed to become more involved in an attacking sense that season: "He has a very good smell when to arrive and a very good finish."

He did not claim the performance was flawless, which qualifies the rebuttal rather than abandoning it: "It is not a frustration, in the end, we won but we could have made our lives much easier. We started very good, proactive, brave, we created a lot of chances in that moment, we could have gone up with two or three goals."



---


# Premier League Standings And Other Results November 2023

Manchester City led the Premier League table on 28 points, with Liverpool going into second on 27, above Arsenal on goal difference, and Tottenham fourth on 26 after successive defeats, The Roar reported on Nov. 12, 2023.

Aston Villa moved to fifth, three points off the top, with a 3-1 win over Fulham at Villa Park, courtesy of an own goal from Antonee Robinson before strikes from John McGinn and Ollie Watkins. Sheffield United clawed their way off the bottom of the table with a 1-1 draw at Brighton, while Tomas Soucek grabbed a late winner as West Ham came from behind at the London Stadium to beat Nottingham Forest 3-2.



---


# Ten Hag's Rebuttal Of Carragher's "Going Backwards" Claim

Erik ten Hag disagreed with Jamie Carragher's claim that Manchester United are going backwards this season, attacking the premise directly by saying the statistics show his team has actually improved, Sky Sports reported on 28 October 2023.

Carragher's argument, made in his column in The Daily Telegraph, was that United's summer signings have led to the club becoming "stale" and that Ten Hag should now be questioned about whether he can get the best out of his squad. Ten Hag hit back at those claims in his pre-match press conference before the Manchester City derby. "In possession we have to do better, but there are reasons and I don't go into them, but everyone is seeing why. But there are also facts so I disagree [with Carragher], we are much better," he said. The premise he denies is the factual one about performance level, and the evidence he offers is pressing data: "In high ball regains, we are a top of the Premier League. In the middle [of the pitch] ball regains, we are top. The pressing is very good. So that's not the truth, what he [Carragher] is telling."

Ten Hag conceded ground on consistency without conceding the direction of travel. In a fortnight in which United had picked up three straight wins against Brentford, Sheffield United and FC Copenhagen, albeit via far from convincing performances, Christian Eriksen said United still need to find their "balance and routines" this season. Asked about those comments, Ten Hag said: "We are in the right direction. We have a way to go. I see positives but I see negatives. What Christian is referring to is we are not consistently in possession on the level where we can be. Like Arsenal away, the first 30 minutes in Bayern Munich away. We should do this on a consistent basis. We don't take the benefit in the attacking transition moments, we should be because the ability in the team can take benefit from it. We pay attention to it, we need to grow. Then games will become easier." United hosted Manchester City in a Super Sunday derby that weekend, live on Sky Sports with a 3.30pm kick-off, billed as the latest acid test of how far the side had improved from last season.



---


# Manchester United's 3-3 Draw With Galatasaray

Manchester United drew 3-3 with Galatasaray in the Champions League, once again dropping points from a winning position in a damaging result for their bid to reach the last 16, talkSPORT reported on 29 November 2023.

Goals from Alejandro Garnacho and Bruno Fernandes fired Erik ten Hag's side into a two-goal lead within 18 minutes before Chelsea loanee Hakim Ziyech struck back. Scott McTominay scored what he thought would have been a crucial third shortly after the break, but United failed to hold on: another free-kick from Ziyech caught Andre Onana off guard once again, and a strong strike from Kerem Akturkoglu levelled the scoring.

The consequences were immediate. United now have to beat Bayern Munich and hope Galatasaray draw with FC Copenhagen on the final matchday to progress, and it was the third time in the Champions League that season that they had been in a winning position and then failed to emerge victorious. The wider context is that United's domestic form had certainly shown signs of improvement in recent weeks, but that was far from the case in Europe.



---


# Manchester United's 2023/24 Champions League Elimination

Manchester United were out of Europe altogether after a limp display against Bayern at Old Trafford, where Kingsley Coman sealed a 1-0 win for Thomas Tuchel's side on the final day of Champions League group-stage play, per Sporting News on Dec. 12 and Dec. 13, 2023.

The Red Devils finished bottom of their four-team group, leaving them eliminated from Europe in their worst performance in the competition since 2005. On top of that, they set the record for most goals against in a Champions League group stage by an English club, with 15 conceded in their six games.

Their defensive record had collapsed as the season went on: from a Premier League standpoint they sat eighth in the English top flight, but their -5 goal differential was the worst of any club in the top 10.



---


# Guardiola Reaction To Chelsea City Draw

Manchester City coach Pep Guardiola said the 4-4 scoreline was a fair reflection of the game, The Roar reported on Nov. 12, 2023.

"The Premier League has quality players with the ability to drive the ball from deep. I'm happy for the result. We were close. I think it's a fair result. We were controlled enough," he said. "I always have to think about what we can do to get better. It's not going to happen that we come here and win 7-0. They are trying to rebuild. We have no complaints." He described the midfield battle as "like chess. They had Enzo, Gallagher and Caicedo. They are so dangerous. Liverpool couldn't do it. They were much better than Arsenal. It's Chelsea. They have speed, physicality and a bench. We go into the international break top of the league and I didn't expect that after the Arsenal defeat."



---


# Pre-Match Build-Up To Manchester United vs Chelsea, December 2023

Sporting News' countdown to kickoff at Old Trafford on Dec. 6, 2023 recorded the team-news surprise that Marcus Rashford started from the bench, along with Ten Hag's pre-match message about Chelsea's defending.

At 1 hour 30 mins until kickoff the blog noted Chelsea had won three of their last four Premier League away games but were without a league win at Old Trafford since 2013. At 1 hour until kickoff the team news was in: the eyebrow-raising decision from Erik ten Hag was that Marcus Rashford started from the bench, while Mauricio Pochettino started the former Man City man Cole Palmer. At 45 mins until kickoff the blog noted Raheem Sterling had failed to score in any of his 24 matches against Man United, and asked whether the night might be the ex-Liverpool and Man City player's.

At 30 mins until kickoff the warm-ups were underway at Old Trafford on a chilly night, and Ten Hag had just told MUTV that Chelsea do not "like to defend" and that United must take advantage of that. At 15 mins until kickoff the teams had headed down the tunnel at the Theatre of Dreams.



---


# Second Half Live Updates From Manchester United 2-1 Chelsea

United won the second half 1-0 and held on for a crucial three points, with McTominay's 70th-minute header the decisive goal, per Sporting News' live blog of Dec. 6, 2023.

Both sides made a change at the break in the 46th minute: Sergio Reguilon came on for Lindelof and, much to the delight of the Chelsea fans, Reece James came on for Cucurella. In the 49th minute Jackson had a glorious chance at the back post to make it 2-1 but could not keep his header down. In the 54th minute lightning did not strike twice for Garnacho, whose latest acrobatic effort went well wide. Antony's trivela was deflected for a corner in the 61st minute, and it may have been going wide. In the 62nd minute there was a penalty appeal for United when Shaw rocketed an attempt goalwards and it looked as though Colwill may have blocked it with his hand; VAR took a quick look and play continued. Antony tried one of his trademark curling efforts from the right after cutting in on his left in the 69th minute, but it was wide.

In the 70th minute came the goal for 2-1 United and McTominay's brace: a great ball to the back post by Garnacho, met by McTominay's header from inside the six-yard box, putting him in terrific goalscoring form and making him United's top scorer that season. In the 74th minute an insane recovery run and block by Reece James denied Garnacho from doubling United's lead after he was picked out superbly by Onana to kickstart a rapid counter by the hosts. In the 80th minute Garnacho so nearly made it 3-1 but his delicate finish toyed with the goalline. In the 90th minute Broja hit the post — so close to the equaliser for Chelsea — with four minutes of added time to come. At full time United could breathe a sigh of relief and hold onto a crucial three points.

# Taylor Swift's Arrowhead Stadium Appearance, September 2023

Two days after Travis Kelce's 22 September 2023 charity event, the "All Too Well" singer was spotted cheering for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end from the box seats at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri, sitting next to Kelce's mother Donna and appearing to yell "let's f***ing go" in response to Kelce's third-quarter touchdown reception.

The Chiefs beat the Chicago Bears 41-10. After the game, Kelce was seen leaving the stadium in a blue and white splatter-paint denim suit, and eagle-eyed fans were quick to believe the outfit paid homage to Swift's forthcoming album 1989 (Taylor's Version), due for re-release on 27 October. According to photos and videos posted online, the two escaped the crowd at Arrowhead in Kelce's convertible, and the football star reportedly rented out Prime Social Rooftop in Kansas City for a post-game celebration with his family, his teammates and Swift.

A witness described the party to Entertainment Tonight: "Travis bought out the restaurant for his family and team. Taylor arrived, wearing a denim dress, and was seen snacking, having some cocktails and dancing alongside Travis. The two were very affectionate with one another but kept things fun and lighthearted. Travis' teammates also showed up to the after-party, as well as his mom, Donna Kelce. The party lasted until 2 am."

# Travis Kelce Invites Taylor Swift To Arrowhead

On 21 September 2023 Travis Kelce announced on The Pat McAfee Show that he had invited Taylor Swift to watch one of his games, The Age reported on 26 September 2023.

He described the invitation in his own words: "I told her, 'I've seen you rock the stage in Arrowhead, you might have to come see me rock a stage at Arrowhead and we can see which one's a little more lit.' We'll see what happens in the near future."

The timeline then moves to the fated sighting of Swift at Arrowhead Stadium on the Monday, cheering on No. 87 with gusto.

# Britney Spears' Unconfirmed Romances With Wade Robson And Colin Farrell

Two of the romances attributed to Britney Spears in the early 2000s were never confirmed by either party. Shortly after her breakup from Justin Timberlake, Spears was rumoured to be dating Wade Robson, a dancer and choreographer who appeared in the music video for her 2009 song "(You Drive Me) Crazy"; neither Spears nor Robson confirmed the rumours.

In 2003, Spears and Colin Farrell made headlines when they were spotted holding hands at the premiere of The Recruit, sparking speculation that they were dating. Farrell explicitly denied it in an interview with Entertainment Tonight at the time, saying the two were just friends: "She's just a mate. Seriously, we just met a week ago, [we're] having a laugh." The quote was reported by People in 2003.



---


# The Taylor Swift And Travis Kelce Romance Overview

Rumours that singer Taylor Swift and Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce were dating ran for weeks and only intensified as Swift attended five Chiefs games during the season, according to CBS Sports' timeline of the rumoured romance published 12 October 2023.

The report gives the pattern of appearances. At the first game she attended the previous month, the Eras Tour singer was seen chatting with the tight end's mother, Donna Kelce, and cheering emphatically when No. 87 scored a touchdown. The week before publication she was in attendance to watch the Chiefs defeat the Denver Broncos in Week 6 on "Thursday Night Football." She was once again at Arrowhead Stadium, this time to watch the Chiefs take on another AFC West opponent, the Los Angeles Chargers.



---


# Swift And Kelce's Public Appearances Together

Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce appeared together publicly through the autumn of 2023, at his games, at her concerts, and away from both. On 22 October Swift returned to Arrowhead Stadium to watch the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Los Angeles Chargers — her fourth time attending one of Kelce's games amid ongoing reports that they were dating — and the pair seemingly confirmed the relationship there. Afterwards Chariah Gordon, the partner of Kelce's teammate Mecole Hardman Jr, posted an Instagram picture of Swift standing next to Kelce and reaching to kiss his cheek. Kelce also responded warmly when a fan shouted "Let's go Taylor's boyfriend" while he waited for an elevator, smiling slightly and pumping his fist into the air.

The couple were also photographed together away from stadiums, including a date earlier that month in New York City after their surprise appearances on the season 49 premiere of Saturday Night Live. Sources alleged to Entertainment Tonight that during that date Kelce got too close to Swift's security personnel and told her bodyguard to step aside; on his podcast Kelce explained what he had said and denied pushing anyone: "I placed my hand on the gentleman's back to let him know I was behind him. If I would have pushed him, he probably would have turned around and tased me." Kelce reciprocated the support in November by travelling to Buenos Aires, Argentina, for one of her Eras Tour shows, where Swift changed her "Karma" lyrics to "Karma is the guy on the Chiefs, coming straight home to me," laughing as fans screamed; after the show the "Style" singer was seen running into his arms and kissing him before he whisked her backstage.

# Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift Dating Rumours in 2023

Speculation that Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift were dating began in July 2023, when Kelce confessed that he had tried and failed to give Swift a friendship bracelet bearing his phone number at one of her Eras Tour concerts; he later invited her on his podcast to one of his games at Arrowhead Stadium, an invitation she famously accepted on 24 September 2023, and she had attended three more of his games by 25 November 2023.

Kelce first told the bracelet story to his brother on their podcast back in July. "I was disappointed that she doesn't talk before or after her shows, because she has to save her voice for the 44 songs that she sings," he explained. "So I was a little butthurt I didn't get to hand her one of the bracelets I made for her. If you're up on Taylor Swift concerts, there are friendship bracelets and I received a bunch of them being there, but I wanted to give Taylor Swift one with my number on it."

The NFL star officially addressed the dating rumours during an episode of The Pat McAfee Show on 21 September 2023, in which he mocked his brother Jason Kelce for joking that he "100 per cent" believed his younger sibling was dating Swift. "It's hilarious how much traction this has actually gotten, right now it's like a game of telephone," Kelce said. "Where everybody's whispering in each other's ears and hearing random stuff. No one actually knows what's going on, especially when you got Jason Kelce on live television telling people just both sides - he doesn't know, it's true, this and that." He also said he remained open to pursuing a relationship with Swift, revealing that he had subtly asked whether she would attend one of his games: "I threw it out there, I threw the ball in her court. I told her, you know, I've seen you rock the stage in Arrowhead [Stadium], you might have to come see me rock the stage in Arrowhead and see which one's a little more lit. So, we'll see what happens in the near future."

# How Taylor Swift And Travis Kelce's Relationship Began

Taylor Swift, 33, revealed in her December 2023 Time interview — her first time publicly speaking about Travis Kelce — that the relationship began in July 2023, after he confessed on his podcast that he had tried and failed to give her a friendship bracelet with his phone number on it during one of her Eras Tour shows. "This all started when Travis very adorably put me on blast on his podcast, which I thought was metal as hell," the "Bad Blood" singer explained. "We started hanging out right after that. So we actually had a significant amount of time that no one knew, which I'm grateful for, because we got to get to know each other."

She also corrected the widely held assumption about her first appearance at Arrowhead Stadium in September: by then the two were already a couple. "By the time I went to that first game, we were a couple. I think some people think that they saw our first date at that game? We would never be psychotic enough to hard launch a first date," she said. The "All Too Well" singer had been romantically linked to the tight end since that summer, when he first confessed to the attempt to pass her his number.



---


# Taylor Swift's Subsequent NFL Appearances And SNL Cameo

After her first Chiefs game, Taylor Swift kept appearing at Kansas City fixtures and made a Saturday Night Live cameo with Travis Kelce, according to CBS Sports' timeline published 12 October 2023.

On 1 October she went to her second consecutive Chiefs game, against the Jets — who, the timeline notes, technically play in New Jersey — showing up with famous friends Blake Lively, Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman after a week of reports that she would attend; the Chiefs won 23-20. On 12 October, one day after her movie premiere, Swift was in the house for the Chiefs' "Thursday Night Football" divisional matchup against the Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium, where she has performed herself and attended a game before; according to Al Michaels the game would have minimal Swift coverage, though there had already been a mention of the superstar.

On 15 October the two were spotted out in New York City together and then made a surprise appearance on "Saturday Night Live," with Kelce appearing in a skit about how much coverage Swift was getting during games while the singer introduced the musical act of the night, Ice Spice. On 22 October Swift attended her fifth Chiefs game, having now attended games broadcast across all five networks — CBS, NBC, Fox, ESPN and Amazon — watching the Chiefs face the Chargers on CBS in a Chiefs sweatshirt, seated next to Patrick Mahomes' wife, Brittany.



---


# Taylor Swift's First Chiefs Game Appearance On 24 September 2023

Taylor Swift took Travis Kelce up on his offer and attended the Chiefs' Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears on 24 September 2023, according to CBS Sports' timeline published 12 October 2023.

Swift was dressed on theme and watched intently, cheering and even chest bumping someone during big plays; she was especially thrilled to see Kelce get in the end zone on a three-yard catch that put the Chiefs up 41-0, and Kansas City went on to win 41-10 to improve to 2-1. She sat next to Donna Kelce in the box, the two seen talking and laughing as the game went along.

The postgame press conference seemed more about Swift and Kelce than about the actual game, with the media wanting any insight into the relationship and how Swift ended up at Arrowhead. "He told me at the last minute," Patrick Mahomes said when asked if he knew Swift was coming. "There's some things with Trav where he kind of just says it and you don't know if it's true or not. He says it so calmly. ... Friday he was like, 'Yeah, I think she's coming to the game this weekend,' and then moved about his business." Head coach Andy Reid, asked about his star tight end's supposed relationship, quipped, "I set them up."

Afterwards the two were photographed together for the first time, walking side by side, Kelce fittingly wearing an outfit with "1989" in the title and Swift wearing a Chiefs zip-up; they were then spotted leaving in a convertible with the tight end driving, and Kelce reportedly rented out a restaurant for a private party with Swift and his teammates. A source told Entertainment Tonight that "Taylor Swift likes that Travis Kelce 'pursued her' and the two are having a 'great time getting to know each other,'" adding that "'Taylor wants a guy that's into his career, does his own thing, but is also supportive and understands her,'" and "'Travis fits those qualities.'"

# Taylor Swift's Arrowhead Appearance And Its Easter Eggs

At Arrowhead Stadium, the 12-time Grammy winner appeared to shout "let's f—ing go" after Travis Kelce scored a touchdown before chest-bumping other Chiefs fans, and fans then found a string of apparent Easter eggs around the visit, The Age reported on 26 September 2023.

Because Swift is known for being an Eagles fan — she is originally from Pennsylvania and even references the team in Gold Rush — her outward support for Kelce's team seemed extra telling. Swifties were immediately on high alert, with some capturing Swift and Kelce leaving the stadium together. Extra observant fans noted that Kelce's blue and white post-game outfit was supposedly labelled the "1989 bedroom painting set", perhaps an intentional reference to Swift's 2014 album, which she was due to re-release in October; the paper suggests Swift's penchant for Easter eggs must be rubbing off on the tight end. They were also spotted in a "getaway car" together outside the stadium, potentially a nod to her 2017 track.

None of this actually confirms Swift and Kelce are dating, the piece notes. But regardless of whether it is a friendship or a romantic relationship, it has sent shockwaves through two massive cultural franchises, expanding the NFL's audience into uncharted territory — a cultural pairing on par with, and perhaps even bigger than, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West.

# NFL Figures React To The Swift-Kelce Romance

Coaches, players and owners around the NFL commented publicly on the Swift-Kelce story in late September 2023, according to CBS Sports' timeline published 12 October 2023.

On 25 September, New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick — who does not always comment on situations that take place in the game — was fully ready with a sound bite: "Well I would say that Travis Kelce's had a lot of big catches in his career. This would be the biggest."

We get a lot of eye balls. She blew it off the charts. It is amazing. It makes you smile. But it just shows the depth of her following, especially with her core constituency. We all, I think, felt the same way when she's sitting up there with [Travis Kelce's] mom and she's going nuts when he's playing and those hearts are popping out everywhere. How do you not get that? That's called images right there."

# Travis Kelce's "Vigilante S***" Friendship Bracelet

Fans spotted Travis Kelce wearing a beaded friendship bracelet reading "Vigilante S***" — a reference to Taylor Swift's song from her 2022 album Midnights — in a photo taken at the Kelce Car Jam charity event on Friday 22 September 2023, days before Swift attended his Kansas City Chiefs game. # Britney Spears And Charlie Ebersol

Britney Spears and Charlie Ebersol — known as the co-founder of Tempus Ex Machina and The Company — started dating in 2014 and broke up officially in June 2015, after eight months together. Their relationship was fairly low profile.

Spears had previously explained what drew her to Ebersol, telling People at the time: "There was something about him that made me feel really peaceful and at ease. And he was really hot, too. Adorably hot."



---


# Donna Kelce At The 2023 Chiefs-Jets Game

On the New Heights podcast, Travis and Jason Kelce said the person most delighted by the gathering of musicians, actors and athletes at the 1 October 2023 Chiefs-Jets game was their mother, Donna Kelce — "Mama Kelce" — who travelled from Philadelphia to New Jersey to watch both her sons play football on the same day. I appreciate you always trying to make it to both of our games.'" # The Swift-Kelce Dating Rumours Going Public In September 2023

The Swift-Kelce dating rumours moved into public commentary in mid-September 2023, according to CBS Sports' timeline published 12 October 2023.

On 14 September, Jason Kelce — who is very close with his brother — was asked whether rumours of the two hanging out were true; he did not confirm them, but he also did not deny them. On 17 September the rumours began to pick up, and a lot of people, commentators included, started making Swift references around Kelce. When the tight end caught a touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes, CBS Sports' Ian Eagle said, "Kelce finds a blank space for the score." The timeline notes this was only the start of many, many Swift lyrics being referenced during NFL games.

# Travis Kelce's First Contact Attempt And The Eras Tour Bracelet

The first link between Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce was established in 2016 when Kelce played "Kiss, Marry, Kill" on AfterBuzz TV and said he would kiss Swift, and the first real contact attempt came in July 2023, when he tried and failed to give her a friendship bracelet with his number on it at her Eras Tour concert in Kansas City, The Age reported on 26 September 2023.

In the 2016 game Kelce — who helped bring his team to Super Bowl victory in both 2020 and 2023 — was given the options of Swift, Katy Perry and Ariana Grande, and said he would ultimately kill Grande, marry Perry and kiss Swift. That was about six years earlier, but it more recently set tongues wagging as fans wondered how long the plan for them to meet had been in the works.

Seven years on, things started to heat up: in July, speaking on the podcast he shares with his brother, New Heights, Kelce said he intended to give Swift a friendship bracelet with his number on it during her Eras Tour concert in Kansas City. The bracelet never made it to her wrist, nor his digits to her phone. "I was disappointed that she doesn't talk before or after her shows because she has to save her voice for the 44 songs she sings," he said. "She doesn't meet anybody, or at least she didn't want to meet me, so I took it personal[sic]." At that point any attraction seemed one-sided, but Kelce, exhibiting the tenacity typical of a professional sportsman, remained determined to get her attention — and the Kelce brothers could not stop talking about Swift on the podcast, her name popping up everywhere, including during conversations about facial hair.

# Britney Spears And Justin Timberlake's Relationship

Britney Spears' first highly public relationship was with Justin Timberlake, her co-star from the Mickey Mouse Club. The pair made many appearances together while dating, including the moment — described by The Independent as iconic — when they wore matching all-denim outfits to the American Music Awards in 2001.

They broke up in 2002, shortly after Timberlake and his boy band NSYNC released their hit "Cry Me a River." The song's music video, which featured a woman with blonde hair, sparked rumours that the couple had split because Spears had allegedly cheated on him.
