# Trump Tower Fifth Avenue Penthouse Valuation Dispute

Among the allegations in the New York case was that Trump claimed his Trump Tower apartment in Manhattan — a three-storey penthouse replete with gold-plated fixtures — was nearly three times its actual size, and valued the property at $327 million; no apartment in New York City has ever sold for close to that amount, Attorney General Letitia James said. The Age's comparison in November 2023 listed Trump's 2021 valuation at $US131.3 million and Bloomberg's 2023 valuation at $US40 million, with no current New York estimate available.

The size inflation is documented over a specific window: between 2011 and 2016, Trump valued the apartment on the basis of it being 30,000 square feet (2,787 square metres), almost triple its actual measurement of 10,996 square feet, and because of this New York State arrived at a valuation about a third of Trump's in those years. Space inflation was not the only issue: between 2014 and 2015 Trump increased the apartment's value to $US327 million from $US200 million, which the prosecution argues was to mask a drop in the value of another of his properties. "A discrepancy of this order of magnitude, by a real estate developer sizing up his own living space of decades, can only be considered fraud," Judge Arthur Engoron wrote in his September ruling.

Bloomberg values the property using recent Trump Tower sales and those of comparable Manhattan penthouses. While some splashy residences in much newer Billionaires Row buildings have listed for well in excess of $US100 million, they typically boast higher ceilings, more up-to-date finishes, contemporary layouts, outdoor space and better views. A better comparison, the report says, would be a 9,450-square-foot penthouse in Olympic Tower, five blocks south on Fifth Avenue, on and off the market for $US35 million since 2016; or Carl Icahn's 14,000-square-foot penthouse at Museum Tower on West 53rd Street, listed for $US35 million in 2019 before he attempted to split and sell it as two apartments, both eventually delisted.

# Trump Net Worth Valuation Dispute at Trial

Thousands of pages of exhibits detailing the performance of Donald Trump's assets, made available during the New York fraud trial, have provided a deeper look into his fortune. His 2021 statement of financial condition, filed as part of the lawsuit, pegged his net worth at $US4.5 billion. Bloomberg's calculation has consistently been below Trump's figures; at the same time, Bloomberg measured the value of some Trump properties higher than what New York state claims.

Trump took the stand and testified that the properties whose values he is accused of inflating were actually undervalued, based on the premium his "brand" adds. He also said that banks did not rely on his statements of financial condition when weighing loans: "They just weren't a very important element in banks' decision-making process," Trump told the court. # Engoron Summary Judgment That Trump Committed Fraud

A judge ruled on Tuesday 26 September 2023 that Donald Trump committed fraud for years while building the real estate empire that catapulted him to fame and the White House. Judge Arthur Engoron, ruling in a civil lawsuit brought by New York's attorney general, found that the former president and his company deceived banks, insurers and others by massively overvaluing his assets and exaggerating his net worth on paperwork used in making deals and securing financing.

As punishment, Engoron ordered that some of Trump's business licences be rescinded, and said he would continue to have an independent monitor oversee the Trump Organization's operations. A Trump spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling, and Trump has long insisted he did nothing wrong.

Fortune described the decision, which came days before the start of a non-jury trial in Attorney General Letitia James' lawsuit, as the strongest repudiation yet of Trump's carefully coiffed image as a wealthy and shrewd real estate mogul turned political powerhouse.

Letitia James, a Democrat, sued Trump and the Trump Organization a year before this September 2023 ruling, alleging a pattern of duplicity that she dubbed "the art of the steal" — a twist on the title of Trump's 1987 business memoir "The Art of the Deal."

The lawsuit accused Trump and his company of routinely inflating the value of assets like skyscrapers, golf courses and his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, padding his bottom line by billions.

# Trump Park Avenue Rent-Stabilised Unit Valuations

Trump Park Avenue, the residential condo tower on Manhattan's Upper East Side formerly known as the Hotel Delmonico, is not one of Trump's best-known buildings, but according to the prosecution it has been the source of some significant asset inflations. Trump's 2021 valuation was $US90.9 million, Bloomberg's 2023 valuation $US86.4 million, and New York's 2021 valuation $US80 million.

The dispute centres on rent-stabilised units. The building's value to Trump mostly stems from unsold condo units owned by the Trump Organisation and rented out, a varying number of which have been rent-stabilised, meaning tenants pay below market rates; such apartments are typically valued at a discount because tenants can stay indefinitely, sometimes even passing them on to children. In 2010, 12 rent-stabilised apartments owned by Trump were valued at an average of $US62,500 each in an appraisal provided by a real estate company; the following year Trump valued them at $US4.1 million each, more than 65 times greater, and has continued to value stabilised apartments in the building at market rates, including in his 2021 statement of financial condition. Rent-stabilised units "with a positive cash flow are often valued at 15-25 cents a dollar of the open market value, versus single digits for negative cash flow," said Jonathan Miller, president of appraiser Miller Samuel.

Trump's optimism was shown to be at least partially justified: by 2021, only five of the 12 apartments remained rent stabilised. The prosecution also claims two additional non-stabilised apartments in the building were overvalued because Trump ignored an option his daughter, Ivanka Trump, had to buy them at a price lower than the market value he used. The Age also records an assessment of the brand effect on price generally: "There would be a Trump premium because the person that would want that property is likely to be a Trump supporter," Eli Beracha said, though it is also likely that the association with Trump would turn off some buyers.

# Mar-a-Lago Valuation Dispute

Mar-a-Lago is the sharpest of the valuation disputes: Trump valued the Palm Beach estate as high as $739 million — more than 10 times a more reasonable estimate of its worth, Fortune reported in September 2023 — on the idea that the property could be developed for residential use, when deed terms prohibit that, Attorney General Letitia James said. Judge Arthur Engoron's finding is that Trump's conduct went beyond boasting into legal violation: beyond mere bragging about his riches, Trump, his company and key executives repeatedly lied about them on his annual financial statements, reaping rewards such as favourable loan terms and lower insurance premiums.

# Fraud

## Definition

Fraud, in the corpus's usage, is the criminal or civil charge of knowingly deceiving others — misrepresenting facts, misappropriating funds, or overstating value — for financial gain, and it recurs across the corpus as the central charge in several 2023 prosecutions rather than a single incident.

## Context

The clearest instance is Sam Bankman-Fried's federal trial: he faced seven counts of fraud and conspiracy for his role at collapsed crypto exchange FTX, including wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering and to misuse customer funds, and was ultimately found guilty on all seven counts including wire fraud.
The Securities and Exchange Commission's civil allegation sharpened the charge's scope, framing FTX as a fraud "from the start" with a "multi-billion-dollar deficiency caused by [Bankman-Fried's] own misappropriation of customer funds," and U.S. Attorney Damian Williams called the alleged scheme "one of the biggest financial frauds in American history."
Fraud also appears outside crypto: Judge Arthur Engoron ruled in a civil suit brought by New York Attorney General Letitia James that Donald Trump "defrauded banks with 'fantasy'" by deceiving banks and insurers through years of overvaluing his assets and exaggerating his net worth to secure financing — a civil, not criminal, fraud finding that led to rescinded business licenses and continued independent monitoring rather than jail exposure.
A related but distinct offense sits alongside these cases: Binance and CEO Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty not to fraud but to anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations, paying $4.3 billion to resolve the charges — the corpus treats this as adjacent misconduct in the same 2023 wave of crypto-industry legal reckonings, but the DOJ's own framing (failing to maintain an anti-money-laundering program, not deceiving victims for gain) keeps it conceptually separate from fraud proper.

## Key Characteristics

- **Deception for gain** — the common thread across cases is knowingly misrepresenting facts (asset values, fund safety, company solvency) to obtain money or credit, as in Bankman-Fried's alleged misappropriation of FTX customer funds and Trump's overvalued asset filings.
- **Criminal and civil tracks both exist** — Bankman-Fried faced criminal wire-fraud and conspiracy counts with prison exposure, while Trump faced a civil fraud finding from Engoron with business-related penalties, not incarceration risk.
- **Often bundled with conspiracy or related charges** — Bankman-Fried's indictment paired substantive fraud counts with conspiracy counts (to commit money laundering, to misuse customer funds) rather than resting on fraud alone.
- **Distinct from anti-money-laundering violations** — Binance/Zhao's guilty plea was for AML program failures and sanctions violations, not for defrauding customers, illustrating that not all crypto-industry 2023 prosecutions in the corpus were fraud cases even though they are often discussed together.

# Gen Z: Definition And Formative Events

Gen Z, as characterized in this account, is the cohort aged 11 to 26 as of October 2023 and the first fully digital native generation — the feature that discriminates it from every earlier cohort is not the scale of the history it has lived through but that it has been plugged into the world through the internet from such a young age. Social media posts are its lingua franca, and the "disturbing images" warning is one it is used to encountering there.

The formative events listed are dense. This generation has already lived through a once-per-century pandemic; the Jan. 6 insurrection, an event unseen for centuries in American politics, when armed right-wing extremists stormed the Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021 following the election defeat of former President Donald Trump; the first major European ground war since World War II, in Ukraine; and market crashes in 2008 and 2020 that recall the Great Depression. Three years before the article, as Gen Z emerged into young adulthood, online videos of the murder of George Floyd shook the country in May 2020, resulting in a summer of violent Black Lives Matter protests and riots. School shootings have only increased in frequency since Columbine in 1999, with more students documenting the terror on their phones and sharing it online — one of them, the Parkland shooting of 2018, tragically created the first spokespeople of the post-millennial generation. Most recently, on Saturday, 2023-10-07, the Islamic militant group Hamas launched an unprecedented attack on Israel, resulting in the worst war the region has seen in 50 years; in three days more than 1,500 people died on both sides, and graphic, difficult-to-watch videos blanketed the internet.

The boundary case the account itself raises is that every generation has lived through era-defining historical events: millennials remember the 9/11 terrorist attacks and the U.S. invasion of Iraq, and baby boomers lived through the civil rights movement and the Vietnam War. What sets Gen Z apart is the medium — experiencing it all through videos, images, and articles online, which is shaping their mental health, workplace attitudes, and financial habits in visible ways.

# The Epoch Times, The 2020 Election And Pro-Trump Coverage

In the runup to the 2020 election, The Epoch Times directed millions of dollars in advertising toward supporting President Donald Trump's campaign and published dozens of articles parroting his lies about the election, which produced huge growth in both its audience and its coffers.

That strategy drew criticism from fact-checking groups and got the outlet banned from advertising on Facebook, but it ultimately paid off, putting the once-fringe newspaper on a path that perhaps only its leader — who claims to have supernatural powers — could have foreseen. As its marketing strategy shifted, so did its content: by 2020 it had become a megaphone for the United States' most extreme right-wing stories. There was plenty to write about, since an election marred by disinformation, the bubbling culture wars and, most helpfully for a media company missioned with ending the Chinese Communist Party, a pandemic originating in China all provided endless opportunities for takes aligned with hawkish conservatives and conspiracy theorists.

The Epoch Times was also an early and aggressive promoter of election misinformation, according to the Election Integrity Partnership, a coalition of researchers that documented misinformation around the 2020 vote. That group cited the news organization as a "repeat spreader" of false and misleading voter fraud stories, as well as a major promoter of debunked conspiracy theories about Dominion voting machines and of the "Stop the Steal" movement aimed at overturning the election results. Months after the election, The Epoch Times still refused to acknowledge the results.

# Volcker's And Powell's Rate-Hiking Cycles Compared

The consumer price index rose at a peak of around 14% in 1980 before then-Fed Chair Paul Volcker's hawkish policies sent mortgage rates to 18% within a year — cooling inflation but sparking a recession, and causing a serious downturn in housing in which home sales and building levels cratered while national home prices actually remained stable. At the start of Volcker's term as Fed chair in August 1979 the median U.S. home sales price was $64,700, and even after a near doubling of mortgage rates that figure rose to $69,400 by the second quarter of 1981. A second account puts the average 30-year fixed mortgage peaking at about 18% by late 1981, and records that home sales activity plummeted from 1978 to 1982, with existing-home sales dropping 50% over that period according to the Office of Policy Development and Research.

Over the 18 months preceding October 2023, current Fed chair Jerome Powell has been following a very similar game plan, raising interest rates aggressively to quash inflation and setting the tone for the most aggressive global hiking of rates in the modern era. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate, the most common type in the U.S., soared from 3.8% in March 2022 to over 7.5% by 2023-10-06, and by the week of 2023-10-20 mortgage rates hit 8%, the highest in more than 20 years. This in turn slowed mortgage purchase applications and caused home sales to plummet, just as in the '80s; but home prices, echoing the dynamic of that era, have yet to collapse. While home sales activity levels this low had not been seen since the 2000s, the housing market more closely mimics that of the '80s, according to a report published in the week of 2023-10-20 by Fortune 500 financial services company First American.

# Millennials As The New Boomer Homebuying Cohort

One of the key reasons for the resilience of the housing market in both the early 1980s and today is demographics: "Noticeably, demographics were favorable back then, with baby boomers having entered the prime homebuying age," Jeseo Park and her Bank of America team wrote, arguing that millennials are in a similar position today. The structure of the argument is that a large generation reaching prime homebuying age supplies a floor of demand that offsets rate-driven weakness — millennials are a giant generation all collectively coming of homebuying age nearly simultaneously, just like their boomer parents in the 1980s, and as Redfin puts it they are the biggest share of the "homebuying pie," purchasing about 60% of homes bought with mortgages during the past few years.

The relation Bank of America draws from this holds over a specific range. "Some sales activity should be supported by millennials reaching the prime homebuying age, and single-family building permits have steadily held up. This can help the housing market retain some of its momentum without falling apart," Park's team wrote. They believe low inventory of existing homes for sale combined with solid home sales to millennials could help put a "floor beneath home prices" — but that does not mean there won't be some near-term pain due to higher mortgage rates.

# Totals Line Movement Drivers

The totals line can move, and Sporting News attributes that movement to four kinds of input: betting activity, injury updates, weather conditions, and other news and updates.

Betting activity is one of the most common reasons for line movement — a significant amount of money wagered on one side, either the over or the under, leads bookmakers to adjust the line to balance the action and protect themselves from potential losses. Injury updates work through the expected score: if a key player is injured or unable to play, that can influence the expected total score, leading bookmakers to adjust the line accordingly. Weather conditions matter in outdoor sports; heavy rain or snow in a football game might create expectations of a lower-scoring game, causing the line to move down. Finally, any other news that might affect team performance — changes in team strategy or recent performances — can influence totals lines.



---


# Why Moneyline Odds Change

Lines at sports betting apps change quickly for two primary reasons — public betting and new information — and sportsbooks adjust moneyline odds to stay profitable, balance their book and reflect the most current information about an event. Before setting odds oddsmakers gather extensive data, then release the finalized odds to the public; from that point a bettor can bet immediately or wait for shifts, though predicting those shifts is challenging.

The time dimension shows how an opening price drifts. Odds for the next Super Bowl champion released shortly after the previous Super Bowl are based mostly on the recently concluded season; as the new season approaches and teams make changes, the odds adjust to perceived championship chances, and as games progress the lines keep evolving with team performances.

The mechanism has five named drivers. Public betting patterns move a line because, when a significant amount of money lands on one team or participant, sportsbooks adjust the odds to balance their liability — making the price less favorable for the heavily-bet side and more favorable for the less-bet side to encourage even betting and reduce financial risk. New information matters because changes in player injuries, player substitutions or weather conditions alter the perceived outcome, and books adjust once such information becomes public. Professional bettors move lines because large wagers from sharp bettors often reflect insights or information that can influence the odds. Initial miscalculation is a fourth driver: sometimes the opening odds are perceived as offering value, and heavy betting on one side signals that the initial price was potentially "off," prompting an adjustment. Event dynamics is the fifth, applying to live betting placed while the event is in progress, where the evolving dynamics of the match lead to frequent changes.

# Sports Betting Odds

## Definition

Sports betting odds are the numbers a sportsbook posts alongside a wager to show the payout a bettor stands to win relative to their stake, and they are set by oddsmakers using computer models and analytics before being released to the public. The same underlying odds concept takes different shapes depending on the bet type — a moneyline price on who wins outright, a point spread price on a handicapped margin, and a totals (over/under) price on the combined score — and can be displayed in American, decimal, or fractional format.

## Context

In the corpus, odds are the common thread across every major bet type: moneylines, point spreads, totals, and prop bets all price outcomes with the same odds conventions, and combined-market previews such as college bowl coverage post moneyline, spread, and total odds side by side for a single game. Odds are not static — sportsbooks move them ("line movement") in response to public betting patterns, injury or roster news, and sharp/professional money, with the goal of balancing action on both sides of a bet so the book keeps its built-in profit regardless of outcome. Because different sportsbooks can carry different odds for the same event, bettors practice "line shopping" — comparing odds and lines across multiple sportsbooks before wagering to find the best price. Odds also extend beyond single games into futures and award markets, such as season-long odds on the NFL MVP race between Brock Purdy and Lamar Jackson.

## Key Characteristics

- **American odds format dominates U.S. listings** — a negative number (e.g., -110) shows the favorite and how much must be wagered to profit $100; a positive number (e.g., +250) shows the underdog and how much a $100 wager profits.
- **Three display formats carry the same price** — American, decimal (multiply the odds by the stake for total payout), and fractional (numerator = profit, denominator = stake) are alternative notations for identical odds.
- **Odds move for identifiable reasons** — sportsbooks shift a line or its odds because of lopsided public betting, new information (injuries, weather), sharp bettor action, or a perceived initial mispricing.
- **Odds differ by bet type but share the sign convention** — moneyline odds price the outright winner, point spread odds price a handicapped margin near even money, and totals odds price the over/under of a combined score; all three commonly display as American odds.
- **Line shopping exploits cross-sportsbook odds variance** — because oddsmakers and sportsbooks don't always move in lockstep, checking odds at multiple books before betting can secure a better price on the same wager.

# Point Spread Odds And Line Movement

Alongside a point spread, sportsbooks attach odds indicating the potential payout relative to the amount wagered, and those odds sit close to even because the spread itself is designed to level the playing field between the two teams. The same payout can be expressed in several formats: American (for example -110 or +110), Decimal (for example 1.91), and Fractional (for example 10/11), each a different way of stating the same potential return.

Point spread odds are not fixed once set; the shifts are commonly called "line movement." Lines move when the point spread or the odds attached to a particular bet change after sportsbooks have initially set them, and Sporting News identifies several drivers. The most common cause is an imbalance in the money being wagered on one side: if a significant majority of bettors back one team to cover, the top sports betting apps adjust the spread to make the other side more appealing and thereby balance the betting action. A second driver is unexpected events — injuries to key players, changes in team strategy, or significant weather events that might affect a game's outcome; for instance, if a star quarterback is announced as injured days before a big game, the spread might shift in favor of the opposing team. A third driver is information and public perception: when a piece of news or a prevailing sentiment about a team's increased chances of winning gains traction, it influences how people bet and leads sportsbooks to adjust their lines accordingly.



---


# Line Movement As A Signal Of Betting Value

Sporting News argues that bettors should monitor line movement before a game starts, because line moves reveal where the value in a bet lies. The claim is stated for both markets it covers: point spread odds can and do change based on a combination of actual betting patterns, unexpected events, and shifts in public perception, and savvy bettors keep a close eye on these line moves, as they can offer insights into where the value lies in a particular bet.

The grounds are how the lines are made and remade. Sportsbooks set game totals considering factors like recent performances, weather, and player status, and as new data emerges and betting trends develop, this line can shift — if many bettors choose the "over," the sportsbook might raise the total to balance the bets. The warrant joining grounds to claim is that line movements often reflect public betting sentiments and therefore offer insights to informed bettors: because a move encodes information the book has absorbed about data and about where the public money is, watching it tells the bettor something they did not otherwise have. Hence bettors must monitor any line changes before the game starts and strategize accordingly to optimize their betting success.

The argument stops short of endorsing either side of a totals bet in the abstract: neither wager holds a universal advantage, and success in over/under betting hinges on a thorough evaluation of both the set line and the competing teams.



---


# How Sportsbooks Set And Move Betting Lines

The best sportsbooks employ oddsmakers and oddsmaking services to set their lines and odds, while other sports betting apps simply copy those lines. The oddsmakers and services use computer models and algorithms that consider analytics, statistics, injury and roster news, performance, matchup data and more to develop the lines and odds. Those lines are then subject to change based on the betting public's reaction and any additional information that emerges before the game, and a book will move the line or change the odds if the public bets heavily on one side.

The governing objective is balance rather than prediction. Every sportsbook's goal is to even out the betting on both sides of every bet, because that lets the book earn the small profit built into the odds and lines without worrying about which side wins. Sportsbooks want even betting so much that they will move a line or change the odds specifically to draw more bets to the other side.

The relation that matters to a bettor is that books do not all move together. The betting is rarely the same at every sportsbook: one book may be forced to move a line or change the odds because of the money it has taken while another is not, and the lines and odds may even differ right from the jump. That divergence is what creates the chance to book a bet at improved odds or a more favorable line.

The range over which this holds is narrow and specific. When a line moves for a legitimate reason such as an injury or roster move, every sportsbook jumps on board, and it is difficult to find value; when a line moves because of betting patterns, only the sportsbook that saw that betting makes the change, and that is the opportunity. Line shopping is the tool for spotting the second kind: choose a side, shop around at online sportsbooks, compare the lines and odds, and pounce when you find one offering something different and more favorable to your viewpoint.

# The Timing Trade-Off In Rookie Of The Year Futures Betting

There is a fixed trade-off in when to bet NBA Rookie of the Year futures: the earlier you bet, the better the odds, but you bet without much information that could be key to an educated decision; conversely, if you wait for the data you need for an informed bet, the odds tighten and you see less of a return.

The mechanism is symmetric between bettor and book. When the lines are first released, the season has not started, so there are no statistics, trends or player news — the pre-season odds are so favorable precisely because even the oddsmakers lack the data to craft more specific lines. Once the season starts and you can see how the rookies are performing, you can gather the relevant data; but sportsbooks are gathering the same information and tighten the Rookie of the Year lines in response. So while you can better guess who will hoist the Wilt Chamberlain Trophy, the odds are tighter and your potential return reduced.

Stated as pros and cons: betting early gives an opportunity to find better value and betting odds that are fresh and unadjusted, but carries much higher risk because a player's performance, health and team dynamic can change through the season, and offers limited information. Waiting gives a lot more information for an informed bet and avoids betting on a player not remotely in contention, but reduces the opportunity to find value and the odds may not be as favorable. The range over which this holds is bounded by the individual: it is always important to take your risk tolerance into consideration while weighing the potential rewards, and no matter when you decide to wager, always gather as much information as possible before risking your money.

# The Three Staple NBA Bet Types: Point Spreads, Moneylines And Totals

For anyone new to NBA betting the staple wager types are point spreads, moneylines and over/unders. NBA point spreads bet on games via margins of victory or loss: if the New York Knicks are -7.5 favorites over the Miami Heat, the Knicks need to win by 8 points to win a spread bet, while the Heat can lose by up to 7 points or win outright. NBA moneylines are the simplest form of betting — you pick the winner of the game and are paid based on the odds when you finalize your bet slip, with favorites shown at negative odds such as -135 and underdogs at positive odds such as +165. NBA over/under bets, also known as totals, focus on the combined point total of the two teams, with winners and losers irrelevant: if the over/under in Knicks vs. Heat is 211.5 points, the over needs the teams to combine for 212 or more, while the under needs 211 or fewer.

Team props are also available, such as whether a team will lead at the end of a certain quarter, or an over/under on the total number of points a team will score.

The NFL is the king of sports betting, and NFL betting sites have no qualms about showcasing every possible bet type. Bettors find many prop opportunities, especially for the Super Bowl; during the regular season one of the most popular options is the "anytime touchdown scorer" bet, where you wager on a player to score a touchdown at any point in the game, and other props focus on one team or both teams.

Baseball, hockey and soccer follow the same logic on their own stat lines. MLB props focus primarily on individual players and statistical achievements such as home runs, RBI and strikeouts — an over/under for a starting pitcher's strikeouts, or the number of bases a hitter will reach. NHL sites carry the props you would expect from a major North American league, such as player assists or a certain player scoring a goal, plus shots on goal, team goals in a game, and which team will score first. In Major League Soccer, where demand has increased as the sport's popularity grows nationwide, props often focus on individual accomplishments such as scoring a goal or collecting an assist, and also include how many cards the two teams will combine to draw or a team's total number of corner kicks.

The National Basketball Association (NBA) is the top professional men's basketball league in the United States, grouped in the corpus among "the four major US pro sports leagues" alongside the NFL, MLB, and NHL, and described elsewhere as "the pinnacle of the sport" of basketball.

## Context

In the corpus the NBA appears in three overlapping roles: as a cultural institution with its own holiday tradition, as a subject of sports betting coverage, and as a point of contrast with other basketball leagues.
Its Christmas Day games date back to 1947 and are described as a tradition older than the Super Bowl; last season's slate averaged 4.27 million viewers across platforms — about 200% more than a typical regular-season game — and games are broadcast to over 200 countries in more than 50 languages.
The league is regularly set up as a rival tradition to the NFL's Thanksgiving Day games, with commentary noting the NBA "far outperforms" the NFL in global popularity even though the NFL draws more domestic viewers.

# Timing An NBA MVP Futures Bet: Early Versus Late

You can bet on the regular-season NBA MVP award well before the season starts, and the Sporting News argues the best time to do so comes down to your tolerance for risk versus reward — there is no single correct answer.

The grounds are informational. The odds are so favorable when the lines for NBA Most Valuable Player are first released because the oddsmakers, like you, have very little information to work with: they are basing their odds on past performance and expected future accomplishments, as well as the quality of the team around the top candidates for the award. The warrant is that price tracks information — while you wait for more, such as a player's performance during the regular season, the lines shift and become less favorable, because the oddsmakers are gathering information and applying new data and analytics to make their lines as accurate as possible.

The conclusion is therefore a choice rather than a rule: as a bettor you must decide which approach works best for your strategy — wager when the lines are released with little information at your disposal but the best potential return, or wait until you have more solid information to craft your MVP speculation.

# Sports Betting Terminology Glossary

CBS Sports set out the top Kentucky betting terms for new bettors on 13 October 2023, defining each bet type by what the bettor is actually wagering on and, in several cases, by a worked Kentucky example.

Against the spread means that instead of betting on an exact winner, the widely popular spread bet levels the playing field by letting you wager on how many points a team will win by: in basketball, if Kentucky is the 7.5-point favorite against Louisville then Kentucky covers by winning by 8 or more, while Louisville as the 7.5-point underdog covers by winning outright or losing by 7 or fewer. Money line is an elevated outright bet with odds adjusted to reflect a favored team and an underdog: if Kentucky is a -200 favorite against Florida you'd need to bet $200 to return $100, while Florida at +200 would return $200 on a $100 bet. An outright bet is the easiest wager to place and is perfect for horse racing, one of Kentucky's biggest sporting events — bettors choose one athlete, or thoroughbred, to win an entire event. An Over/Under has the sportsbook post an estimated total of both teams' final scores, with the bettor wagering on whether the actual final will be higher or lower: if the Over/Under for a Kentucky-Louisville basketball game is 125.5, you wager on the final total being Over 126 or Under 125. A player prop projects a player's stat at the end of a game and asks you to wager over or under that projection, with popular examples being how many touchdown passes a quarterback throws or how many three-pointers a basketball player hits; Kentucky is one of the 18 states that allows prop bets on collegiate athletes.

The remaining terms describe the market's participants and mechanics. The underdog is the team deemed less likely to win based on the odds, and a bet on one typically yields a larger return than a bet on the favorite; the favorite is deemed more likely to win, and bettors often pay a premium for backing one though they more often win outright. Consensus odds are generally defined as an average of all available betting markets, since different sportsbooks may price markets variably based on the action they've taken or their own interpretation of information. Futures markets encompass almost anything outside single-game bets — total regular-season wins, championship odds, MVP odds and more. A parlay requires two or more bets within a single wager, all of which must win: wagering $100 on a three-leg parlay at 6 to 1 odds could win $600 if all three legs win. Juice, also known as the vig or vigorish, is effectively the tax oddsmakers charge for handling a wager — if a book judges a game a virtual coinflip it may price both options at -110 to give itself a 10% rake on all the action. A push is a bet where neither the bettor nor the sportsbook wins: if an over/under for total points is set at 44 and both teams combine for exactly 44, the result is a push and the principal is returned. Live or in-game betting allows bets on several different markets in real time — in basketball, on the outcome of a quarter, individual statistics and live-updated spreads and totals.

# Over/Under Totals Bet Definition

A totals bet, commonly known as an over/under bet, is a wager on the combined score of both teams in a game: bookmakers set a predicted total score, and bettors choose whether the actual combined score will surpass it ("over") or fall short of it ("under"). Rather than picking the winner or the winning margin, totals betting asks only about the game's combined score, and it sits alongside point spreads and moneylines as a favorite option in sports betting.

The discriminating feature is that the bettor's only concern is whether the final combined score falls over or under the line set by oddsmakers — the identity of the winner is irrelevant. Sporting News illustrates with an NBA game whose total is set at 210.5 points: those who bet the "over" win if the combined score of the two teams is 211 or more, while those who bet the "under" win if the score totals 210 or less. The 0.5 ensures no chance of a tie, since teams cannot score in half-points.

The category is broader than points. Over/under bets involve wagering on whether a particular number will be over or under the figure the bookmaker set, and that number can be combined points scored in a game, total rounds in a fight, or total games in a tennis match.

context:
# Erik Ten Hag Under Pressure In December 2023

Erik ten Hag faced a demanding week in early December 2023 amid reports indicating disunity within his team, and by mid-December the pressure around the Dutch boss continued to get more palpable as Manchester United's season continued to slip away.

On Dec. 6, 2023, Sporting News reported that the United manager had faced a demanding week amid reports indicating disunity within his team, and that his players did exceptionally well to block out the noise and focus on footballing matters. Two hours before kickoff against Chelsea the live blog noted it had been a relatively busy start to the week off the pitch for Ten Hag, and that it was time to see what happened on it. Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) posted on December 5, 2023 that Erik ten Hag claimed there was not a good culture among staff and players before he joined Man United.

By Dec. 13, 2023, Sporting News framed the situation as one in which, as Manchester United's season continued to slip away, the pressure around Ten Hag continued to get more palpable.



---


# Jean-Claude Blanc and the United Chief Executive Challenge

The question The Guardian posed on 25 December 2023 is whether any chief executive can make Manchester United a best-in-class elite club again — and the candidate in frame is Jean-Claude Blanc, billed as the "Lionel Messi of business" by Nice's chief executive, Fabrice Bocquet.

Blanc's credentials are unusually broad for the role. He has an MBA from Harvard, and at 60 years old has been Juventus CEO and president, CEO at Paris Saint-Germain and at French Tennis, and the executive overseeing the Tour de France.

The boundary on those credentials is the club itself. The report argues that once Blanc, or whoever becomes Arnold's successor, is in place, it will dawn rapidly that United are a one-off hydra-headed beast of a club which is treacherously difficult to control. And there is the competitive gap: across town Manchester City have accrued six championships since United's last in 2013, and boast a commercial operation that leaves Ratcliffe's new concern light years behind.



---


# Manchester United's European Decline Since Ferguson

The Independent argued on 12 December 2023 that Manchester United's 1-0 defeat to Bayern Munich should have been a landmark low but instead felt grimly routine, because group-stage elimination has become the club's normal European outcome in the post-Ferguson era rather than an aberration.

The grounds are frequency and pattern. Manchester United, one of the grandest and richest names in this competition, have again gone out of the Champions League at the group stage; it is the third time it has happened since Sir Alex Ferguson, meaning it is their most common round of exit in that period. The night is presented as one more entry in a decade of disappointment in a competition in which this club rose to its most emotional heights — a low, but just part of that longer run.

The warrant is the gap between the occasion and the performance. These are not the sounds we are used to hearing after that Champions League theme; something does stir when the anthem is played at Old Trafford amid the lights — well, for most, that is, except the players. United should not be performing like this on what is supposed to be the classic European night at Old Trafford, and the display was a reminder that all they are going to have for some time are their memories. Having been involved in so many ludicrously chaotic matches, the biggest of all ended up being a non-event: this game never threatened to stir anything, and United never threatened at all. That, the argument runs, can now be talked about definitively, since it has been decisively ended.



---


# Erik Ten Hag's Position Under Ratcliffe

Erik ten Hag's team are treading water at precisely the wrong moment, The Guardian reported on 25 December 2023: Sir Jim Ratcliffe is taking charge of Manchester United's sporting department before making sweeping changes to the posts that will directly affect the manager.

Two lines of authority above Ten Hag are in play. Richard Arnold has left, despite officially staying until the end of the year, and into his role may come Jean-Claude Blanc, the CEO of Ratcliffe's Ineos Sport, as the man Ten Hag reports to. Ten Hag's line manager may change too, as Ratcliffe considers whether a new football director is required — a position held by John Murtough.

The report suggested an early tell of Ten Hag's standing in Ratcliffe's new empire: whether he is sounded out for his view on a prime factor in his ability to coach and manage the side to success, namely United's transfer policy.



---


# Ten Hag Rejects The Crisis Framing Of Manchester United's Season

Asked about a potential crisis at Manchester United after the Chelsea win, Erik ten Hag rejected the premise outright: "Crisis? Not for us. We keep calm. We know where we have to build. We are going in the right direction. This team is capable to be successful," per Sporting News on Dec. 6, 2023.

The premise he attacks is that United's results amount to a crisis rather than a build. The immediate evidence he could point to is that United were successful that night thanks to McTominay; Ten Hag explained how his midfielder had managed to become more involved in an attacking sense that season: "He has a very good smell when to arrive and a very good finish."

He did not claim the performance was flawless, which qualifies the rebuttal rather than abandoning it: "It is not a frustration, in the end, we won but we could have made our lives much easier. We started very good, proactive, brave, we created a lot of chances in that moment, we could have gone up with two or three goals."



---


# The Manchester United Crisis News Cycle Under Ten Hag

The Guardian's argument is that results at Manchester United no longer settle anything, because the club's crisis news cycle consumes wins as quickly as defeats: a stirring recovery against Chelsea bought Erik ten Hag only a few days' grace.

The grounds are the pattern of the week itself — rancour, rumour and recrimination, barbs in the press and barbs at the press, defeat at Newcastle followed by the Chelsea win and the startling realisation that United were three points behind Manchester City, all before Thursday. The warrant is a claim about the institution rather than the team: such is the way of things at football's most reliable content provider, and this beast must always eat, so the warm flume of goodwill would last only as long as it took for Dominic Solanke to run through on goal for Bournemouth on the Saturday afternoon, returning United to the grip of crisis and the now-familiar lexicon of surly unsourced stories about dressing room discontent. A second, related argument is that assessing any United manager requires filters: Ten Hag would of course take the blame for the early Champions League exit, and plenty of mistakes had been made, not least in the players the manager had been allowed to sign — but to be United manager is to undertake three concurrent roles.



---


# Manchester United 2023 Galatasaray Group Decider

United's match against Galatasaray on the Wednesday was not a knockout game, but in truth the scenario was not much different, The Guardian reported on Nov. 27, 2023: defeat would again end United's Champions League campaign prematurely, while a win — assuming Copenhagen lost against Bayern Munich — would put qualifying for the latter stages back in their hands.

United would face the same atmosphere as they had 30 years earlier, because the home fans knew victory would turn their subsequent trip to Denmark into a potential shootout for who goes through with Bayern, with the achievement of knocking out a club with the storied history of United only adding to the pleasure. Galatasaray had already beaten United 3-2 at Old Trafford in early October, Mauro Icardi scoring the winner.



---


# Manchester United Recent Champions League Failures

Thirty years on from Istanbul, United headed to Turkey knowing they had rarely been convincing in the Champions League in recent years, The Guardian reported on Nov. 27, 2023: a 3-1 away win against Paris Saint-Germain in the 2018-19 round of 16, after losing the home leg 2-0, was the last time they won a crunch match.

In 2020-21 they lost their final two group games and were eliminated, while back in 2015-16 Wolfsburg won the deciding group match to knock them out. United had done little learning in recent times, repeating the same failures in Europe's elite competition. It would not be a disgrace to lose against a good Galatasaray team, especially given Erik ten Hag was missing key players, but if the worst happened, everyone would need to come out of the experience stronger — regardless of the result, it should be a night of education about the demands of the Champions League.



---


# United's Shot Dominance In The Win Over Chelsea

Manchester United's December 2023 win over Chelsea felt a lot tighter than it really was: United hung on inexplicably at the end despite enjoying 28 shots and an xG tally of 4.07.

For long periods United played some of their most authentically thrilling football of the season, a doctrine of relentless attack that had Diogo Dalot flying forward from right-back even as the minutes ticked down. It was also a game that felt more chaotic than it really was — the slippery, slingy nature of the play was largely by design, with United hollowing out their midfield to throw bodies forward and Chelsea hollowing out theirs to leave men up for the breakaway. It was a game that hung on United's determination to keep allowing Chelsea counterattacks and Chelsea's determination to keep messing them up, and above all on the curious main character energy of Scott McTominay.



---


# Preview Of Chelsea's December 2023 Visit To Old Trafford

Manchester United would love a repeat of the previous season's 4-1 home win over Chelsea when the Blues visited Old Trafford that Wednesday, per Sporting News on Dec. 5, 2023.

The pressure on United had grown again following their lacklustre 1-0 defeat at Newcastle on the Saturday, and another setback against a Chelsea side — who beat Brighton & Hove Albion 3-2 the following day — would worsen the misery around Old Trafford.

Sporting News framed the meeting as one between two heavyweights of world football: United and Chelsea are two of only seven teams to have won the modern Premier League, and are only behind Liverpool when it comes to English success with European trophies. Chelsea's recent record against United was poor, but they had won the Premier League twice since United last did so in the 2012/13 season and could exploit the poor form of Ten Hag's side. The article set out to look at a rivalry that stretches back decades and had been sharply in focus over recent years.



---


# Manchester United's 2023 Champions League Group Stage Exit

Ten Hag's United compiled arguably the worst performance by any English team in a Champions League group stage in 2023, finishing bottom of their group and shipping 15 goals — more than any other English team ever.

The Guardian conceded it was no Blackburn Rovers, but gave extra marks for United's pedigree, for the fact the group really was not much of a group, and for finishing bottom. There were also many moments of farce along the way, a six-part saga of chaos, collapse and laughter in the dark: Onana diving out of the way of the ball in Munich, Onana again diving out of the way of the ball in Istanbul, Casemiro's red card, lost leads in Manchester, and Marcus Rashford unfairly convicted of a venomous stamp in Copenhagen. And yet, with both group games blank at half-time on the final night, United were still just one goal away from going through to the last 16. Bayern, for all their own flaws, were basically a good version of whatever United were attempting to piece together: Kimmich-Goretzka-Musiala an A-grade version of Amrabat-McTominay-Fernandes, Manuel Neuer the thing Onana is trying so earnestly to be, and Bayern actually did go ahead and sign Harry Kane. From there United's season continued to narrow — they could not win the league, the Champions League or the Carabao Cup, leaving the FA Cup and the extended pursuit of fourth or even fifth place, although the state of the coefficient meant the thing that might keep Manchester United out of Europe the next season could be Manchester United being so bad in Europe that season.



---


# Old Trafford and Carrington Infrastructure Decay

Rain leaks through the roof of Old Trafford on Manchester's many wet days — the detail The Guardian used on 25 December 2023 as shorthand for the state of Manchester United. The stadium remains a storied venue, but as it continues to crumble the tale of disrepair has become a central narrative in its recent history, and the neglect of a ground dating to 1910 is presented as emblematic of the Glazers' quasi-absentee proprietorship over a decade in which the club has won zero Premier League titles.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe will invest $300m (£237m) into infrastructure, but the report calls this small beer against the multibillion-pound facelift or new venue required. The problem is not confined to the stadium: the Carrington training base is cramped, and as on Sir Matt Busby Way the footprint is large but the configuration and facilities are ageing badly.



---


# Manchester United's Defeat To West Ham In December 2023

Goals from West Ham's Jarrod Bowen and Mohammed Kudus beat Manchester United on 23 December 2023, extending United's miserable run in the English Premier League, as reported by The Roar that day.

Bowen bundled home at the second attempt in the 72nd minute for his 11th league goal of the season, breaking the deadlock, and Kudus struck his fourth goal in as many games to settle matters, finishing after a defensive howler from Manchester United — a goal Kobbie Mainoo would not want to see back, and one created by an assist from Lucas Paquetá.

The result is recorded as another worrying setback for manager Erik ten Hag: United had now suffered a 13th defeat in 26 games in all competitions.



---


# Pre-Match Build-Up To Manchester United vs Chelsea, December 2023

Sporting News' countdown to kickoff at Old Trafford on Dec. 6, 2023 recorded the team-news surprise that Marcus Rashford started from the bench, along with Ten Hag's pre-match message about Chelsea's defending.

At 1 hour 30 mins until kickoff the blog noted Chelsea had won three of their last four Premier League away games but were without a league win at Old Trafford since 2013. At 1 hour until kickoff the team news was in: the eyebrow-raising decision from Erik ten Hag was that Marcus Rashford started from the bench, while Mauricio Pochettino started the former Man City man Cole Palmer. At 45 mins until kickoff the blog noted Raheem Sterling had failed to score in any of his 24 matches against Man United, and asked whether the night might be the ex-Liverpool and Man City player's.

At 30 mins until kickoff the warm-ups were underway at Old Trafford on a chilly night, and Ten Hag had just told MUTV that Chelsea do not "like to defend" and that United must take advantage of that. At 15 mins until kickoff the teams had headed down the tunnel at the Theatre of Dreams.



---


# Ratcliffe's Bid For A Manchester United Stake

As of 28 October 2023, Sir Jim Ratcliffe's bid to buy 25% of Manchester United for an inflated £1.3bn in return for control of football policy was expected to go through imminently, marking a new phase in the protracted sale of the club.

Erik ten Hag had overseen his squad through those recent weeks and, despite any implications the deal might have for the futures of his players, did not think the matter was a distraction. "Of course, they are committed to the club but especially they are committed to this team," Ten Hag said. "They want to be successful and are therefore aware you need [to focus on] the team, your teammates. That is how the players are thinking and they are not thinking about strategic reviews or structures or whatever."



---


# Ten Hag's Defence Of Manchester United's Performance

Erik ten Hag tried to put a positive spin on the defeat to West Ham on 23 December 2023 by claiming to the BBC that his side were the better team before the first goal: the claim is that the loss came from a single lapse rather than a systemic failure, and the warrant is that United created the better chances and had recently matched the top of the league.

His grounds for the first part are the shape of the match: "I think it was a decent 72 minutes where we didn't take our chances. We should've gone in the lead but we didn't and then it was one moment of switching off."

His grounds for the second part are the previous fixture, which he uses to set the standard he says the team must reproduce: "At this moment we are not top, but we have seen last week against the top of this league we were head-to-head. We didn't score, we had the best opportunities of the game." He added: "There we defended very well for 90 minutes, that has to be always our standard like what we did there. You have to bring that to every game on the pitch."



---


# Reece James Return From Injury Chelsea

Reece James was a constant menace to Blackburn's defence as he started for the first time since the opening day of the season on his return from injury, and Mauricio Pochettino admitted he was delighted to have his captain back, The Guardian reported on Nov. 1, 2023.

"He is one of the best full-backs in the world and to have been without him for so long has been difficult," Pochettino said. "But we need to be careful and little by little he will get back to full fitness."



---


# Manchester United's 1-0 Defeat To Bayern Munich, December 2023

Manchester United lost 1-0 at home to Bayern Munich on the final Champions League group matchday, reported by The Independent on 12 December 2023, with Kingsley Coman scoring on 71 minutes from a Harry Kane assist to condemn United to a seventh home defeat of the season.

The goal came at near walking pace. Coman weaved his way through the centre, the ball was eventually worked to Kane, and the English forward clipped an artful ball back through for Coman, who finished emphatically. Bayern were already through and perhaps looking to make a point after their own 5-1 defeat to Eintracht Frankfurt, but did not even need to step it up to win; they were quite low-intensity themselves, and Coman's winner came from the forward almost walking through the middle of their team. Kane did not score but did set it up. Bayern still had more of the ball and more of the attacks, which was another tension for Ten Hag to overcome: United were playing in quite a controlled way when they were going to eventually have to go for it, yet Bayern were getting through that with relative ease, so the team almost looked like they were in two minds. Bruno Fernandes blazed United's best opportunity over the bar after good work from Aaron Wan Bissaka.

The atmosphere matched the performance. There was no energy or intensity; the Stretford End eventually implored United to "attack attack attack" but the complete absence of any such impulses left some of the stadium booing the side off at the end, and it was another utterly forgettable display in a drab game before a muted crowd. News came through shortly before the hour that Lukas Lerager had scored for Copenhagen, though it did not really change the atmosphere. In context this was far from United's worst performance of the season — nowhere near as bad as Bournemouth or Crystal Palace or Newcastle, or the other defeat to Newcastle, and not as self-destructive as they had been in Denmark and Turkey and at home to Galatasaray — and they were vaguely competent on the night. But they still lost, 24 years after Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's stunning intervention against the same opponent.



---


# Harry Kane, The Striker Manchester United Did Not Sign

Harry Kane, the England captain and the forward Manchester United neglected to bid for in the summer, unlocked United's defence with a lovely flick to set up Bayern Munich's winner on 12 December 2023 — a reminder, The Independent wrote, of what could have been for United.

The comparison the reports draw is with the striker United did buy. Rasmus Hojlund has at least struck in the Champions League, but in domestic competitions he has been outscored 18-0 by Kane. United, cast out of continental competition altogether, became just the fourth English team to prop up a Champions League group when it concluded, and there was something predictable about the manner of their demise.

The Bayern game also showed one reason why Kane is at Germany's biggest club rather than England's: his side are through with ease and among the favourites for the competition, even if they do look lacking in a few areas.



---


# The Manchester United Takeover Bidding Process, 2022-2023

The sale process for Manchester United ran for roughly eleven months from November 2022, when the Glazer family announced they were open to offers, to mid-October 2023, when the withdrawal of Qatari bidder Sheikh Jassim bin Al Thani left Sir Jim Ratcliffe clear to complete a partial takeover, as reported by talkSPORT on 18 October 2023.

It was in November 2022, while Qatar was hosting the controversial 2022 World Cup, that the deeply unpopular Glazers revealed they were looking to cash in all or at least some of their shares, a decision that had United fans rejoicing. The move was mainly influenced by the fact that Raine had brokered a deal with Todd Boehly to commit £4.5bn to take control of Chelsea, which gave the Glazers grand ideas that they could rake in as much as double that for a global sporting institution like United. After several rounds of bidding the race narrowed to a straight shootout between Oldham-born Ratcliffe, who had previously offered £4bn to buy Chelsea, and Sheikh Jassim bin Al Thani, who professed to being a lifelong Red Devils fan and set up the "'92 Foundation" in tribute to the famous class of '92 of David Beckham and company.

It had initially been hoped the process would conclude in time for the summer transfer window, but the longer it dragged on — prompting several large-scale protests from United fans — the more apparent it became that Joel and Avram were reluctant sellers, as talkSPORT revealed in March. Sheikh Jassim's public statement promising to restore United "to former glories" was also seen as a thinly veiled swipe at the Glazers, which did not help his negotiating hand. The Qatari banker's patience finally snapped, and his withdrawal at the end of the preceding week left the pathway clear for Ratcliffe to complete what he has always viewed as his dream purchase. At times the saga resembled an X-Factor style judges' houses audition.



---


# Sheffield United vs Manchester United Preview, October 2023

Sheffield United, rock bottom of the Premier League with just one point on the board, hosted Manchester United at 8:00pm on 21 October 2023 live on talkSPORT, with talkSPORT noting the previous day that their hopes could be looking up given Erik ten Hag's men's disappointing season.

Sheffield United's season could not be going much worse. Manchester United sat tenth in the table, having won four and lost four of their opening eight games. Their most recent Premier League victory, over Brentford, may nonetheless give the Red Devils hope that their season is on the up — a dramatic win secured before the international break.



---


# Manchester United's 2023-24 Champions League Group-Stage Record

Manchester United finished bottom of their 2023-24 Champions League group with four points, in fourth place, eliminated from European competition altogether rather than dropping into the Europa League, The Independent reported on 12 December 2023.

The decisive results came from outside the Bayern fixture. It was not Bayern who eliminated them: it was Galatasaray, who won at Old Trafford and scored six goals over 180 minutes against United, and FC Copenhagen, who qualified instead of them — Rasmus Hojlund's former club will be in the last 16 while his current one will not, making Copenhagen the anomalies in the draw, the outsiders with the spot that had seemed reserved for United. The second place United aimed for went instead to Copenhagen, a club with a fraction of United's budget, and that is where the damage was done. On the final night the Danish side's victory over Galatasaray ensured any United win would be irrelevant, leaving only a slim hope beforehand.

The campaign produced records of the wrong kind. When Coman scored, United became the first Premier League side to concede 15 goals in a Champions League group stage. United won a lone game in the competition, and even that required a penalty save to deny FC Copenhagen a draw. Two months earlier Raphael Varane had said United could win the Champions League; the quadruple Champions League winner may need a rethink. There was no hint of a repeat of their most famous comeback against Bayern, nor even the sense of heroic failure that accompanied their 2010 quarter-final exit to the same club — just crushing failure. When Maguire hobbled off holding his groin and Evans came on, United had a man who played in their 2007-08 Champions League-winning campaign dragooned into service 16 years later.



---


# Jim Ratcliffe Completes His 25% Stake In Manchester United

Jim Ratcliffe completed the formalities around his investment into Manchester United, taking control of 25% of his boyhood club after a year of negotiations, per Sporting News on Dec. 13, 2023.

Sporting News reported that with the deal done the pressure on Erik ten Hag would be piled on even more — Ratcliffe wanted United back at "the very top of world football."

Against that backdrop, Sporting News laid out all the options should Man United move on from Ten Hag and look for a new beginning, in the hopes of salvaging the 2023/24 season.



---


# Manchester United's 2023/24 Champions League Elimination

Manchester United were out of Europe altogether after a limp display against Bayern at Old Trafford, where Kingsley Coman sealed a 1-0 win for Thomas Tuchel's side on the final day of Champions League group-stage play, per Sporting News on Dec. 12 and Dec. 13, 2023.

The Red Devils finished bottom of their four-team group, leaving them eliminated from Europe in their worst performance in the competition since 2005. On top of that, they set the record for most goals against in a Champions League group stage by an English club, with 15 conceded in their six games.

Their defensive record had collapsed as the season went on: from a Premier League standpoint they sat eighth in the English top flight, but their -5 goal differential was the worst of any club in the top 10.



---


# Schmeichel's Criticism Of Manchester United's Lack Of Identity

Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel attacked the premise that the defeat to West Ham on 23 December 2023 could be read as a performance at all: his counter is that there was no plan to the display, so the question of whether United played well before conceding does not arise.

Schmeichel lashed the team's lack of a plan and blasted them for looking slow against the Hammers. "It was just in many ways irrelevant. There was no plan to it," he said. "West Ham got an easy win which is a little bit silly to say." He then pressed the point beyond the single match, into the team's identity: "When I look at the team, I don't know what the identity of the team is. What is the style of play, what's the plan?"

His prescription attacks the manager's framing directly by naming two concrete failures instead: "He needs to take a step back, ten Hag, and say what do I need to do with these players I have available in order to first of all stop leaking goals, because that's a problem, and secondly, score goals – how do I get the next goal? Four games without a goal, it's a long time."



---


# The Three Concurrent Roles Of A Manchester United Manager

Barney Ronay models the Manchester United job as three concurrent roles — managing the past, managing the dysfunction of the present, and managing the everyday metrics on which the manager is judged.

First you must manage the past, which is constantly in the room and which skews every act, achievement and expectation. Second you must manage the dysfunction of the present, which expresses itself in every detail from a leaking stadium roof to the deep ills of a playing squad peopled with squatters and long-term missteps. Finally you get to manage the everyday metrics — team, results, style, energy, messaging: win things, improve players, create a coherent and happy internal culture, but do it during an unceasing takeover circus while star players sulk and brief against you, and while the ghost of Hamlet's father still skulks in the eaves. The three hold together only under those conditions; as of the December 2023 Champions League exit, Ronay judged, this felt like the end of one thing, perhaps even the beginning of the end of something else.



---


# Team News And Lineups For Manchester United vs Chelsea, December 2023

United lined up 4-2-3-1 and Chelsea 4-3-3 at Old Trafford on Dec. 6, 2023, with both sides missing a long list of players, per Sporting News.

For Manchester United, midfielder Casemiro and defender Lisandro Martinez remained out, while Christian Eriksen might not return in 2023. Mason Mount missed United's defeat at Newcastle United on the Saturday and Jonny Evans had not played for almost a month because of a thigh issue; Amad Diallo and Tyrell Malacia had long-term injuries. The Man United lineup (4-2-3-1, right to left) was: Onana (GK) — Dalot, Maguire, Lindelof, Shaw — Amrabat, McTominay — Antony, Bruno Fernandes, Garnacho — Hojlund, with 12 substitutes to be confirmed.

For Chelsea, Ben Chilwell remained unavailable and Malo Gusto was missing with a knee injury, but fellow defender Reece James was available again after suspension, as was Marc Cucurella. Romeo Lavia and Christopher Nkunku were likely to still be sidelined and Conor Gallagher was banned after receiving two yellow cards against Brighton; Carney Chukwuemeka, Trevoh Chalobah and Wesley Fofana were out. The Chelsea lineup (4-3-3, right to left) was: Sanchez (GK) — Disasi, Silva, Colwill, Cucurella — Sterling, Fernandez, Caicedo — Mudryk, Palmer, Jackson, with 12 substitutes to be confirmed.



---


# The INEOS Plan For Manchester United's Football Operations

Sir Jim Ratcliffe is demanding an executive role and overall control of Manchester United's day-to-day football matters, and plans to appoint his own sporting director, with former Tottenham and Southampton transfer guru Paul Mitchell one of the main names in the frame, talkSPORT reported on 18 October 2023.

The plan reaches across the club's football leadership. Ratcliffe's arrival raises doubts over the future of current sporting director John Murtough and chief executive Richard Arnold, although manager Erik ten Hag is believed to be on a solid footing despite United's poor start to the season. Sir Dave Brailsford — the mastermind behind Team GB's cycling success at the London 2012 Olympics and director of sport for Ratcliffe's company INEOS — is expected to have a prominent role in any reshuffle. Ratcliffe also has ambitious plans to upgrade Old Trafford and turn it into a 90,000-seat stadium. He wants the deal ratified in time for the January transfer window, though because of FFP concerns there is no guarantee United will be able to spend big. Despite turning 71 the day before the board meeting, his plans appear to centre on long-term stability and success rather than a short-term turnaround in United's fortunes.

The ownership rationale is that Ratcliffe would take charge of footballing matters, something the Glazers have been accused of having little to no interest in. He is already a top-tier European owner through OGC Nice — and also owns Lausanne in Switzerland — where there has been some success but nothing compared to Nice's French riviera neighbours, the club to which Ratcliffe appears set to look for inspiration.



---


# Glazer Communications Silence and Ratcliffe's PR Task

The Guardian's argument on 25 December 2023 is that opening and maintaining a regular line into supporters is a "tap-in" for Sir Jim Ratcliffe — an easy win he should not pass up. The grounds are the Glazers' record: they treat a microphone or TV camera as United fans do Liverpool or Manchester City, as a fierce enemy, and no family member has given a press conference or interview during their 18-year tenure. The family have little relationship with Manchester United's fans.

A class action lawsuit filed in the week of 15 December 2023 in the U.S. District Court in D.C. accuses Google and parent company Alphabet of anticompetitive behavior in violation of U.S. antitrust law, the Sherman Act and others, on behalf of news publishers. # Antitrust

Antitrust is the label the corpus uses for a 2023 wave of U.S. and EU legal actions against dominant tech and payments companies — the FTC's suit against Amazon, the DOJ's *US v. Google* search-monopoly trial, Epic Games' Sherman Act/Cartwright Act suit against Google Play, Helena World Chronicle's Sherman Act/Clayton Act class action against Google, PayPal's anti-steering class action, and the EU's competition review of Amazon's iRobot acquisition.

## Context

The corpus documents a wave of parallel antitrust actions against major tech and payments companies in 2023. The FTC and 17 state attorneys general sued Amazon, alleging it used its dominant position to inflate prices, overcharge sellers, and stifle competition via an "anti-discounting strategy" and buy-box penalties for third-party sellers who priced lower elsewhere; the FTC sought to hold Amazon liable for violating anti-monopoly law, with remedies to be determined only after a liability finding. Separately, the DOJ's *US v. Google* trial over Google's search dominance turned on the Information Services Agreement making Google the default search engine on Apple devices — Apple's Eddy Cue testified about the ISA's revenue-share renegotiation with Google (specific dollar figures were reserved for closed court sessions), while separate testimony from Google's search head Prabhakar Raghavan put Google's 2021 default-placement payments at $26.3 billion total, with a New York Times report cited alongside that testimony putting Apple's share at roughly $18 billion; the DOJ argued Google's default-placement deals with Apple, Samsung, and Mozilla foreclosed rivals from the data needed to improve competing search products. Epic Games separately sued Google over Google Play's app-distribution and payment-processing practices, invoking Sherman Act Sections 1 and 2 alongside California's Cartwright Act and Unfair Competition Law. A class action by news publisher Helena World Chronicle accused Google of "anticompetitive behavior in violation of U.S. antitrust law, the Sherman Act, and others" over its use of publisher content in Knowledge Graph and AI search features. PayPal was hit with a class action alleging its anti-steering rules — modeled on tactics Visa and Mastercard abandoned after a DOJ antitrust suit — stifled competition from lower-cost payment platforms like Stripe. In the EU, regulators used antitrust competition-concern findings (a formal statement of objections) to scrutinize Amazon's proposed acquisition of iRobot over fears it would let Amazon foreclose rival robot-vacuum makers on its marketplace.

## Key Characteristics

- **Statutory basis** — in the U.S., Sherman Act Sections 1 (anticompetitive agreements) and 2 (monopolization) and the Clayton Act are the primary tools; the FTC additionally proceeds under anti-monopoly/unfair-methods-of-competition authority, and states can add their own statutes (e.g., California's Cartwright Act).
- **Conduct at issue** — cases target using dominance to raise prices or fees, penalize rivals' lower prices (Amazon's buy-box mechanism), pay for default placement to foreclose competitors (Google-Apple), restrict app distribution and billing options (Google Play), or impose anti-steering rules that block cheaper alternatives (PayPal).
- **Enforcers vary by jurisdiction** — DOJ and FTC (plus state AGs) bring U.S. federal cases; private plaintiffs can also bring antitrust class actions (Helena World Chronicle, PayPal consumers); the European Commission enforces EU competition law and can use a formal statement of objections short of blocking a deal to press for remedies.
- **Remedies are typically litigated after liability** — the FTC's Amazon complaint explicitly left remedies undetermined pending a liability finding, and the historic Microsoft case (the precedent both DOJ v. Google and Epic v. Google draw on) resulted in required API-sharing and a ban on anticompetitive, exclusive deals with computer manufacturers.
- **Merger review is a distinct antitrust track** — the EU's iRobot objections show competition authorities scrutinizing prospective mergers for foreclosure risk before a deal closes, separate from post-hoc conduct cases.

## Background (external)

The corpus uses "antitrust" as a familiar label for these cases without defining the term itself. Per the Federal Trade Commission, U.S. antitrust law originates with the Sherman Act of 1890, a "comprehensive charter of economic liberty aimed at preserving free and unfettered competition," joined in 1914 by the FTC Act and the Clayton Act (FTC, *The Antitrust Laws*, accessed 2026-09-02). Sherman Act Section 1 prohibits contracts, combinations, or conspiracies that restrain trade, and Section 2 addresses monopolization and attempted monopolization; the Clayton Act separately reaches practices like mergers that may substantially lessen competition, and the FTC Act prohibits "unfair methods of competition" (FTC, *The Antitrust Laws*, accessed 2026-09-02). The Department of Justice brings criminal Sherman Act cases, the FTC enforces the FTC Act against similar conduct, and state attorneys general and private plaintiffs can enforce parallel state antitrust statutes (FTC, *The Antitrust Laws*, accessed 2026-09-02).

# Google Paid $26.3 Billion In 2021 For Default Search Placement

Google paid $26.3 billion in 2021 to multiple browsers, phones and platforms — from companies including Apple, Samsung and Mozilla — to be everyone's default search engine. The figure was revealed by Google's search head Prabhakar Raghavan when he testified in court on October 28, according to The Verge.

About $18 billion of that total went directly to Apple, according to a New York Times report published earlier in October 2023, and Google has had its deal with Apple in place since 2003 — so the payment is the current year of a two-decade arrangement, not a one-off. Questioned on the amount of money Google spends to get first pick of search engines, Pichai said the decision was made with the consumer in mind: Google pays big bucks to be everywhere so that it can take in all the data and be the best search engine across different companies' devices, he said, according to The Verge.

The trial also produced evidence that Google understood the value of defaults very early on. U.S. Justice Department lawyer Meagan Bellshaw showed Pichai a 2007 email from a Google product strategy meeting containing data showing that when people changed their browser homepage to Google, they did 15% more Google searches, and that when they switched away, their Google searches dropped 27%. The email summarizing that meeting, sent to Pichai as well as other Google leaders, read: "Nitin argues that focusing on homepage market share is one of the most effective things we can do to make gains in search market share," according to The Verge.

As of TechCrunch's November 13, 2023 roundup, the Justice Department's landmark antitrust case against Google was nearly two months old, and the trial record was still producing fresh revelations.
