# Video Game Release

## Definition

A video game release is the point at which a title becomes available to the public to buy or play, and the terms attached to that moment — which platforms it launches on, whether it is exclusive or day-one on a subscription service, and how its price behaves over time — are as much a part of "release" as the launch date itself.

## Context

The corpus discusses release terms most directly around the Microsoft-Activision Blizzard deal: Bethesda's Starfield launched in September 2023 exclusively on PC and Xbox and was playable on Xbox Game Pass from day one, the pattern Microsoft is expected to repeat with future Call of Duty titles once Activision Blizzard's catalog moves to Game Pass. This is presented as a departure from the prior arrangement, in which Sony typically held early access to Call of Duty ahead of general release, including early access to the game, testing, and bonus features. Separately, Black Friday 2023 shopping coverage shows how release timing shapes a game's retail position after launch: a newly released PS5 title, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, was added to the $500 PS5 bundle for no extra cost without any qualification about the deal's value, while Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, released back in 2018 and still retailing for $50-$60 on its own, was also added free to a $350 Nintendo Switch OLED bundle but drew the caveat that its age made it "hard to call...an amazing deal."

## Key Characteristics

- **Day-one platform and service availability** — a release can be tied to specific hardware (Starfield: PC and Xbox only) and can be simultaneously playable on a subscription service like Xbox Game Pass "on the first day they release," rather than requiring a separate purchase.
- **Exclusivity windows precede or follow release** — before the Microsoft-Activision deal, Sony's arrangement with Activision gave it early access to Call of Duty ahead of the general public, plus early testing and bonus features; UK regulators required a 15-year carve-out (via Ubisoft's cloud-streaming rights) to prevent Activision Blizzard titles from becoming Xbox-exclusive after release.
- **Release age shapes how a free pack-in game is framed** — a title's distance from its release date affects how retailers' holiday bundles are perceived: the newly released, critically acclaimed Spider-Man 2 was added free to the full-price $500 PS5 bundle with no caveat, while the 2018-released Smash Bros. Ultimate — still worth $50-$60 on its own — was called out as making its $350 Switch OLED bundle "hard to call...an amazing deal" precisely because the pack-in game was five years old.
- **Distribution model (buy vs. access) is a release-time choice** — Microsoft's habit of putting blockbuster titles on Game Pass at release leaves buyers choosing between purchasing the game outright or paying a monthly fee to access it from day one.

# MacBook Pro Design, Ports And The Space Black Finish

The clearest functional difference between the MacBook Pro and the Air is ports: the Pro has three Thunderbolt 4/USB-C ports to the Air's two, plus an HDMI port that is key for external display support, and an SD reader that Apple keeps to the Pro system.

On the SD reader, the reviewer concedes it is a niche need in these days of everyone shooting everything on their phones, so Apple's justification for restricting it to the Pro is understandable — the new iMac does not have one either — but he recounts having to locate an Apple Store in the Venetian at the previous year's CES because his external SD reader failed. On ports generally: more ports is better, it is simple math, and on the Air all of the ports save the headphone jack are on the same side, so things can get crowded fast. Both systems have the latest MagSafe connector, though despite being a bespoke charger you can top the laptops up faster via Thunderbolt.

From an industrial design perspective, not much has changed from the 2021 model. Apple has settled into a look it likes, balancing rounded edges with a flat, almost boxy design not dissimilar from the iPhone in that respect. On top is the familiar reflective Apple logo, while "MacBook Pro" is etched into the bottom; around that is a series of small screws that signal the company's newfound push into repairability spurred on by the broader call for right to repair legislation, and there is a heat vent on either side. The Pros are a good bit thicker than the Air — the 14- and 16-inch are 0.61 and 0.66 inches tall respectively versus the 15-inch Air's 0.45 inches — due in no small part to the Pros' inclusion of a fan and airflow system; you are unlikely to trigger the fan during most everyday operations, but more complex tasks like 3D rendering require a lot of compute power, so it is there when you need it. The 14-inch Pro at 3.4 pounds weighs just a hair more than the 15-inch Air at 3.3 pounds, while at 4.7 and 4.8 pounds for the M3 Pro and Max there is a pronounced increase with the 16-inch Pro.

Space black is the new color, and its distinguishing property is fingerprint resistance. Apple fans love a new color, which in the MacBook line may be attributable to there being little variation in the laptops' aluminum design; the last few generations traded almost exclusively in space gray and silver, though the new Airs opened this up with starlight, a subtle light-gold, and midnight, a much darker gray. Space black gives off a nice glow when the light hits it, but the biggest thing is the fingerprint factor: the midnight Air is a notorious fingerprint magnet, with pages and pages of conversations about it on Reddit including "tips" for a fingerprint-free midnight Mac. Apple describes the new color in the most Apple way possible: "The finish features a breakthrough chemistry that forms an anodization seal to greatly reduce fingerprints." The company has not perfected a wholly fingerprint-proof surface, but the new finish does an excellent job keeping things to a minimum.

# MacBook Pro Display, Camera And Audio Systems

Both new MacBook Pro models are built around Apple's Liquid Retina XDR display: the 14-inch has 3024 x 1964 pixels and the 16-inch 3456 x 2234 pixels, both coming out to a pixel density of 254 ppi, against the 15-inch Air's 224 ppi.

The 16-inch system's display is largely unchanged from the 2021 model, with 1000 nit sustained brightness and 1600 nit peak with HDR content; for SDR content, however, brightness has been bumped up from a 500 to a 600 nit maximum. On the camera, Apple finally started bumping its webcams from 720p to 1080p back in April 2021, a long-awaited refresh for a company that puts so much emphasis on its mobile imaging, and the new hardware was coupled with improvements brought on by the M1's on-board digital signal processing. The camera hardware has remained the same since, but updates to the chips have further tweaked picture quality; as it stands the webcam is totally fine, and the addition of portrait and studio lighting modes further improves it, though portrait mode still has some trouble with edges — the reviewer wears over-ear headphones while podcasting and it has not quite figured out what to do with the gap between the band and his head. Apple's biggest enemy here is itself: Continuity Camera, which lets a mounted iPhone take over webcam duties, is a game changer for many and there is really no comparing the two.

The on-board speaker and microphone systems remain mostly unchanged from the 2021 M1 Pro. There are six speakers, with two large grilles on either side of the keyboard, and the system supports both Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos; it is not an exceptional speaker system, but it gets the job done. The Pro also has a three-mic array with directional beamforming.

# Hardware Device

## Definition

A hardware device, in this corpus, is a physical consumer electronics product — a smart speaker, handheld game console, smart glasses, or similar standalone gadget — that a company designs, manufactures, and sells as a distinct unit, as opposed to software or a service.

## Context

The corpus covers hardware devices from two angles: unveilings/reviews and retail deals. Google's annual "hardware event" is where the company unveils an entire slate of new devices at once — the Pixel 8 and Pixel 8 Pro phones, the Pixel Fold, Pixel Buds, and the Pixel Watch 2 — showing that "hardware" in this reporting names the physical product line a company ships, distinct from the software layered on top (Android 14, Bard, Google Assistant) that runs on it.

Retail-deal roundups organize hardware devices into shopping categories — Amazon's Cyber Monday guide lists separate sections for Echo/Fire TV/Kindle devices, speakers, headphones, tablets, and gaming gear — treating "speaker" as one device sub-category among several, not a synonym for hardware in general.

Smart glasses form a recurring device category: the Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses combine a camera, open-ear audio, and a voice assistant, while Amazon's Echo Frames center on giving hands-free access to Alexa, and both trace the category back to the Google Glass Explorer Edition as its 2013 origin point.

Handheld gaming hardware is treated the same way: the Steam Deck OLED is discussed as a physical device with its own chip, screen, and battery specifications, refreshed mid-cycle the way a phone or headphone line would be.

## Key Characteristics

- **Physical and purchasable** — a hardware device is a standalone unit with a price and a retail listing (the Echo Frames at $314.99, the Ray-Ban Meta glasses at $299, the Steam Deck OLED at $549), not a subscription or app.
- **Distinct from the software it runs** — Google's hardware event unveils devices (Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel Watch 2) separately from the software updates (Android 14, Bard) that ship alongside them.
- **Organized into device sub-categories** — retail guides split hardware into categories such as Echo/Fire TV/Kindle, speakers, headphones, tablets, and gaming, each reviewed and discounted on its own terms.
- **Defined by internal components** — reviews describe a device's identity through its chip, screen, and battery (the Steam Deck OLED's die-shrunk APU, 7.4-inch OLED panel, and 50Whr battery), the specs that distinguish one hardware generation from the next.
- **Ambiguous surface form** — "speaker" in the corpus denotes both an audio hardware device (a smart speaker) and the office of Speaker of the House; only the device sense belongs to this concept.

# Game Patch Notes

## Definition

Neither corpus article uses the phrase "patch notes," but both document the same underlying pattern: a studio bundling a slate of changes — new content, rebalancing, and quality-of-life fixes — under a single named or numbered update tied to a release date.
Polygon's Diablo 4 coverage lists that pattern for "Season 2"/"Season of Blood": leveling speed, new endgame bosses, a Nightmare Dungeon rework, mount handling, and Renown/gem-Stash changes, all bundled to arrive together on Oct. 17 (doc_0533).
Polygon's games-of-the-year piece shows the same pattern for Cyberpunk 2077's named "Patch 2.0," a systems-revamping update shipped alongside — but distinct from — the paid Phantom Liberty expansion (doc_0213).

## Context

The corpus's clearest example is Diablo 4's Season 2 update, "Season of Blood," reported by Polygon on 2023-10-04: alongside new vampire powers, Blizzard shipped a broad slate of quality-of-life changes covering leveling speed, endgame bosses, Nightmare Dungeon design, mount handling, and the Renown and gem/Stash systems, all set to arrive together on Oct. 17 as one seasonal patch.

Polygon's broader 2023 games-of-the-year piece shows the same pattern in a second game: Cyberpunk 2077's Phantom Liberty expansion arrived "alongside the sweeping Patch 2.0," which revamped the base game's role-playing progression systems, improved enemy AI, and "course-corrected a litany of other details" — a patch bundled with, but distinct from, the paid DLC content it accompanied.

## Key Characteristics

- **Versioned or seasonal framing** — changes are grouped under a single identifier (Patch 2.0, Season 2/"Season of Blood") rather than released piecemeal, per doc_0533 and doc_0213.
- **Mix of change types** — a single patch bundles new content (Diablo 4's five endgame bosses), rebalancing (faster leveling, reworked Nightmare Dungeon affixes), and quality-of-life fixes (Renown carryover, gems no longer taking bag space), per doc_0533.
- **Developer-explained rationale** — studios attach commentary to justify changes, as when Diablo 4's game director Joe Shely and associate director Joe Piepiora told Polygon the quality-of-life focus came from finally having time to react to player feedback, unlike the rushed first season (doc_0533).
- **Distinct from paid content** — a patch can ship independently of or alongside paid expansions; Cyberpunk 2077's Patch 2.0 revamped core systems while Phantom Liberty (the paid DLC) added new story content, and reviewers credit the patch as much as the DLC for the game's improved reception (doc_0213).

## Background (external)

Outside the corpus, this kind of update bundle has a generic industry name: release notes (also called patch notes).
Per Wikipedia, release notes "describe important information about a distribution of a hardware or software product" and typically include "a list of what is new in the release, including bug fixes and new features" (Wikipedia, "Release notes," accessed 2026-09-02).

# Apple Silicon Chip Naming And Relative Performance

Apple's chip numbering system is not as straightforward as it seems at first blush: while the M3 represents an advance over the M2, you can still expect the M2 Ultra to outperform the M3.

The structure behind that is a two-dimensional grid rather than a single line. Pros, Maxes and Ultras are progressively larger versions of their baseline chip, containing more CPU, GPU and neural engine cores — the Ultra, for all intents and purposes, is two Maxes stitched together — so generation number and tier trade off against each other. Other factors also bear on realized performance: Mac Studio and Mac Pro do a better job with heat dissipation, while the MacBook Pros are better equipped than the fan-less Airs, which throttle performance more quickly due to heat. There are still a handful of ways in which even the baseline M3 will outperform the M2 Ultra, two clear instances being ray tracing and mesh shading, which were previously software-accelerated.

Apple's own generational comparisons are now made against the M1 rather than Intel: the reviewer noticed during the presentation that Apple is leaning less heavily on Intel comparisons, since four-year-old non-proprietary chips are no longer the main point of comparison and the M1 was announced three years earlier that week. Apple's claims: "Rendering speeds are now up to 2.5x faster than on the M1 family of chips. The CPU performance cores and efficiency cores are 30 percent and 50 percent faster than those in M1, respectively, and the Neural Engine is 60 percent faster than the Neural Engine in the M1 family of chips."

# Apple M3 Chip Architecture And GPU Features

The M3 line is the first of Apple's desktop chips to be created using the 3nm process, following the iPhone 15 Pro's lead — Apple had employed the 5nm process since the M1's introduction in 2020 — and the new process brings performance gains with less power consumption, making the Mac the first PC line to employ the technology.

GPU updates were the centerpiece of the M3 announcements, with gaming an important narrative for Apple's silicon journey. The first new feature is Dynamic Caching. Apple writes: "With Dynamic Caching, only the exact amount of memory needed is used for each task. This is an industry first, transparent to developers, and the cornerstone of the new GPU architecture. It dramatically increases the average utilization of the GPU, which significantly increases performance for the most demanding pro apps and games." More simply put, the idea is allocating just the right amount of local memory to a given task, something Apple has been working on for a while.

The other two additions are hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading. Ray tracing is designed to bring added realism to the gaming experience through more accurate depictions of lighting and reflections; mesh shading, a triangle computer shader, makes processing complex geometrical images more efficient, which in turn allows for higher-quality graphics and more scene detail.

# ChatGPT Legal And Privacy Controversies

ChatGPT has generated a run of legal and privacy controversies: an Australian mayor publicly announced he may sue OpenAI for defamation over ChatGPT's false claims that he had served time in prison for bribery, which would be the first defamation lawsuit against the text-generating service, and there have been other cases of ChatGPT accusing individuals of false crimes.

The libel exposure follows from how the models work: they do not know or care whether something is true, only that it looks true — a problem when the output is used for homework, and potentially libel when it accuses someone of a crime they did not commit. How troubling statements produced by ChatGPT will be handled was expected to play out over the following months as tech and legal experts tackled the fastest moving target in the industry. As of the article, there were no lawsuits specifically targeting ChatGPT, but OpenAI is involved in at least one lawsuit with implications for AI systems trained on publicly available data, which would touch on ChatGPT. There are also plagiarism issues: text-generating AI models like ChatGPT have a tendency to regurgitate content from their training data. Copyright in output sits with the user — the person who requested the input from ChatGPT is the copyright owner.

On privacy, OpenAI has said that individuals in "certain jurisdictions" such as the EU can object to the processing of their personal information by its AI models by filling out a form — the "OpenAI Personal Data Removal Request" — which includes the ability to request deletion of AI-generated references about them, although OpenAI notes it may not grant every request since it must balance privacy requests against freedom of expression "in accordance with applicable laws." In its privacy policy OpenAI makes a passing acknowledgement of the objection requirements attached to relying on "legitimate interest," pointing users to instructions on how to opt out of use of their information to train its models. ChatGPT chats are not public, but OpenAI disclosed a bug, since fixed, that exposed the titles of some users' conversations to other people on the service.

Other controversies span platforms and schools. Discord integrated OpenAI's technology into its bot Clyde, and two users tricked Clyde into providing instructions for making methamphetamine and napalm. CNET found itself in controversy after Futurism reported the publication was publishing articles under a mysterious byline completely generated by AI, and Red Ventures, the private equity company that owns CNET, was accused of using ChatGPT for SEO farming even where the information was incorrect. Several major school systems and colleges, including New York City Public Schools, have banned ChatGPT from their networks and devices, claiming the AI impedes the learning process by promoting plagiarism and misinformation — a claim not every educator agrees with.

# MacBook Pro M3 Generation Deals

Apple announced Macs using a new M3 processor at its "Scary Fast" event the night before Halloween, including a new 14-inch MacBook Pro that replaces the 13-inch M2 model — meaning Touch Bar Macs are finally dead, though some outgoing M2 models remain available. The new entry point is a MagSafe-equipped MacBook Pro that uses the existing 14-inch design and slightly pares it down: the 14-inch M3 MacBook Pro has the same 3024 x 1964 resolution display and 120Hz refresh rate as its pricier siblings and adds an SD card slot and HDMI port, but starts with just 8GB of RAM and lacks the third USB-C / Thunderbolt port found on the M3 Pro and M3 Max models, as well as Thunderbolt 4 speeds.

The M3 MacBook Pro is a bit of an odd middle child but still a very good laptop, The Verge wrote — especially on a deal that puts more price distance between it and the M3 Pro version. The base model with 512GB of storage had already been seen at $150 off during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, and was available for an even better $1,399 at Amazon, Best Buy, and B&H Photo, $200 off; the 1TB configuration was at its all-time low of $1,599, $200 off, at Best Buy and B&H Photo, and the configuration with base storage and 16GB of RAM was $1,599, $200 off, at B&H Photo. Anyone planning a higher-spec configuration than that would likely want to spring for the M3 Pro model instead.

The 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros for late 2023 are another round of spec-bump models, much like their 2022 incarnations, now starting with the M3 Pro chip or the speedier M3 Max and 18GB of base RAM instead of 16GB, and remain targeted at creatives doing video editing, photo processing, and other graphical work. Like their predecessors and the M1 Pro generation before them, they offer MagSafe charging, three USB-C / Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI-out, and a full-size SD card slot, with prices starting at $1,999 for the 14-inch and $2,499 for the 16-inch — and they can be specced up considerably, as with the 16-inch review unit Apple sent The Verge, which cost an eye-watering $7,199. Discounts had begun on the versions actual humans buy: the 14-inch in its base M3 Pro configuration (11-core CPU / 14-core GPU, 18GB of RAM, 512GB SSD) was $1,749 at B&H Photo, $250 off; a similar version with 1TB of storage and a 12-core / 18-core M3 Pro was $2,149, also $250 off, at B&H Photo; and the base 16-inch with the M3 Pro (12-core CPU / 18-core GPU), 18GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD was $2,249 at Amazon and B&H Photo, $250 off.

# ICC World Cup 2023: Leading Wicket Takers

As listed on 18 November 2023, the leading wicket takers of the ICC Men's ODI World Cup 2023 were: 1. Mohammed Shami (IND), 7 matches, 23 wickets; 2. A Zampa (AUS), 11 matches, 23 wickets; 3. D Madushanka (SL), 9 matches, 21 wickets; 4. JJ Bumrah (IND), 11 matches, 20 wickets; 5. G Coetzee (SA), 8 matches, 20 wickets; 6. Shaheen Shah Afridi (PAK), 9 matches, 18 wickets; 7. M Jansen (SA), 9 matches, 17 wickets; 8. RA Jadeja (IND), 11 matches, 16 wickets; 9. Josh Hazlewood, 11 matches, 16 wickets; 10. MJ Santner (NZ), 10 matches, 16 wickets; 11. BFW de Leede (NED), 9 matches, 16 wickets.

The accompanying commentary gives the bowling detail, and for the top two names cites figures that differ slightly from the table. Shami announced his return to the World Cup by picking a fifer in the very first match he played for India, and is described as having picked up 24 wickets in just six matches while conceding just 257 runs, including three five-wicket hauls and a seven-wicket haul against New Zealand in the semi-final on Wednesday, 15 November at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. Adam Zampa, the highest wicket-taker for the Aussies, picked up 23 wickets including three four-wicket hauls while conceding 515 runs. Dilshan Madushanka finished high on the list despite Sri Lanka's dreadful campaign, picking up 21 wickets and conceding 525 runs. Jasprit Bumrah took 20 wickets conceding 373 runs and had the best economy rate in the whole tournament at 4.06. The 23-year-old Gerald Coetzee picked up 20 wickets for the Proteas in eight matches conceding 396 runs. Shaheen Shah Afridi was the best bowler for Pakistan with 18 wickets conceding 481 runs in nine matches. Marco Jansen, standing 6 feet 7 inches tall and making full use of his height, took 17 wickets in nine matches conceding 450 runs. Ravindra Jadeja bowled beautiful spells especially in the middle overs, taking 16 wickets and conceding just 398 at an economy rate of 4.25 in 10 matches. The Australian pacer Hazlewood was phenomenal with the new ball, creating movement batters struggled with, and picked up 16 wickets in 11 matches. New Zealand's bowling mostly depended on Mitchell Santner, effective on the turning tracks of India, who picked up 16 wickets and conceded 449 runs in 10 matches.

Harshal Patel went into the IPL 2024 auction having been released by RCB but with strong Vijay Hazare Trophy numbers behind him: 18 wickets in 10 matches, plus 183 runs, meaning he would be considered for an all-rounder role. The observation was posted at 12.04 PM on auction day.

# India vs Australia In The 2023 World Cup League Match

The most recent clash between the two sides before the 2023 final was the league match of that same World Cup, which India won by six wickets. Australia won the toss, chose to bat first and posted a target of 200 runs, being bowled out in 49.3 overs; David Warner scored 41 runs off 52 balls and Steven Smith 46 runs off 71 balls. For India, Ravindra Jadeja picked up three wickets, with Kuldeep Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah picking up two each.

India were in a terrible position at the start of the second innings as both openers got out for a duck and India lost three wickets for just two runs. Two brilliant and sensible innings by KL Rahul and Virat Kohli, who scored 97 runs off 115 balls and 85 runs off 116 balls respectively, took India to shore.

# India vs Australia At The 1996 World Cup

Australia beat India by 16 runs in a match described as one of the most exciting played between the two sides. Australia batted first and posted a target of 259 runs in 50 overs, courtesy of a brilliant 126 runs off 135 balls by Mark Waugh, with Venkatesh Prasad and Venkatapathy Raju picking up two wickets each for India.

India batted well courtesy of Sachin Tendulkar, who made a brilliant 90 runs off 84 balls, along with Sanjay Manjrekar, who scored 62 runs off 91 balls, but India were bowled out within 242 runs in 48 overs as Damien Fleming took five wickets for Australia.

# Adil Rashid's T20I Milestones And Series Form

Adil Rashid reached his 100th T20I wicket in the first match of the December 2023 series against West Indies — on his 100th T20I appearance — and finished the series with eight wickets at 15 and an economy rate of 6.26.

In the first T20I in Barbados he had Kyle Mayers caught by Brook in the deep for 35 at 79-3, his 99th T20I wicket, off what was in truth a bit of a drag down but delivered from the front of the hand so it skidded on; England needed that badly. He then bowled Hetmyer's dismissal for 1 at 101-4, caught by Duckett on the midwicket sponge after Hetmyer danced out of his crease and got a good piece of the length ball — the 100th wicket, and a crucial one in the context of the game as England looked to ramp up the pressure. In the deciding fifth T20I he finished with figures of 4-0-21-2, and the live blog noted he had had a great series with those eight wickets at 15 and an absurd economy rate of 6.26, but was going to end on the losing side. The Guardian's report added that amid the wider theme of transformation Rashid's excellence remained constant: the 35-year-old, who had risen to the top of the T20 bowling rankings for the first time that Wednesday, took two wickets and conceded just 21 in the decider, while Topley was even better, also claiming a pair of victims but conceding only 17 — England took plenty of positives from the series, but the result was not one.

# India vs Australia At The 2019 World Cup

India took their revenge at the 2019 World Cup, winning by 36 runs after annihilating the Australian bowlers to post a target of 353 runs in 50 overs. Shikhar Dhawan scored a blistering 117 runs off 109 balls, with Virat Kohli joining in with 82 runs off 77 balls.

In the second innings Indian bowlers bowled out the Australian side within 316 runs, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Jasprit Bumrah picking up three wickets each and Yuzvendra Chahal picking up two.

# West Indies' Middle Overs In The T20 Decider Chase

Adil Rashid took two wickets through the middle overs of the decider chase — Johnson Charles for 27 and Sherfane Rutherford for 30 — but West Indies still moved to 95-4 with the run rate under control.

In the seventh over Rehan Ahmed's first over disappeared for 12: four singles and a two off the first five balls, then a no-nonsense straight six from Charles, taking West Indies to 51-2. Rashid struck straight away in the eighth, accidentally bowling a very wide, dipping full toss that Charles clunked low to Buttler at short extra cover, 54-3. Moeen replaced Rehan in the ninth and rushed through four singles. In the tenth, West Indies knew how dangerous Rashid was and were content to sit on him — the live blog thought that had been Charles' plan too before he saw a low full toss and his brain went rogue — and at drinks West Indies needed 71 from 60. England reviewed an LBW appeal against Rutherford off a Rashid legbreak that had hit him on the pad in front of middle and leg, but it was comfortably missing leg stump and England lost the review. In the eleventh, after 23 balls without a West Indian boundary, Rutherford lifted Moeen handsomely over extra cover for four. In the twelfth England appealed unsuccessfully for caught behind when Rutherford missed a swipe at Rashid and decided not to risk their last review — a good job, as there was nothing on UltraEdge — before Rutherford launched a full ball down the ground for six. In the thirteenth Rehan returned, perhaps hoping to tempt Rutherford into one big shot too many, but Hope, happily playing the anchor role, faced five of the six deliveries as England ran out of time. In the fourteenth Rutherford hooked new bowler Sam Curran for six more in an over worth 11, with Rutherford on 30 from 23 balls and Hope 19 from 28, both playing their roles to perfection. Buttler then brought Rashid back for his final over knowing it was now or never, and got an immediate reward as Rutherford smashed a drive towards short extra where Curran dived to his left for a superb catch, 95-4.

# Australia Women's Test Defeat To India In Mumbai, December 2023

Australia stumbled to their first Test defeat to India, by eight wickets in Mumbai on Sunday, after being outplayed by the hosts in foreign spinning conditions, as reported by The Roar on 24 December 2023.

The scorecard detail given is that Australia were all out for 209 in their first innings and looked far more confident in their second effort of 261 despite the wicket showing more signs of wear; the hosts then easily chased down 75 in the fourth innings.

The report places the loss against Australia's recent record. It comes after one of the more difficult periods for the side in the past six years, following the retirements of Meg Lanning and Rachael Haynes. Earlier in 2023 Australia won their fourth straight global ICC event in the 50-over World Cup, then retained the Ashes via a drawn multi-format series in England in July — a tour that included losing four of six white-ball matches, with Australia's win in the Test enough to leave them level on points with England and hold onto the trophy. The current tour of India is not a multi-format series, and the defeat in the one-off Test marks Australia's first loss in a four-day game since January 2014.

# IPL 2024 Auction: Overseas Availability Concerns

Overseas players who cannot serve a full IPL season should expect their price to suffer, because availability — not just ability — determines what a franchise is buying. # IPL 2024 Auction: Expert Previews And Team Strategy

Pundits at the IPL 2024 auction argued that franchises should shop to their squad's specific gaps rather than chase headline names, with the ground conditions and existing leadership setting each team's priorities. AB de Villiers made the case for Royal Challengers Bangalore at 12:50 PM IST: "RCB will focus on the bowlers because it is difficult to defend at the Chinnaswamy Stadium. I am very excited with the Cameron Green but I am sure the major focus will be on the bowlers." The warrant is the venue itself — a ground where defending totals is hard makes bowling the binding constraint.

Zaheer Khan made a parallel case for Lucknow Super Giants at 12:51 PM IST: "LSG will be looking at the smart buys. That should be their thought process. They got to be smart." LSG coach Justin Langer, at 12:53 PM IST, grounded that restraint in the squad already assembled: "Everyone around the cricket world is watching today. Everyone is excited to see who the big earners are. KL Rahul is a calm captain and he is comfortable with the squad he has."

IPL Chairman Arun Dhumal spoke at 1:10 PM IST, crediting the fans for the league's standing: "Dubai resonates the the spirit of cricket. Welcome to the fans who are at the Coca-Cola arena for the auction. It's because of the fans that IPL is now the second most popular league in the world."

# India vs Australia At The 1987 World Cup

The 1987 tournament was the first time the World Cup was hosted outside of England, and the first India-Australia meeting there was one of the closest matches played between the two sides: Australia won by just one run. Batting first, Australia posted a target of 271 runs courtesy of a 110-run knock off 141 balls by Geoff Marsh. India fought well through two well-made 70s by Krishnamachari Srikkanth and Navjot Singh Sidhu, but were bowled out in 49.5 overs with 269 runs on the board; Craig McDermott took four wickets for Australia.

The two sides met a second time in the same World Cup and India won that one by 56 runs. Batting first, India set a target of 290 runs courtesy of four half-centuries, by Sunil Gavaskar, Navjot Singh Sidhu, Dilip Vengsarkar and Mohammad Azharuddin. Australia were bowled out within 233 runs, with David Boon scoring 62 off 59 balls, while Mohammad Azharuddin and Maninder Singh picked up three wickets for India.

# India vs Australia At The 1992 World Cup: The Rain-Affected One-Run Defeat

In the 1992 World Cup meeting, rain spoiled not just the match but India's winning chances, and India lost by just one run on a revised target. Australia set a target of 237 runs in 50 overs, losing nine wickets in the process, with Dean Jones scoring 90 runs off 108 balls; Kapil Dev and Manoj Prabhakar picked up three wickets each for India.

In the second innings rain interrupted play after 16.2 overs and the revised target was recalculated to 236 off 47 overs. India needed 5 runs off 4 balls, but were bowled out due to two run-outs on the very last ball. Mohammad Azharuddin scored a brilliant 93 runs off 102 balls for India.

# The 2003 World Cup Final: India vs Australia

Australia beat India in the 2003 World Cup final, a memory the article says is still fresh in the minds of many Indians. India won the toss and chose to bowl first, which turned out to be a big mistake as Australia posted a target of 360 runs in 50 overs. Australian captain Ricky Ponting played a brilliant knock of 140 runs in 121 balls, along with Damien Martyn, who scored 88 runs in 84 balls; Ponting's innings famously created the conspiracy that he had a spring in his bat.

India gave up a tough fight, with Virender Sehwag making 82 runs off 81 balls and Rahul Dravid scoring 47 runs off 57 balls, but the lack of support from the other batters led to India being bowled out within 234 runs. Brett Lee and Andrew Symonds took two wickets each as Australia lifted the World Cup for the third time.

# England 132 All Out In The T20 Series Decider

England were bowled out for 132 in the deciding fifth T20I on Dec. 21, 2023, less than half the 267-3 they had made on the same surface two days earlier, leaving West Indies needing 133 to win the series.

The Guardian's live blog set the contrast starkly: Tuesday at Tarouba, England 267-3 with 19 sixes; Thursday, England 132 all out with five sixes. England assembled exactly the same players in exactly the same place and exactly the same situation — losing the toss, put in to bat — but this was an entirely different performance, on a wicket once so true that turned untrustworthy. The report suggested that as a tour enters its final days thoughts often turn to home, and perhaps the focus was not as laser-sharp as it might have been; whatever the reason, the pyrotechnics of the two previous matches never sparked. It took a fabulous delivery from Gudakesh Motie to end Phil Salt's run of absurd form with his score a modest 38, but some of the other wickets seemed a little careless: in the fourth over Jos Buttler casually turned a Jason Holder delivery to fine leg where Oshane Thomas was positioned, hands cupped, and Harry Brook tried to paddle-sweep Motie but sent the ball only a few feet into the air for an easy Nicholas Pooran catch, making it 70 for four one ball into the ninth over, at which point Liam Livingstone and Moeen Ali had to focus on disaster prevention rather than entertainment. Akeal Hosein's four overs went for just 20 and brought the wickets of Will Jacks and Moeen — the latter undone by a relay catch on the boundary after he and Livingstone added 40 for the fifth wicket — and Livingstone followed precisely two overs later, prodding the ball limply back to Motie, at which point things really fell apart, the last five wickets surrendered in 20 balls for just 11 runs. England were 109 for four after 14 overs and then the house fell down: in the 19th over Andre Russell, who bowled really well, finished with two for 25 and would have had three wickets in four balls had Hosein taken a tricky low chance at third man to dismiss Sam Curran; Adil Rashid was run out for 1 at 132-9, sacrificing himself just as in the 2019 World Cup final so that Curran could stay on strike with four balls remaining; and Curran clouted the next ball to long-off, caught by Rutherford off Holder for 12, to end the innings.

# Rehan Ahmed And Adil Rashid Through The Middle Overs

England's spinners were taken apart and then struck back through the middle of West Indies' chase in the first T20I, with Rehan Ahmed conceding nineteen in his first over before removing Nicholas Pooran.

In the seventh over Rehan bowled to Kyle Mayers, whose first ball was dragged down and launched over the midwicket boundary for six, followed by a supreme lofted drive down the ground for six more; Rehan came back with two sharply turning leg breaks before Shai Hope smeared a length ball over mid-on for the third six of the over, leaving West Indies 78-1. In the ninth over Tymal Mills replaced Rehan and started with another wide before a series of slower balls and back-of-the-hand trickery restricted Pooran and Hope, with the final ball top-edged over Buttler's head for a one-bounce four — 87-2, and West Indies needing 85 from 66 balls. In the tenth Adil Rashid was given another over after an excellent first: Pooran spotted the googly and drove it down the ground for six, singles were exchanged, and a short ball was panned into the deep for a couple, leaving West Indies 99-2 and needing 73 from 60. In the eleventh Rehan returned and had Pooran caught and bowled for 13, taking a nifty tumbling catch to his left at 100-3; Shimron Hetmyer opened his account with a single and Rehan got out of the over with three dots. In the twelfth just a single and a wicket came from the over as Hope could not break the legspin shackles, with West Indies captain Rovman Powell the new man and Buttler cranking the pressure by inserting a slip.

# West Indies' Death Overs Win In The First T20I

West Indies won the first T20I by four wickets when Andre Russell smashed the winning runs off Sam Curran — a length ball spanked over point for a one-bounce four — to go 1-0 up in the series.

The closing overs swung twice. In the thirteenth Rehan Ahmed had two balls left, the first flayed for four by Powell behind point and the last a dot, leaving West Indies needing 60 from 42. In the fourteenth Liam Livingstone came on instead of Rashid and kept it to singles as England tried to take the game as deep as possible and hope West Indies fluffed their lines at the death, with 55 needed from 36. Rehan then struck twice: Shai Hope, who had just hit him for six, holed out to Brook for 36 at 123-5, and Shepherd poked a leg break to Curran at slip first ball for 0 at 123-6, putting Rehan on a hat-trick. Russell faced the hat-trick ball and patted a decent delivery on the stumps back, then worked a couple; Ahmed finished with 3-39 from his four overs, leaving 47 needed from 30. In the sixteenth Livingstone conceded four singles before Rovman Powell crunched consecutive sixes down the ground for sixteen off the over — 31 needed from 24. In the seventeenth Tymal Mills conceded sixteen, including a mighty top-edged six from Powell and a short, wide ball sent to the fence, leaving 15 needed from 18. In the eighteenth Rashid was recalled and Russell smashed his googly clean out of the ground for six, then drove a four, eleven off the over leaving West Indies needing four.

# India's 2003 World Cup Semi-Final Against Kenya

India beat underdogs Kenya by 91 runs in the last-four stage match in Durban on 20 March 2003. Man-of-the-Match India skipper Sourav Ganguly scored an unbeaten 111 runs in 114 balls and Man-of-the-Tournament Sachin Tendulkar an 111-ball 83, as India comfortably scored 270 for four wickets in 50 overs.

In reply Kenya were no match for Indian dominance: barring skipper Steve Tikolo, who top-scored with 56 runs, no Kenyan batsman could score more than 29, and Zaheer Khan took 3 wickets in 9.2 overs for just 14 runs. Though India breezed into the semi-finals easily, the tournament is also remembered for Kenya's best run in the World Cup, as a team from a country with limited cricket facilities and no proper grassroots structure reached as far as the semi-finals.

# Boycott: England Failed To Prepare For The 2023 World Cup

Sir Geoff Boycott argued in The Telegraph, in reaction reported on Oct. 26, 2023, that England were paying the price for poor preparation in the lead-up to the World Cup as well as shoddy team selection extending back to The Ashes earlier that year — leading a scathing UK reaction from a swathe of English cricket greats.

His grounds are historical and specific. "It is an old saying: 'By failing to prepare, you prepare to fail'," he wrote, adding that history shows England rarely bat well in India where the ball spins: "Our guys are okay on flat pitches but if it turns they have a problem." The warrant connecting that record to the remedy is that exposure to difficult conditions is what sharpens a team — "batting and bowling against stiff opponents sharpens your game and puts you on your mettle" — so the best way to overcome the spin problem would have been for the squad to get to India early and play four or five warm-up matches.

What England actually did, Boycott wrote, was plan only two warm-up games, one of which was rained off, which he called not smart planning; against Sri Lanka they were once again exposed. He extended the charge to the players' approach: "Too many of our guys just want to play crash, bang wallop all the time irrespective of the type of pitch or opposition. Again not smart."

# England 171 All Out In The First T20I

England were bowled out for 171 with three deliveries to spare in the first T20I in Barbados, an innings of two halves that ran from 77 for no loss to all out.

Tymal Mills got a gossamer-thin edge through to Pooran to end the innings, completing what the live blog called a turnaround for West Indies, who had been staring down the barrel with England flying at 77-0 after six overs. # Ray-Ban Meta: Design And Discreetness

The Verge's reviewer found the Ray-Ban Meta glasses both good-looking and genuinely inconspicuous — in many ways, she wrote, they feel like they belong in a spy movie, since James Bond always looks good and the gadgets Q gives him are discreet. ## Definition

In the corpus, the Super Bowl is the season-long reference point every team, player, and betting market is measured against — the game whose winners are still identified as "defending Super Bowl champions" months later (doc_0059) and which is called "the pinnacle for prop betting" and "the most prominent sports betting day of the year" (doc_0201).

The corpus never defines "Super Bowl" itself — it only reports how teams, players, and betting markets relate to it.

# Rookie Kickers In The NFL Postseason

Postseason field-goal make rates since 2000 stack up pretty evenly between rookie kickers and veterans — 86% (67 of 78) for rookies against 84% (720 of 862) for veterans — so there is no statistical indication that rookies are less effective in the postseason, The New York Times reported on 16 October 2023.

The question arose because the 49ers lost that Sunday when their rookie kicker missed from 41 yards. San Francisco had raised eyebrows among some when they used their second-highest pick in the 2023 draft — a third-round choice, 99th overall — on Michigan's Jake Moody, a cost-effective successor to veteran Robbie Gould; general manager John Lynch called Moody a potentially "foundational" player whose stock in the draft was so high that other teams were trying to trade ahead of San Francisco for a shot at him. The season had seen Moody and Saints rookie Blake Grupe miss game-winning tries. By distance band, the postseason rates since 2000 are: under 33 yards, rookies 97% (31 of 32) versus veterans 94% (330 of 351); 34-44 yards, rookies 75% (21 of 28) versus veterans 82% (230 of 279); 45-50 yards, rookies 78% (7 of 9) versus veterans 73% (121 of 165); 51-55 yards, rookies 100% (8 of 8) versus veterans 59% (33 of 56); and 56-plus yards, rookies 0% (0 of 1) versus veterans 55% (6 of 11).

A veteran evaluator entered the caveat that the numbers do not capture the moment: "Playoff teams have a different aura, different feel in the locker room. Percentages are one thing, but who is the guy who trots out there to try the game-winner? It's a different pressure shooting free throws up by 20, down by 20, than in that type of situation." Fans might recall rookie kickers missing playoff kicks — Rodrigo Blankenship with the Colts in 2020, Harrison Butker with the Chiefs in 2017, Nate Kaeding with the Chargers in 2005 — but the NFL has also seen plenty of rookies kick effectively in the postseason: Evan McPherson made all 14 postseason tries with the 2021 Super Bowl Bengals, the 2017 Eagles won a Super Bowl with rookie Jake Elliott performing well, the 2012 Super Bowl champion Ravens had rookie Justin Tucker, and the 2006 Patriots trusted rookie Stephen Gostkowski.

# Most Valuable Player (MVP)

## Definition

In the corpus, MVP (Most Valuable Player) names the player judged most valuable to a team's or league's success, and the term surfaces at several distinct scopes: a formal season-long league award (NFL MVP, NBA MVP), a single-game honor (Super Bowl MVP), and an informal team-level or cross-sport label applied by media, players, and coaches.

## Context

At the league-season level, the NFL MVP and NBA MVP are formal annual awards contested among a small pool of star players. Sporting News's Dec. 5, 2023 awards-odds piece had Brock Purdy, Dak Prescott, and Jalen Hurts as the current NFL MVP favorites after Week 13, with C.J. Stroud and Jared Goff as the longshot cases. Separately, Yardbarker's Dec. 24, 2023 Christmas Day preview framed the Ravens-49ers game explicitly as "the decisive clash for the MVP Award," with Brock Purdy the heavy favorite (-230) and Lamar Jackson — the 2019 MVP — holding the second-shortest odds (+525). At the single-game level, MVP denotes a game-specific honor, as with Patrick Mahomes's two Super Bowl MVPs. At the team level, MVP is used informally by outlets like Yardbarker to name each team's most indispensable player at a season's midpoint — a designation that need not track the league-wide award and can go to a non-quarterback, as when Miami's Tyreek Hill or New England's Jabrill Peppers is named team MVP. The same informal usage crosses sports, as when an MLS goalkeeper calls forward Luciano Acosta "the MVP" of FC Cincinnati. MVP is also a standard sports-betting futures market: bettors wager on which player will win the season MVP award well before or during the season, alongside markets like Rookie of the Year and Offensive/Defensive Player of the Year.

## Background (external)

Beyond this corpus's sports-betting and news coverage, Wikipedia describes an MVP award more generally as an honor bestowed on the individual (or individuals, in case of a tie) "whose individual performance is the greatest in an entire league, for a particular competition, or on a specific team," recognizing one player's contribution within a team effort. (Source: Wikipedia, "Most valuable player," https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_valuable_player, accessed 2026-09-02.)

## Key Characteristics

- **Multiple scopes** — the same "MVP" language covers a formal season-long league award (NFL, NBA), a single-game honor (Super Bowl MVP), and an informal team-level or sport-crossing designation used by media and players alike.
- **Voting-panel awards lack fixed criteria** — the NBA MVP, for instance, is chosen by a panel of sportswriters and broadcasters (format since 1980, weighted 5/3/1 points for first/second/third-place votes) with no set selection rulebook, which is why outcomes are notoriously hard to predict and can produce "upset" winners.
- **Quarterback bias in NFL MVP framing** — corpus coverage repeatedly frames the NFL MVP as typically going to a quarterback from a top-seeded team, to the point that a non-quarterback like Christian McCaffrey is described as facing long odds "if the MVP wasn't a quarterback-driven award."
- **Betting futures market** — MVP odds are a standing futures category at sportsbooks (alongside moneylines, spreads, and other award markets), bet on well ahead of the outcome and repriced as the season's results accumulate.
- **Team-level MVP is unofficial** — team MVP picks (e.g., Yardbarker's AFC team-by-team roundup) are editorial judgments, not sanctioned awards, and can diverge sharply from who is in the league MVP conversation.

# Grading The 2022 NFL Draft Quarterback Class

Sportskeeda graded the nine quarterbacks of Purdy's draft class and concluded that the last pick has outperformed all eight taken before him, awarding Purdy an A+ against grades ranging from B down to F for the rest. The grounds are each player's current standing on an NFL depth chart; the warrant joining grounds to claim is that a quarterback's grade should track whether he has won and held a starting job.

Working from the top: Kenny Pickett, Pittsburgh Steelers, Pick 20, grade B — the starting quarterback for the Steelers, a home-grown University of Pittsburgh talent whom the fans are behind, and while he has not done anything special in the NFL just yet, he is one of just four QBs in the 2022 class currently an undisputed starter. Desmond Ridder, Atlanta Falcons, Pick 74, grade C — he earned the starting job ahead of the 2023 season and has not been spectacular, but at least he is starting games at the highest level. Malik Willis, Tennessee Titans, Pick 86, grade D — the QB2 or QB3 in Tennessee depending on who you ask, which is interesting given that some draft analysts thought him the most naturally gifted QB in the class; he is fighting a losing battle after the franchise drafted the highly rated Will Levis, and a "D" might even be generous. Matt Corral, Carolina Panthers, Pick 94, grade E — the Panthers have mainly ignored him, electing to trade up to number one for Bryce Young in the 2023 draft, and he left the franchise ahead of his sophomore season.

Continuing: Bailey Zappe, New England Patriots, Pick 137, grade C- — Mac Jones' backup plays for the worst Patriots team of the past twenty years, not a dream spot for the Western Kentucky alum. Sam Howell, Washington Commanders, Pick 144, grade B — the franchise quarterback for the usually trigger-happy Commanders, which shows the new ownership group has faith in his ability, and he gets a positive grade for that sole reason. Chris Oladokun, Pittsburgh Steelers, Pick 241, grade F — yet to make a start in the NFL and rated an F until that changes, though it will not be on the team that drafted him as the Steelers waived him a while ago. Skylar Thompson, Miami Dolphins, Pick 247, grade D — the third-string QB heading into 2023, who could be eligible for a Super Bowl ring if the Dolphins go all the way. Finally, Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers, Pick 262, grade A+ — arguably the best "Mr. Irrelevant" of all time, who, if he stays healthy in San Francisco, can become one of his generation's finest QBs; the article suggests, clichéd as it is, that we might have the next Tom Brady in front of us.

FLEX QB Jordan Love, Packers ($16,000): from one quarterback to another, the writers like this game to feature a lot of points, something that doesn't happen often on "Thursday Night Football" but should change this week, because the Lions seem incapable of playing in low-scoring, grind-it-out games; Love has seven passing touchdowns through the first three weeks and faces a bottom-10 passing defense per PFF, plus Detroit's banged-up secondary just beginning life without C.J. Gardner-Johnson (pec). FLEX TE Luke Musgrave ($8,000): coming off his best game of the season with six catches for 49 yards, he gets a matchup against the second-worst defense against tight ends — the Lions giving up 14.8 fantasy points per game to the position according to FantasyPros — and if Watson does return it could help the rookie as Detroit's defense focuses elsewhere.

# Taylor Swift's Attendance At Kansas City Chiefs Games

By early December 2023 Taylor Swift had attended five of Travis Kelce's games, including one on 3 December, often seated in the Kelce family suite — and since her first NFL appearance in September her occasional attendance had drawn pushback from NFL fans who believed her presence was distracting from the game itself. Swift told Time she has little sense of how much she is on screen: "There's a camera, like, a half-mile away, and you don't know where it is, and you have no idea when the camera is putting you in the broadcast, so I don't know if I'm being shown 17 times or once." She said she does not pay much attention to the cameras and fans around her because she is watching her boyfriend play.

Her answer to the criticism was direct: "I'm just there to support Travis. I have no awareness of if I'm being shown too much and pissing off a few dads, Brads, and Chads." Asked about the many Swifties who had started watching NFL games since she began dating Kelce, she joked: "Football is awesome, it turns out. I've been missing out my whole life." Her effect on the league was visible in October, when a Chiefs-Jets game she attended with famous friends became the most-watched Sunday NFL show since Super Bowl LVII in February 2023.

# Evaluating Brock Purdy And The San Francisco 49ers, 2023

The New York Times argued on 16 October 2023 that Brock Purdy is a good, young quarterback well-suited to run Kyle Shanahan's offense at a high level by making quick decisions when given time to find open receivers — but not the kind of quarterback who can carry the 49ers when the supporting cast is missing.

The grounds start with what the 49ers do not have in Purdy: an AFC North-certified, weatherproof Ben Roethlisberger clone able to overpower the elements, break away from defensive linemen and thrive in the conditions Purdy faced against Cleveland. The warrant is that Purdy's effectiveness is conditional on time and on receivers getting open, which is a property of the system around him rather than of improvisation.

An NFL executive made the same point about the system's dependencies: "The 49ers knew they needed a good quarterback to win the Super Bowl, and they knew they could help Purdy be that. Give him a great receiving tight end, two good receivers and a great halfback who fits the system, and they'll get someone open on every pass play. But then Deebo Samuel gets hurt, Christian McCaffrey gets hurt, and now we don't have as many guys open. Especially when you face a defensive coordinator who says, 'You show me you can beat me throwing the ball outside the numbers — best of luck, and to do that, you are going to have to take a five-step drop and I'm going to have Myles Garrett chasing you every play.'"

# Taylor Swift's First Chiefs Game Appearance On 24 September 2023

Taylor Swift took Travis Kelce up on his offer and attended the Chiefs' Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears on 24 September 2023, according to CBS Sports' timeline published 12 October 2023.

Swift was dressed on theme and watched intently, cheering and even chest bumping someone during big plays; she was especially thrilled to see Kelce get in the end zone on a three-yard catch that put the Chiefs up 41-0, and Kansas City went on to win 41-10 to improve to 2-1. She sat next to Donna Kelce in the box, the two seen talking and laughing as the game went along.

"He told me at the last minute," Patrick Mahomes said when asked if he knew Swift was coming. "There's some things with Trav where he kind of just says it and you don't know if it's true or not. He says it so calmly. ... Friday he was like, 'Yeah, I think she's coming to the game this weekend,' and then moved about his business." Head coach Andy Reid, asked about his star tight end's supposed relationship, quipped, "I set them up."

Afterwards the two were photographed together for the first time, walking side by side, Kelce fittingly wearing an outfit with "1989" in the title and Swift wearing a Chiefs zip-up; they were then spotted leaving in a convertible with the tight end driving, and Kelce reportedly rented out a restaurant for a private party with Swift and his teammates. # National Football League (NFL)

## Definition

In the corpus, the National Football League (NFL) is the professional football league covered as both a sports competition and a media business — its 2023 season tracked through AFC/NFC conference standings and playoff seeding, its "Thursday Night Football" package sold to Amazon Prime Video, and its revenue growth under Commissioner Roger Goodell, credited by Essentially Sports with a $27 billion revenue target for 2027.

## Context

The corpus treats the NFL as both a sports league and a media business: Essentially Sports traces its "humble beginnings in 1920" to its status as an "$18 billion juggernaut" today, with Commissioner Roger Goodell targeting $27 billion in revenue by 2027.
The same piece cites an estimate from Joe Pompliano that the NFL "will bring in $20 billion in revenue this year, more than the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, and Ligue 1 combined," and separately states outright that "the NFL is already the world's richest league."
Its season structure surfaces repeatedly in the corpus: standings are tracked by conference and division (AFC East/North/South/West, NFC East/North/South/West), with regular-season results determining division leaders and wild-card seeding heading into the playoffs.
Weekly games are also branded by broadcast window — most notably "Thursday Night Football" — which airs exclusively on Amazon Prime Video under an 11-year rights deal, with only the two competing teams' local markets exempted from needing a Prime subscription.
The league also anchors seasonal traditions distinct from other major U.S. leagues, most notably Thanksgiving Day games, which in 2023 drew an average of 34.1 million viewers across three games — a tradition the corpus contrasts with the NBA's Christmas Day slate — alongside a growing Christmas Day broadcast tradition of its own.

## Key Characteristics

- **Two-conference structure** — teams are split into the AFC and NFC, each further divided into divisions, with standings and tiebreakers (head-to-head record, conference record) determining playoff seeding.
- **Regular season into playoffs** — the corpus's Week 13 standings coverage shows an 18-week regular season narrowing toward division leaders and wild-card contenders as the playoff picture takes shape.
- **Commissioner-led revenue strategy** — under Commissioner Roger Goodell, the league has set an explicit financial target ($27 billion by 2027) and, per the corpus, is already "the world's richest league."
- **Thursday Night Football broadcast rights** — the "Thursday Night Football" window airs exclusively on Amazon Prime Video under an 11-year deal, with local-market exemptions for the two competing teams.
- **Recurring scandal and safety scrutiny** — the corpus notes a history of controversies (Kaepernick's protest, domestic-violence cases, Deflategate, Bountygate, CTE concerns) running alongside active initiatives such as international games and the "Play Smart, Play Safe" concussion-safety program.
- **Holiday broadcast traditions** — Thanksgiving Day games are a fixture of the NFL calendar with viewership the corpus contrasts directly against the NBA's Christmas Day tradition.

## Background (external)

Outside the corpus, the NFL is the highest level of professional American football: 32 teams split evenly between the American Football Conference (AFC) and National Football Conference (NFC), each with four four-team divisions.
Each season runs an 18-week regular season in which every team plays 17 games and takes one bye week, after which seven teams per conference enter a single-elimination playoff bracket whose conference-championship winners meet in the Super Bowl (Wikipedia, "National Football League," https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League, accessed 2026-09-02).

# Jordan Croft AFL Draft Prospect 2023

Jordan Croft, profiled in Kevin Sheehan's top 40 for the 2023 AFL Draft as reported by The Roar on Nov. 15, 2023, is a tall forward who is lightly built but extremely athletic. State: Victoria Metro. State League Club: Calder Cannons. Community Club: Maribyrnong Park. Date of Birth: 12/05/05. Height: 200cm.

He uses his mobility and height to create opportunities as a marking forward, with his speed and precise kicking key features of his game. He only fully focused on a potential AFL career the previous year after previously playing volleyball. He starred with the Calder Cannons and Victoria Metro that year, kicking 33 goals in the talent pathway, and his 2km time of 6:05 at the national Draft Combine was a strong indicator of his elite endurance but also his competitiveness for a player of his size. The eligibility condition attached to him: he can join the Western Bulldogs under the father-son rule as the son of former Bulldogs utility Matthew Croft, who played 186 games for the club, and he nominated as a father-son prospect for the Bulldogs. Weapon: Aerial ability. AFL player comparison: Max King (St Kilda).

# The NFL Super Bowl Contender Landscape, Week 6 Of 2023

The New York Times' Pick Six column of 16 October 2023 addressed the key questions facing the ten teams with the shortest Super Bowl odds — the Chiefs, Eagles, 49ers, Bills, Bengals, Cowboys, Ravens, Lions, Dolphins and Jaguars — with one-third of the 18-week regular season nearly complete.

The prompt for the exercise was a weekend that changed the picture at the top. The San Francisco 49ers entered Week 6 riding a 15-game winning streak and looking unstoppable with a young quarterback, Brock Purdy, who was making the game look easy; they exited with a 19-17 defeat at Cleveland, injuries to key players and, for the first time that season, a question mark or two. The previously unbeaten Philadelphia Eagles also lost ugly that Sunday.

The season to that point had produced a set of contradictions the column set out to test. The Miami Dolphins had set NFL records for offense, only to lose by four touchdowns in their lone game against a true contender. The Kansas City Chiefs had won with defense, sometimes in spite of their offense. The Buffalo Bills had incurred devastating injuries. For each of the ten teams the column ran through what the writer thinks and what NFL insiders have to say.

# Playoff Seeding

Playoff seeding is the numbered ranking assigned to each team that has qualified for a postseason field, used to set which team hosts each game, which teams earn a bye, and how the bracket is arranged.

## Context

In the corpus, seeding shows up in two different forms depending on the sport's postseason structure.

For the NFL, Sporting News' Week 13 playoff-picture roundup builds seeding directly from division standings and tiebreakers: the No. 1 seed in each conference gets home-field advantage and the lone first-round bye, and teams below the four division leaders are ranked as wild-card "in the hunt" entrants — for example the Dolphins held the AFC's No. 1 seed on the conference-record tiebreaker over the Ravens, while the Cowboys, as a division runner-up, could finish "No. 1, No. 2 or No. 3" if they won their division or were "locked into No. 5" otherwise.

For college football, the corpus shows a different seeding mechanism entirely: the four-team College Football Playoff field is not set by a standings formula but by a selection committee that ranks and numbers teams by subjective judgment of "best" versus "most deserving" — the 2023 field was numbered 1. Michigan, 2. Washington, 3. Texas, 4. Alabama, with an unbeaten Florida State left out of the numbered field altogether.

MLB's postseason coverage in the corpus treats seeding's practical payoff — home-field advantage — as uneven in impact: The Athletic's ranking of playoff ballpark atmospheres notes that a Rangers team with nine fewer regular-season wins than the Rays still swept the Rays at the Rays' home ballpark, illustrating that seeding-conferred home-field advantage does not guarantee an edge.

## Key Characteristics

- **Numbered rank within a bracket** — each qualified team gets a single ordinal number (No. 1, No. 2, etc.) that determines its bracket position, as in the NFL's AFC/NFC seed lists and the CFP's 1-4 field.
- **Drives home-field advantage and byes** — in the NFL, the No. 1 seed in each conference gets the lone first-round bye and home-field advantage, a stake the corpus describes the Eagles as being "in real danger of losing" to the 49ers, while the Ravens held only a half-game lead for the same spot over three teams right behind them.
- **Built from different inputs by sport** — the NFL derives seeds from win-loss record, division titles, and tiebreakers (head-to-head, conference record); the CFP derives its numbered field from a committee's ranked judgment rather than a fixed statistical formula.
- **Division winners are seeded above wild cards** — the NFL's seeding format ranks all division leaders (seeds 1-4) ahead of the best non-division-winning teams (wild cards, seeds 5-7), regardless of overall record, as when the 6-6 Falcons held a division-winner seed while stronger wild-card contenders sat lower.
- **Home-field advantage from seeding is not decisive** — MLB coverage of the 2023 postseason shows the Rangers, with nine fewer regular-season wins than the Rays, sweeping the Rays at their home ballpark despite two of the smallest postseason crowds in the past 100 years there, so seeding sets the schedule and venue but not the outcome.

# Connor Bedard's Shooting Practice Habits

Connor Bedard's shot was not simply a natural gift: NHL skills coach Nick Quinn, who has worked with him each summer for several years, said "I can tell you firsthand it didn't happen by accident. Connor's worked on this since he was little," as reported by The New York Times on 17 November 2023.

The comparison with the club's own history sets the scale. A number of Chicago Blackhawks over the last few decades liked to put in extra time shooting — Patrick Kane would stay out with the young guys, including Alex DeBrincat, well after practice to play shooting games — but even they had a limit. Bedard doesn't have much of a limit: it's common for him to be on the ice an hour after practice taking shots from all over the ice, and he even got a few other rookies, especially defenseman Kevin Korchinski, to join him on a regular basis. As the media waits for him at his dressing room stall for interviews, he shoots and shoots and shoots.

Blackhawks coach Luke Richardson placed the habit in a lineage: "I know Jaromir Jagr did this for a long time. Even at the end of his career — and he skated around and he had the weights around the bottom of his ankles, practiced full practices like that. It's happened. That's their life. They love it so much and they have to be out there. That's where they feel comfortable and don't get tired. Hopefully, they go home and have a nap in the afternoon and not watch 'Young and the Restless.' Take it easy and get ready for the next day. It does add up when you put the hours of the week in." Bedard downplays the sessions — to him it's not like he has weights on his ankles, he's just shooting, nothing too strenuous — and he rejects the label they would seem to earn: "I say it a lot: I don't feel like I'm a shooter," he said. "I'm just trying to make the right play. If the shot's there, I'll take it. Obviously, the goalies are good, you got to hit your spot."

# Britney Spears And David Lucado

Two months after ending her engagement to Jason Trawick, Britney Spears began dating David Lucado, who worked at a legal firm; she announced their split in August 2014 by tweeting "Ahhhh the single life!", and her representative confirmed to People: "Yes, she's single." # Britney Spears' Unconfirmed Romances With Wade Robson And Colin Farrell

Two of the romances attributed to Britney Spears in the early 2000s were never confirmed by either party. Shortly after her breakup from Justin Timberlake, Spears was rumoured to be dating Wade Robson, a dancer and choreographer who appeared in the music video for her 2009 song "(You Drive Me) Crazy"; neither Spears nor Robson confirmed the rumours.

In 2003, Spears and Colin Farrell made headlines when they were spotted holding hands at the premiere of The Recruit, sparking speculation that they were dating. Farrell explicitly denied it in an interview with Entertainment Tonight at the time, saying the two were just friends: "She's just a mate. Seriously, we just met a week ago, [we're] having a laugh." The quote was reported by People in 2003.

# Clark's Cease-And-Desist, The Political Friction, And The Firing For Cause

Clark's cease-and-desist letter cited two documents that had been presented to the board — a pre-acquisition financial analysis of the Deliverr deal, presented by the co-CEOs for board approval and shaped by multiple prior board meetings, and a review of Flexport's first-quarter numbers — both viewed by CNBC.

Clark's camp suggested other factors may have led to the abrupt firing, among them politics. Days after Clark was ousted, Petersen sent him a message, seen by CNBC, blasting one of his key female executives for wasting her days at the company on "far left-wing political activism"; the executive is a registered Republican. Trae Stephens, the Founders Fund partner, had also shared his contempt for that executive weeks before Clark's departure, a person familiar with the board told CNBC, and Stephens did not respond to a request for comment. Petersen is also a venture partner at Founders Fund, the firm started by Peter Thiel, a prominent supporter of President Trump's 2016 campaign who more recently bankrolled Senate candidates in Ohio and Arizona, and many of Thiel's closest confidantes at Founders Fund and elsewhere in venture are outspoken conservatives — though Petersen's sole public political contribution in 2023 was to a Democratic political action committee associated with Sen. Joe Manchin of West Virginia, and he does not talk much about politics. Clark has donated to candidates on both sides of the aisle; upon his departure The Wall Street Journal reported he was considering running for governor of Texas, but two people familiar with his thinking say that is not happening anytime soon. Flexport told CNBC that an employee's politics are not relevant in personnel decisions: "Ryan Petersen does not care at all about anyone's political or personal affiliations. That is their business. It is inappropriate for any employee to spend an excessive amount of time during work hours on activities unrelated to their role." A person familiar with the female executive said her noncorporate endeavors were largely related to charitable organizations. Clark has largely remained silent since he was forced to resign on Sept. 5, though in private he has expressed frustration at how his former team was treated, as many of his allies from Amazon who joined him at Flexport were summarily fired by Petersen shortly after his departure. On Sept. 13, Flexport chief legal counsel Chris Ferro contacted Clark to tell him his resignation a week earlier had not been accepted: instead, Flexport's board met the day after Clark resigned and voted to fire him for cause, though the board minutes did not yet reflect why. Ferro allegedly told Clark that Flexport would give him a block of 2 million shares — worth millions of dollars — if he signed a separation agreement including nondisclosure and nondisparagement clauses; Clark declined. Shortly after, Clark took the stage at the same Phoenix supply chain conference Petersen had spoken at earlier that day and did not hold back: "The only thing I really regret from the past year was I sort of picked the wrong founder. Basically, it was a place of extending my reputational halo to a group that, in my opinion, didn't deserve it. Largely, because about half the team was let go last week on Friday, the most brutal nonseverance packages I've ever seen in my life. It was about as disrespectful a way as humanly possible."

# All You Had To Do Was Stay: A Track Five That Breaks The Pattern

Traditionally, track five on a Taylor Swift album is the record's most raw and vulnerable moment, but All You Had To Do Was Stay is no Dear John or All Too Well — it is instead a big disinterested "nope" to an ex who comes back begging for a second chance. That inversion of the track-five convention is the song's discriminating feature.

Its origin was a dream in which her ex turned up at the door and, instead of giving him a piece of her mind, all that came out was a high-pitched plea to "stay". When she woke, she recorded the sound into her phone and decided to base a song around it — only this time, she got to say everything she wanted.

# Welcome To New York As A Song About Creative And Personal Freedom

Welcome To New York is, in the BBC's reading, the sound of creative and personal freedom — "It's a new soundtrack, I could dance to this beat forever more." Taylor Swift moved to the city in 2014 and was amazed to discover she could go grocery shopping largely incognito, and that shift registered physically: "My friends and people who know me have commented that I'm physically different since being here," she told NYC radio station WKTU.

The song's defining feature, in Swift's own framing, is its orientation towards possibility rather than any particular relationship: "That song is about the endless hopefulness and endless possibilities that New York seems to present," she said in an interview with Access Hollywood. A distinguishing fact about the track, setting it apart from the rest of the album, is that all proceeds from it are donated to New York City's Public Schools.

# Media Coverage Share As The Barrier For Women's Sports

Billie Jean King argues that the money gap in women's sports follows from the media gap: "We only get 5% of the media. That's where the money is." Her answer to the standard question is that it is not a mystery at all — "People always say, 'why doesn't the WTA have as much money as the ATP?' I'm like, really? If you watch a show at night, a sports show, just count how many minutes are on men and how many minutes are on women. We're at 5%. We've got to change that."

Alongside the coverage problem she names participation as the other lever, and frames its payoff broadly: make sure we get girls early in life into sports. "It's really about the health issue, more than anything. More jobs, more everything. Women of color and diversity is really important."

Asked whether he is asked many questions that smack of antisemitism or a lack of understanding and support for Israel's position, Eylon Levy answers "how long have you got" and lists examples from his interviews. The BBC asked him in a radio interview whether there is CCTV evidence that the hostages are in Shifa Hospital and what medical treatment they were receiving. # You Are In Love: Written From Watching Jack Antonoff And Lena Dunham

You Are In Love is a gently-sung romance inspired by Taylor Swift observing her producer Jack Antonoff and his then-girlfriend, Lena Dunham. The song's defining quality is that it describes love from the outside rather than from her own experience. "I remember thinking [the backing track] sounded so much like the sound of actual love, true love. Like, through thick and thin, sickness and health love," she told MTV.

Drawing directly on conversations she'd had with Lena, the song blends scenes of everyday life — burnt toast, borrowed shirts — with moments of incandescent tenderness such as kisses on sidewalks and late night heart-to-hearts. In an interview with Elle, Swift talked wistfully about the couple's ease around each other: "I've never had that. [But] now I have more of a grasp on the fact that when you're in a state of infatuation and you think everything that person does is perfect, it then - if you're lucky - morphs into a real relationship when you see that that person is not in fact perfect, but you still want to see them every day."

The counter-position to the Swift-Kelce media wave attacks its premise that the story is genuine and welcome, and it comes from within the fanbase and from commentators. Sporting News noted on 2023-09-28 that Travis Kelce had been catching a lot more than footballs lately and that fans everywhere had been swift to hop on the Taylor Swift bandwagon; the celebrity couple had been in the news for well over a week, and despite fatigue from many — Chris 'Mad Dog' Russo's rant being among the most vocal — companies like FanDuel just couldn't help but lean into a profitable storyline. Essentially Sports reported on 2023-10-25 that hardcore football fans were pretty much done with the NFL harping about Kelce and Swift. Reality TV star Rachel Lindsay, a longtime NFL fan, had recently slammed the "obnoxious" coverage, highlighting the "exhausting" uptick in Swifties obsessing over football — and that is offered as just one example of how fans were finding the fixation a little too disrespectful towards the sport.
